title: NEET-UG 2026 paper leak: Rouse Avenue court fixes November 18 for order on framing of charges
text: New Delhi, Oct 29 (IANS) A specially designated Fast Track Court at the Rouse Avenue Courts Complex in Delhi on Thursday reserved its order on framing of charges against the accused in the NEET-UG 2026 question paper leak case. A specially designated Fast Track Court at the Rouse Avenue Courts Complex in Delhi on Thursday reserved its order on framing of charges against the accused in the NEET-UG 2026 question paper leak case. The Fast Track Court, constituted to deal with offences under the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024, will pronounce its order on November 18. The case relates to the alleged leakage of confidential question papers ahead of the NEET-UG 2026 examination, which was held on May 3 and subsequently cancelled following the paper leak controversy. The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) filed a chargesheet against 13 accused on July 28, claiming that the question papers were leaked through a network involving National Testing Agency (NTA) subject experts, intermediaries, coaching operators and others. According to the probe agency, three NTA subject experts entrusted with translating, back-translating and proofreading the question papers allegedly took confidential examination questions out of the NTA's office in Delhi by exploiting security lapses. The CBI has claimed that one of the accused, P.V. Kulkarni, wrote down all 135 Chemistry questions, along with their answer options, on small slips of paper and concealed them while leaving the confidential section. The agency also flagged shortcomings in CCTV surveillance at the NTA office, stating that only 20-25 days of CCTV backup were available and that there was no dedicated control room to monitor the live feed from the confidential section. The chargesheet against the 13 accused cited 360 witnesses, 422 documents and 43 material objects in support of the prosecution's case. The accused have been charged under various provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), the Prevention of Corruption Act and the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024. The CBI subsequently filed a chargesheet against Sheshrao Bajrang Suryavanshi, the 14th accused arrested in the case, before the special court in October. The probe agency claimed that Suryavanshi was linked to another accused, Shubham Khairnar, a career counsellor arrested in Nashik, Maharashtra, for allegedly circulating the question paper on social media. The CBI registered the case on May 12 following a complaint from the Department of Higher Education under the Union Ministry of Education over alleged irregularities and leakage of confidential NEET-UG question papers. The original examination was cancelled, and a re-examination was conducted on June 21 under heightened security arrangements. Get the latest Education News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

title: NEET-UG 2026 paper leak: CBI files chargesheet against 14th accused, court hearing on October 22
text: NEET-UG 2026 paper leak: CBI files chargesheet against 14th accused, court hearing on October 22 The Central Bureau of Investigation ( CBI ) has filed a chargesheet against Sheshrao Bajrang Suryavanshi, the 14th accused arrested in the NEET-UG 2026 question paper leak case. The chargesheet was submitted before a special court at the Rouse Avenue Courts Complex in Delhi. The specially designated Fast Track Court has scheduled the next hearing for October 22 and directed that a copy of the chargesheet be supplied to Suryavanshi. Suryavanshi was arrested by the CBI in September. He was subsequently sent to judicial custody after his three-day remand with the probe agency ended. Alleged link with another accused Earlier, the CBI had told the court that Suryavanshi was allegedly linked to Shubham Khairnar, a career counsellor arrested in Nashik, Maharashtra, on May 12. Khairnar is accused of circulating the question paper on social media. The latest chargesheet follows the agency's July 28 filing against 13 accused in the case. The court had subsequently taken cognisance of that chargesheet. CBI details alleged security lapses at NTA office According to the CBI, confidential NEET-UG 2026 question papers were leaked before the May 3 examination through a network involving National Testing Agency (NTA) subject experts, intermediaries, coaching operators and other persons. The agency alleged that three NTA subject experts responsible for translating, back-translating and proofreading question papers managed to remove confidential examination questions from the NTA office in Delhi by exploiting security lapses. The CBI found that one of the accused, P.V. Kulkarni, allegedly wrote down all 135 Chemistry questions, along with their answer options, on small slips of paper. He then concealed the slips while leaving the confidential section. The agency also flagged shortcomings in the office's CCTV surveillance system. It told the court that CCTV footage was retained for only 20 to 25 days and that there was no dedicated control room to monitor the live feed from the confidential section. The NEET-UG 2026 examination was held on May 3 but was cancelled following the question paper leak controversy. The re-examination was subsequently scheduled for June 21. The CBI registered the case on May 12 and investigated the alleged chain of events involving the removal of confidential questions and their subsequent circulation. The case is being heard by a specially designated Fast Track Court at the Rouse Avenue Courts Complex. The court was constituted to deal with offences under the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024, and related matters. title: Government extends Nilekani-led exam reforms panel tenure till January
text: Nandan Nilekani-led task force gets extension till January 2027 as exam reforms, including a possible hybrid NEET-UG format, are reviewed NEW DELHI: Centre has extended the tenure of the Nandan Nilekani-led task force on examination reforms till Jan 2027, with the prime minister's office (PMO) seeking consultations with chief ministers and chief secretaries before the panel finalises its recommendations, TOI has learnt from govt officials. During consultations, some stakeholders and experts have also suggested a hybrid format for NEET-UG 2027, allowing time to expand infrastructure for a complete shift to computer-based testing (CBT) in 2028. A govt official said the PMO wants the task force, earlier expected to submit its report by Oct-end, to seek views from state leadership on challenges particular to different regions. The aim, the source said, is to better understand disparities in testing infrastructure, connectivity and administrative preparedness, and reflect these state-specific concerns in a more comprehensive examination reform roadmap. Watch PM Modi Sets Up Exam Reform Task Force Under Infosys Co-Founder Nandan Nilekani After NEET Backlash Another proposal likely to feature in the task force's recommendations is a nationwide network of CBT centres developed by Centre and state govts with private investment, sources said. Such a model could expand govt oversight of testing facilities while mobilising private capital to build infrastructure, particularly in districts that lack secure, adequately equipped centres. The funding, ownership and operating arrangements would need to be worked out. Such centres could support common security standards, reliable connectivity and better access for candidates outside metros. TOI had earlier reported that the task force is prioritising "debundling" examination responsibilities. Under the proposed restructuring, question-paper setting, conduct of exams, management of test centres and security would be assigned to separate agencies instead of being concentrated with a single operator. The objective is to create clearer lines of accountability and limit the risk of a lapse in one part of the examination process affecting the entire exercise. The approach would, however, require coordination between the agencies handling different stages. Coordinated schedules could help students and job applicants avoid exam-date clashes and allow testing infrastructure to be used more efficiently. The six-member task force was constituted in July following the NEET-UG 2026 controversy, which led to the cancellation of the original exam and a retest. It has held 18 internal meetings and around 40 consultations, in addition to seeking public suggestions. An Oct parliamentary committee report also recommended secure govt-controlled testing centres across districts and a phased transition to CBT for NEET-UG. The extension gives the task force more time to assess the feasibility of its proposals with states. Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

title: Govt warns of tough action against malpractice during teacher hiring test
text: District administrations completed final preparations and trained centre superintendents on Saturday Ranchi: More than 5.65 lakh candidates will appear for Jharkhand Teacher Eligibility Test (JTET) on Sunday, a decade after the last examination, amid heightened scrutiny over malpractice and recruitment irregularities. Organised by Jharkhand Academic Council (JAC), the test is expected to accelerate the recruitment process for nearly 39,000 vacant teaching posts in govt primary and upper primary schools. In a public appeal on Saturday, chief minister Hemant Soren warned that strict action would be taken against those involved in malpractice or those facilitating it. He also cautioned personnel against failing to perform their assigned duties. âStrict legal action under the Jharkhand Competitive Examination Act, 2023 will be taken against anyone engaging in or facilitating malpractice at any level, as well as against personnel who fail to discharge their designated duties,â Hemant said. Under the Act, offences may attract punishment ranging from three years of imprisonment and a Rs 5 lakh fine to life imprisonment and penalties of up to Rs 10 crore, depending on their nature and severity. Govtâs warning comes against the backdrop of nationwide outrage over the alleged NEET-UG paper leak and protests in Jharkhand over suspected irregularities in recruitments conducted through Jharkhand Public Service Commission and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission. âThe state govt is committed to qualitative reform in education and human resource development. Conducting examinations in a malpractice-free environment and publishing results on time is the govtâs priority,â Hemant said. The test will be held at 986 centres in two shifts â from 9.30am to noon and from 2pm to 4.30pm. District administrations completed final preparations and trained centre superintendents on Saturday. In view of the expected rush, South Eastern Railway has introduced special trains for candidates. The services will operate for two days, with four round trips between Ranchi and Medininagar, and Ranchi and Dumka. SER will also run a JTET special between Tatanagar and Deoghar. Train 08119 will leave Tatanagar at 6.30 pm on Sunday and reach Deoghar at 8 am on Monday. Train 08120 will depart Deoghar at 10.10 am on Monday and reach Tatanagar at 2.30 am on Tuesday. JAC has also opened a control room to address candidatesâ queries and logistical problems. The helpline numbers are 7485093436, 7485093437 and 7485093440. For many aspirants, the test marks the end of a long wait. âThe last JTET was held a year before I completed my graduation. Finally, I will be able to appear for the test after a long wait. I am confident I will clear it,â said aspirant Rajesh Kumar. (With inputs from B Sridhar in Jamshedpur) Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. Download the TOI App.

title: âSri Lanka, Bangladesh happen when protests are not allowedâ: Sonam Wangchuk on anti-SIR stir crackdown
text: NEW DELHI: Activist Sonam Wangchuk on Saturday described protests as a âgreat mechanismâ for governments to improve their performance, citing the unrest in Sri Lanka and Bangladesh as examples of what could happen when demonstrations are not allowed. âNations all around the world happily permit protests, and that too right in front of Parliament. In countries like the UK, Norway and Sweden, protests are allowed right in front of Parliament,â the educationist said at an event in Mumbai. âIn India, it was far from Parliament. Even when it was just Jantar Mantar, it was too far,â he added. Wangchuk was referring to demonstrations held at Delhiâs Jantar Mantar, the capitalâs now-denotified designated protest site, in June and July following the NEET-UG paper leak in May. The protests, in which Wangchuk played a key role by undertaking an indefinite fast for over 20 days before being removed and taken to a hospital, ended with the resignation of then-Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan on July 25. His remarks came amid ongoing protests in Delhi demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. The Centre deployed extensive security measures, drawing criticism from opposition parties. âLook what happens when protests are not allowed. That is the example of Sri Lanka, Bangladesh,â Wangchuk remarked, referring to the youth- and student-led demonstrations in Sri Lanka and Bangladesh that culminated in the ouster of the incumbent governments. title: Yet another futile attempt to attack Indian democracy
text: Indian democracy is highly respected across the world. An era of Indian democracy began with the framing of the Constitution by Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar after the end of British rule. Dr. Ambedkar drafted the Indian Constitution after studying the democratic system as well as the constitutions of several other countries. The limitation of democratic system became apparent over the period of time even in a developed country like the United States, which has a deep-rooted democratic legacy. However, Indian democracy continues to serve as an ideal model for many countries even today. It is through this system that the country is rapidly progressing towards becoming a developed nation. Precisely for this reason, anti-India forces have been trying to weaken the system for many years by attacking it through various means. These efforts have intensified since 2014. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has frequently expressed his resolve to achieve the goal of Viksit Bharat by 2047. Many powerful countries in the world are unable to digest Indiaâs ongoing progress towards becoming a developed nation. Several international groups are actively creating obstacles in Indiaâs path with the aim of making Indian citizens lose faith in the democratic system. These groups are getting assistance from the anti-national forces within the country itself. The NEET question paper leak case and the protests against the drive for intensive revision of electoral rolls have completely exposed anti-India forces. The Modi government has thwarted their plans. Several common factors between the ongoing violence in many European countries and the protests that took place in India around the same time have become evident on the international political stage. Indian democracy is strong enough to counter many such attacks. Three months ago, people posing as students suddenly launched a protest in the national capital over the issue of the NEET paper leak. There was a lot of anger among ordinary people over the question of the paper leak incident. The Modi government immediately took note of this public sentiment and made firm decisions to make the examination system completely foolproof. The protesters violated several security regulations by suddenly marching towards Parliament. They attacked the police and security force personnel. It was a clear attempt to breach security and enter Parliament. The police and security forces showed great restraint while handling this tense situation. The plan to incite violence in the country through this protest was completely foiled. The protesters involved in the farmersâ protest at the Delhi border 5-6 years ago and the Shaheen Bagh protest against the CAA (Citizenship Amendment Act) were definitely working with an agenda of provoking the police into opening fire. The riots that broke out in Delhi after the Shaheen Bagh protests proved that a large number of anarchic forces were active in the country. Muslims were systematically incited against the Modi government by spreading several rumours such as the Citizenship Amendment Act is against Indian Muslims and Muslims would be expelled from the country. The same âmodus operandiâ can be observed in the protests that have taken place in the country over the last 7-8 years. Protests were instigated in the same manner in Indiaâs neighbouring countries, such as Bangladesh and Nepal. The violence that followed these protests led to the regime change in both the countries. The protesters were working with the sole purpose of triggering nationwide violence by inciting youth and students to resort to violence while protesting against the âNEETâ question paper leak and intensive revision of electoral rolls, thereby provoking the police and security forces to open fire to bring the unrest under control. This protest, which was in a way a test of the Indian Constitution and democracy, failed as expected. The plot to overthrow the regime failed. This attack on Indian democracy failed because the citizens of this country did not fall prey to the provocations of anarchist forces and chose to stay away from the protest. There was a strong sentiment among students, parents, young people and the general public in India against the NEET question paper leak. Therefore, there was public sympathy for the protests that took place in Delhi in July. The Modi government took many policy decisions to further strengthen this examination system. An expert like Nandan Nilekani was given the responsibility of improving the examination technology system. Strict action was taken against all those involved in the question paper leak. Even then, the protesters revealed their hidden agenda by marching towards Parliament and attacking the police. Once ordinary citizens understood the conspiracy to create anarchy behind the protest, it became clear that the protest was bound to fail. The protesters were not satisfied even after the Modi government obtained the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan during the time of studentsâ protests. They were not willing to leave Delhi even after the government took a step back to have a dialogue with the protestors. The protesters got carried away due to the publicity and a certain degree of public support that they received. This led them to organize another round of violent protests under the pretext of opposing the intensive revision of electoral rolls. Congress and Rahul Gandhi started feeling insecure for their own existence after seeing the publicity and the limelight received by the student protesters. Out of this fear, he made a desperate attempt to project his so-called aggressive image by marching towards Parliament and the Supreme Court. A sense of anger started developing in Delhi and across the country against the protesters, whose daily protests disrupted the lives of ordinary Delhi residents. Despite several attempts, Rahul Gandhi failed to fulfil his aim of inciting violence. Numerous elections have shown that Indian citizens are extremely mature. Ordinary voters have the power to change the government in Indian democracy. The common man has immense faith in Indian democracy. This very belief instils confidence that attacks on Indian democracy will fail. Even though the attempt to topple the government failed, there is no guarantee that anti-India forces will stop trying. The citizens need to remain extremely alert against these elements in the coming days. Disclaimer : Views expressed above are the author's own.

title: 'No' to peace bond, 'yes' to INDIA bloc: Has Neha Bora outsmarted CJP leaders?
text: AISA president Neha Bora and CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke NEW DELHI: When Neha Bora recently said âAISA will not be a part of normalising the signing of peace bondsâ, she inadvertently highlighted a contrast that the Jantar Mantar 2.0 protests against SIR and "vote chori" had brought to the fore. Nehaâs refusal to sign the peace bond before a special executive magistrate and her subsequent challenge to the police move drew an obvious parallel. Did the CJP leaders - Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Sourav Das - give in to peace bond pressure easily? âPeace bonds are being weaponised to curb democratic protests. Signing such peace bonds is no less than signing away our democratic right to dissent,â the AISA national president said and claimed that she was detained within 10 minutes of protesting at Mandi House on October 16 and was told that she and other protesters were in breach of peace. âOn one side, the Constitution gives us the right to dissent. On the other hand, such peace bonds are invoked only to detain people in the name of breach of peace. Therefore, signing such peace bonds is a principally wrong decision for us. It is no less than signing away our democratic right to dissent,â Bora said defending her decision. Neha Bora on why she would not sign peace bond Bora has still not signed the bond and is awaiting copies of 6 FIRs cited as her criminal antecedents in peace-bond proceedings. This, after she insisted for all documents relied upon in the show-cause notice seeking execution of her peace bond. Now, letâs rewind to October 10. The CJPâs call for Jantar Mantar 2.0 on October 10 had, as expected, evoked great national interest and anticipation. All eyes were on Abhijeet Dipke and his associates Sourav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, who had in June-July this year led a successful youth mobilisation against NEET paper leak. The CJP-led protests had ensured that Dharmendra Pradhan was forced to resign as Union education minister. After all, they were the new heroes of GenZ, who had left the politicians far behind. But ahead of October 10, the national capital saw an unprecedented clampdown. The Delhi Police closed down anything and everything that could facilitate the movement of protesters to Jantar Mantar. For the CJP leadership, the message was loud and clear - they will not get a free passage, unlike in June when they were allowed to gather and mobilise youth at Jantar Mantar for their protests against NEET paper leak. But October 10 morning started with an anticlimax. The top 3 CJP leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das travelled together from Mumbai to Delhi and were detained from aircraft as soon as they landed in the national capital. Thousands of protesters who had responded to their calls, braved the police clampdown. They were all detained. The CJP leaders were released a day later after giving an undertaking to maintain public order. Delhi Police said a surety bond of Rs 50,000 was furnished for CJP activists Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das for maintaining peace and good behaviour for one year, following their preventive arrest on October 10. The CJP leaders made two more attempts to reclaim the streets - when Sourav Das and Ashutosh Ranka tried to reach Jantar Mantar and again when Dipke urged people to join the "Lehra Do Tiranga" march with the national flag at Central Park in Connaught Place. However, they were detained again and made to sign peace bonds to come out of detention. And while the CJP leaders failed to recreate the magic of Jantar Mantar 1.0, AISA leader Neha Bora took the centrestage. The AISA national president was detained 5 times between October 2 and October 11. However, every time she was released, she would come back to the streets and continue with her protests. During the peak of the protests, Neha Bora hogged the headlines for foxing the police. On October 11, Neha Bora announced a gathering at RK Ashram Marg Metro Station around 2:30pm as part of demonstrations heading toward central Delhi and Jantar Mantar. Heavy police deployment and barricades were set up around RK Ashram Marg to prevent demonstrators from moving toward Jantar Mantar. During the confrontation, police mistakenly chased and detained another protester whose face was partially covered, believing her to be Neha Bora. While police attention was focused at RK Ashram Marg, Neha Bora surfaced near Connaught Place (CP), breaching barricades and running alongside fellow demonstrators in a dash that went viral on social media. Little wonder then, when a user on X called Neha Bora "more talented" than CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and described her as a "complete GenZ icon", Dipke responded simply: "I agree." The X user had posted: "Maturity is realizing Neha Bora is more talented than Abhijeet Dipke. A complete GenZ icon with an absolutely ridiculous aura.â It was a comparison that manifested all along the âvote choriâ protests. Neha Bora was on the streets every time she was released from detention by the police. She was everywhere - with the CJP leadership, the social activists and also the politicians. When Rahul Gandhi chose to walk behind her during one of the protest marches of INDIA bloc, it spoke volumes about the impact she had made with her street politics. Clearly, the campaign against âvote choriâ had put the spotlight on Neha Bora, even as the CJP struggled to find their way to the centre stage of the protests. Neha Bora, along with Lok Sabha leader of the opposition Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi, during the opposition's protest. For the CJP, it was a harsh realisation that a lot had changed between July and October. Unlike the anti-NEET paper leak protests in June-July, the Congress-led INDIA bloc this time around were already on the streets demanding resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Interestingly, while the INDIA blocâs original protest schedule had only one announced street protest on October 6, the group returned back to the streets four days in a row till October 9, which was a day before the announced CJP protest. The CJP and the Congress had stayed away from each other during the anti-NEET protests. After Jantar Mantar 1.0 was over, the 'cockroaches' carried out their own campaigns in different states, while the Congress shifted focus to protests against SIR and CEC Gyanesh Kumar. So when CJP announced support for INDIA blocâs November 1 rally, it set tongues wagging about their political ambitions. With CJPâs Jantar Mantar 2.0 not shaping out as they would have hoped, perhaps its leadership should take a leaf out of Saurav Dasâs advice on X to a Congress âsoldierâ who had questioned why youth Congress and NSUI activists were being detained as soon as they hit the streets and cockroaches were allowed to roam free. Responding to him, CJP co-founder Saurav Das had then said: âif u guys r detained immediately, then u must rethink ur strategy. donât blame others for ur failures.â The context of that remark was different and CJPâs Jantar Mantar 2.0 campaign was in no way a failure, but Sourav's take on ârethinking strategyâ perhaps holds true for the cockroaches at present. title: AP seeks extension of MBBS admission deadline and reduction in NEET UG percentile
text: Of the 112 vacant NRI quota seats, 95 are in private medical colleges. The remaining vacancies include nine seats at Paderu Government Medical College and eight at Sri Padmavathi Medical College. Vijayawada : The National Medical Commission (NMC) has categorically agreed to examine APâs request to extend the MBBS admission deadline and for a reduction in the NEET-UG qualifying percentile for the 2026â27 academic year, following the vacancy of 112 MBBS seats under the Non-Resident Indian (NRI) quota after the completion of the stray round of counselling. Of the 112 vacant NRI quota seats, 95 are in private medical colleges. The remaining vacancies include nine seats at Paderu Government Medical College and eight at Sri Padmavathi Medical College. In a letter to the NMC chairperson and the Deputy Director General (Medical Education) in the office of the Director General of Health Services, the university registrar explained the situation and sought the necessary relaxations. The university had conducted the first, second and third rounds of counselling, including the mop-up round, followed by the stray round, in accordance with the prescribed guidelines. However, the seats remained unfilled despite the completion of the counselling process. The university also brought to the NMCâs notice a request from the Andhra Pradesh Private Medical and Dental Colleges Managements Association to extend the MBBS admission deadline until Nov 20, 2026. The NMC has indicated that it will examine the universityâs representation after the Oct 26 deadline expires and take an appropriate decision on the requested extension and relaxation in the qualifying percentile. title: In Ahmedabad, 29,201 put in preventive custody from Jan to Sept
text: Ahmedabad: City police took 29,201 people into preventive custody in the first nine months of 2026, averaging one detention every 13 minutes. The figures, which include action under three preventive provisions of the law, work out to around 107 people a day. Police records show that 26,098 people were taken into preventive custody under Section 107 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) between Jan 1 and Sept 30. Another 54 people were detained under Section 109, while 3,049 were taken into custody under Section 110 during the same period. Section 107 of the CrPC allows authorities to act against a person suspected of being likely to breach the peace. The person can be asked to provide a bond â a legal undertaking to maintain peace for a specified period. Section 109 is used when a person is suspected of hiding their presence, and there is a reason to believe they may commit an offence. Section 110 applies to habitual offenders, including those suspected of repeatedly committing crimes such as theft, robbery, or cheating. These provisions are intended to prevent offences rather than punish people for crimes already committed. The figures raise questions about the scale of preventive policing in the city, particularly as the CrPC was replaced by the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) in July 2024. Police records, however, continue to refer to the old provisions. Senior police officers attributed the high number of preventive actions to a range of public protests and agitations across the city. These included demonstrations against price rise and decisions of Union govt, protests over the NEET paper leak, civic body poll-related activities, and various student agitations. âSeveral protests and agitations took place in the city during the period. Preventive action was taken to ensure that these did not lead to a breach of peace,â a senior police officer said. Apart from protests, police drives aimed at preventing crime also contributed to the figures, officers said. text: Savitribai Phule Pune University (SPPU) Main Building Pune: Students from various groups have come together for a joint agitation against Savitribai Phule Pune University âs (SPPU) alleged restriction on peaceful protests, stringent campus access rules and ideological discrimination. The students, who call themselves progressive student groups, met on Thursday and planned to launch the âSave University Democracy Movementâ to protect studentsâ constitutional rights, freedom of expression and democratic space on campus. title: SOG arrests ex-prof who solved leaked SI exam papers for kingpin
text: Manohar Lal Jaipur: A 36-year-old former assistant professor at a govt college, who allegedly solved leaked question papers for both shifts of the 2021 Rajasthan Police Sub-Inspector recruitment examination for paper leak kingpin Jagdish Bishnoi, was arrested by the Special Operations Group (SOG) after evading arrest for years. Manohar Lal Manju, who taught public administration at Seth Mangalchand Govt College in Abu Road before suspension, was traced to Pindwara in Sirohi district on Oct 25 following a tip-off to the district police. He was brought to Jaipur, arrested by the investigating officer and Additional SP Chiranjee Lal Meena, and remanded to police custody until Wednesday. The SOG had announced a reward of Rs 25,000 for information leading to his arrest. A court had issued a permanent arrest warrant against him on April 22, 2025. According to ADGP (SOG) Vishal Bansal, the investigation revealed that question papers for both shifts of the examination on Sept 14, 2021, were leaked before the test from Ravindra Bal Bharati Senior Secondary School in Jaipurâs Hasanpura area. Investigators allege that Bishnoi, a resident of Danta village in Jalore district, orchestrated the leak with associates, including Pankaj Chaudhary alias Unique Bhambu and Shiv Ratan Mot. Manohar Lal allegedly joined Bishnoi and other paper solvers, including Praveen Bishnoi, Praveen Parawa and Rajiv Bishnoi, at a flat in Jaipur, where they solved the leaked papers. The arrangement was allegedly part of a deal with Om Prakash Dhaka. Bishnoi then allegedly sent the solved papers to handlers over WhatsApp before the examination. The handlers allegedly struck deals with candidates and supplied them with the answers, enabling them to clear the written test unfairly and secure selection as sub-inspectors, police said. title: ED attaches five properties worth Rs 2cr in constable paper leak case
text: Representational image Patna : The Patna zonal office of Directorate of Enforcement (ED) has provisionally attached five immovable properties of M/s N C Print Private Ltd, valued at Rs 2.01 crore, under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002, in connection with its probe into the Bihar Constable Recruitment-2023 examination paper leak case, the central agency said here on Friday. The money-laundering investigation was initiated on the basis of an FIR registered by Economic Offences Unit (EOU), Patna. The FIR invoked sections 120B, 420, 467 and 468 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, and Section 66 of the Information Technology Act, 2000, against various Telegram URLs, mobile numbers and bank accounts allegedly involved in the leak of the Bihar Constable Recruitment Examination question paper. According to the chargesheet filed by EOU on Aug 22, 2024, Kaushik Kumar Kar, owner of Blessings Secured Press Pvt Ltd, allegedly orchestrated a conspiracy to secure the contract for printing the question papers through his proxy company, Caltex Multiventures Pvt Ltd. The contract was awarded by Central Selection Board of Constable, Bihar, despite Caltex allegedly having no prior printing experience and no printing press of its own. ED said the arrangement concealed the role of Blessings Secured Press, which had earlier been blacklisted for alleged involvement in examination paper leak cases. The question papers for the 2023 constable recruitment exam were transported from Kolkata to Patna and were allegedly leaked en route to examination centres in connivance with other accused persons. The leak led to cancellation of the examination, causing financial loss to Bihar govt and adversely affecting aspirants. EDâs investigation found that Kar, the beneficial owner of the blacklisted Blessings Secured Press, incorporated Caltex Multiventures Pvt Ltd by appointing associates as dummy directors to bypass restrictions arising from the earlier cases. The agency alleged that Caltex secured the printing contract âthrough cheating, forgery and criminal conspiracyâ and outsourced the work to Blessings Secured Press in violation of its agreement with Central Selection Board of Constable. Caltex allegedly received an advance of Rs 5.9 crore, remitted only part of the funds to Blessings Secured Press, and diverted Rs 2.01 crore through various shell entities. ED said the proceeds of crime were layered through Kolkata-based shell companies lacking genuine business operations, routed under bogus transactions, converted into cash and dissipated. Since the diverted proceeds could not be traced further, ED attached five properties of NC Print Pvt Ltd, another company allegedly controlled and beneficially owned by Kar, as the equivalent value of the identified proceeds of crime. Further investigation is underway, ED said. title: Generate questions at last minute to prevent paper leaks: Nilekani
text: NEW DELHI: Question papers for high-stakes entrance examinations could be generated at the last minute from a massive bank of questions instead of being prepared and stored in advance, as part of a technology-driven overhaul to prevent leaks, Nandan Nilekani , chairperson of the high-powered task force on examination reforms, said on Tuesday. He also said PM Modi was keen to implement the panel's recommendations. Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum 2026 in Delhi, the Infosys chairperson questioned the need for a fixed question paper, arguing that its existence created an economic incentive for theft and sale. "Why do we need to have something called a question paper? Because the moment you have a question paper, that creates an economic incentive for that to be sold," Nilekani said. He suggested creating a massive question bank from which the paper would be assembled just before the examination. This, he said, would eliminate the incentive for advance leaks. Watch Paper Leak Law Passed, But Can Tougher Punishment Alone Stop India's Endless Exam Leak Crisis? Nilekani: Need to expand comp-based testing infrastructure Asked whether artificial intelligence could generate papers on examination day, Nandan Nilekani, replied, "Yeah, sure." The proposal comes as the six-member task force prepares to submit its report later this month, following extensive consultations on examination security, technology and governance. TOI reported on Oct 1 that the panel was prioritising "debundling" examination responsibilities by separating question-paper setting, exam conduct, test-centre management and security among different agencies. The restructuring seeks to reduce concentration of control over exams. A common calendar for major recruitment and entrance tests is also under consideration. Earlier, on Sept 16, TOI reported that multiple attempts at high-stakes entrance examinations and better-equipped, secure testing centres were among the prominent suggestions received by the task force. title: MPSC paper leak case: Suspension is not enough, strict punishment must follow, says Kadam
text: MPSC Paper Leak Case: Suspension Is Not Enough, Strict Punishment Must Follow, Says Kadam Pune: The protest against the MPSC examination paper leak is not merely a struggle by students but a fight for the pride and identity of Maharashtra . The movement has shaken the entire administrative machinery and exposed the challenges posed by corrupt politics. The inquiry committee appointed to investigate the matter must submit a thoroughly transparent report. Those found guilty in the paper leak case must not be let off with suspension alone. They must face the strictest possible punishment under the law so that nobody dares to commit such an offence in the future. Former minister and MLA Vishwajeet Kadam gave this assurance, pledging to stand shoulder to shoulder with the students until their struggle achieves its objective. On Monday, students collectively felicitated MLA Vishwajeet Kadam in recognition of his steadfast support for their demands and his determination to continue the fight until they are fulfilled. The programme was organised at Indulal Complex on Shastri Road in Pune. The programme was organised through the initiative of Swapnil Bhise, Amol Salve, Dhananjay Nikam, among others. Speaking on the occasion, Vishwajeet Kadam emphasised that examination paper leaks are rarely the work of a single individual. Instead, they often involve an entire network that must be identified and exposed. The movement must send a strong message across Maharashtra that nobody should even contemplate leaking examination papers, either today or in the future. He praised the determination of students who come to Pune from every corner of Maharashtra and study for as many as sixteen hours a day despite their financially disadvantaged backgrounds. He described them not merely as students but as the future pillars of Maharashtra. The MPSC paper leak and the corrupt practices of certain individuals have undermined the hard work of aspiring candidates and allowed unsuitable people to occupy positions. Such incidents do more than shatter studentsâ expectations. The anger they generate among young aspirants is entirely understandable. Kadam stressed that the network responsible for such a serious offence must be dismantled rather than protected. He observed that the movement, which emerged under student leadership, has gone far beyond the streets. It has reached households across Maharashtra and even drawn attention at the national level in Delhi. Students Urged to Gather Evidence and Submit It to the Inquiry Committee Addressing the students leading the movement, Vishwajeet Kadam urged them to travel across Maharashtra in groups, gather any additional evidence relating to the paper leak and submit it to the inquiry committee. He assured them of his full support throughout this process. He also called upon Maharashtra govt to remain accountable to the people and ensure that no obstacles are placed in the way of the ongoing investigation. Kadam stated that if the inquiry report was found to be satisfactory, it would certainly be accepted. However, if the findings were considered inadequate or inappropriate, govt would be urged to make the necessary corrections and pursue further investigation. He concluded by reaffirming his unwavering commitment to the students, assuring them that he would stand firmly by their side even if the circumstances required them to return to the streets and continue their struggle. title: NEET cancellation despite security overhaul exposes gaps in NTA reforms: House panel
text: The NTA's 2024-25 annual report recorded 474 court cases, including 356 concerning NEET-UG 2024. The panel said restoring confidence required "consistent, transparent, and two-way communication", rather than engagement largely restricted to portals and notifications. NEW DELHI: Move NEET-UG to computers, build secure question banks and invest NTA's accumulated surplus in government-run test centres: a parliamentary panel has sought a sweeping overhaul of NTA after NEET-UG 2026 had to be cancelled and conducted afresh despite biometric checks, mobile jammers and AI-monitored CCTV. After the 2024 controversies, it questioned whether security upgrades alone can safeguard examinations. The parliamentary standing committee on education, chaired by Mukul Wasnik, in its 382nd report presented on Friday, said the cancellation despite strengthened safeguards demonstrated the need for "greater procedural and institutional reforms". Its 35 observations and recommendations include an independent mechanism to audit examination security, investigate candidates' grievances and report directly to the education ministry. Acknowledging that NTA conducts examinations involving around 1.2 crore candidates annually, the panel welcomed reforms introduced since 2024, including biometric authentication and coordination with states. However, it flagged structural weaknesses in staffing, accountability, outsourcing and transparency, arguing that rebuilding public trust required more than new surveillance measures. The scale of disputes has been substantial. The NTA's 2024-25 annual report recorded 474 court cases, including 356 concerning NEET-UG 2024. The panel said restoring confidence required "consistent, transparent, and two-way communication", rather than engagement largely restricted to portals and notifications. The committee found that 16 of NTA's 39 sanctioned posts were vacant, a 41% shortfall. Existing positions are filled through deputation, limiting continuity in specialised work. It recommended permanent recruitment of experts in psychometrics, examination security, technology and logistics, while discouraging appointments to the director general's post as an additional charge. It also questioned NTA's legal status as a registered society, pointing out that it does not lay its annual report before Parliament and faces less scrutiny than a statutory body. The committee sought a framework ensuring parliamentary accountability. Private examination centres had "often proved to be a weak link in examination security", the report observed. It called for government-owned centres, bringing logistics in-house, and a national registry of blacklisted vendors to prevent disqualified firms from securing contracts elsewhere. On transparency, the panel recommended UPSC-style disclosure of NEET results, noting that centre-wise data released following Supreme Court directions in 2024 had enabled public scrutiny. It also flagged the absence of an official public record of paper leaks, FIRs and investigations. title: Generate question papers at last minute to prevent leaks: Nilekani
text: Nandan Nilekani, head of the examination reforms task force, suggests a transformative approach to create question papers. NEW DELHI: Question papers for high-stakes entrance examinations could be generated at the last minute from a massive bank of questions instead of being prepared and stored in advance, as part of a technology-driven overhaul to prevent leaks, Nandan Nilekani , chairman of the high-powered task force on examination reforms, said on Tuesday. He also said Prime Minister Narendra Modi was keen to implement the panelâs recommendations. Speaking at the Bloomberg new economy Forum 2026 in Delhi, the Infosys chairman questioned the need for a fixed question paper, arguing that its existence created an economic incentive for theft and sale. âWhy do we need to have something called a question paper? Because the moment you have a question paper, that creates an economic incentive for that to be sold,â Nilekani said. He suggested creating a massive question bank from which the paper would be assembled just before the examination. This, he said, would eliminate the incentive for advance leaks. Asked whether artificial intelligence could generate papers on examination day, he replied, âYeah, sure.â The proposal comes as the six-member task force prepares to submit its report later this month, following extensive consultations on examination security, technology and governance. TOI had reported on Oct 1 that the panel was prioritising âdebundlingâ examination responsibilities by separating question-paper setting, examination conduct, test-centre management and security among different agencies. The proposed restructuring seeks to reduce concentration of control over examinations. A common calendar for major recruitment and entrance tests is also under consideration. Earlier, on Sept 16, TOI reported that multiple attempts at high-stakes entrance examinations and better-equipped, secure testing centres were among the prominent suggestions received by the task force. The recommendations included reliable electricity, internet connectivity, biometric verification and CCTV surveillance. Nilekani also stressed expanding computer-based testing infrastructure. He said the existing network of around 1.5 lakh testing locations needed to grow to accommodate a wider shift towards computer-based examinations. âIf you look at it systematically and go to root causes of why it's happening and use technology to solve it... they are solvable issues,â he said. Constituted on July 26 following the NEET-UG controversy and student protests, the task force has held around 18 panel meetings and 40 consultations. It has received over 50,000 suggestions from students, parents, professional associations and examination bodies. A recent parliamentary committee report has also recommended expanding computer-based testing facilities, with at least one centre in every district to reduce candidatesâ travel and accommodation costs. title: Man faces FIR for alleged NCRA recruitment exam question paper leak
text: FIR representational photo Pune: Chatushrungi police on Monday registered a case against a 40-year-old man under the Official Secrets Act, 1923, in connection with an alleged question paper leak during the National Centre for Radio Astrophysics (NCRA), Pune, recruitment examination. The FIR followed a complaint lodged by Vaibhav Sherkar, a technical officer at the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR) in Mumbai. The recruitment examination was conducted in May 2025 for four vacant posts of work assistants at NCRAâs Aundh office near the SPPU campus. Uttam Bhajnawale, senior inspector of Chatushrungi police, said, âSherkar is working as a vigilance officer. NCRA functions with the TIFR and both are govt organisations. â Asked why the complaint was registered after a long gap, Bhajnawale said, âNCRA officials came to know about the question paper leak in July this year. They investigated the matter and, after confirming the sequence of events, registered the case with us.â âSherkar alleged that the question paper had been circulated before the examination and that the matter required investigation,â he said. Citing the FIR, Bhajnawale said, âSherkar received information from a confidential source on July 31 this year that the recruitment examination had faced irregularities. He was informed that one of the recently recruited Class IV employees had received the question paper on a messaging application before the recruitment test took place.â âOne of the contractual employees, who also worked at NCRA as a work assistant, took photographs of the question paper using his cellphone and forwarded them to a candidate,â he said, adding that the employees â the one who photographed the question paper and the one who received it â have been sent on leave by senior officers. Apart from Section 3(5) of the Official Secrets Act, 1923, the police also invoked Sections 316(2) and 316(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) in the FIR. title: High fees leaves over 800 MBBS seats vacant in deemed universities across TN, Puducherry
text: High fees leaves over 800 MBBS seats vacant in deemed universities across TN, Puducherry More than 800 medical seats remain vacant across deemed universities in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry after the final counselling held for NEET UG 2026, sources said on Thursday. High tuition fees have led to this situation, say educationists and industry experts. According to Medical Counselling Committee (MCC) sources, of the total 837 unfilled MBBS seats across the country (including All India Quota seats), 824 were vacant in deemed universities in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry alone. Educationists criticised the lack of a fee cap for deemed universities and pointed out that high-scoring NEET candidates are forced to forgo these seats simply because they cannot afford the exorbitant fees, thereby defeating the core purpose of conducting a merit-based national entrance examination. Senior educationist and State Platform for Common School System - Tamil Nadu (SPCSS-TN) general secretary P B Prince Gajendra Babu told PTI that the high scorer in NEET, whose financial position does not permit them to get admitted to such private institutions with a high fee, simply opts out. Such candidates do not apply for the counselling. "The lesser scorer who is financially sound applies and secures the seat," he said, adding, "NEET failed in both of its objectives -- neither ensure merit nor curb commercialisation of medical education." He said all private medical education institutions, including those deemed to be universities that cannot reduce their fee structure and keep the seats unfilled, must be closed. "The state governments should be encouraged to open an adequate number of medical colleges wherever needed," he added. Industry experts cite the excessive annual tuition fees as the main driver behind the low intake. A Srinath, a higher education career counsellor for the students in the city, claimed annual MBBS fees in deemed universities across Tamil Nadu and Puducherry range between Rs 25 lakh and Rs 35 lakh per year. "The students have to pay hostel and mess fees between Rs 1.2 lakh and Rs 2.5 lakh per year in private institutions. In contrast, the average annual fee across other parts of India in private institutions stands at around Rs 17 lakh, resulting in a substantial fee disparity over the four and a half year duration of the course," he said. With the seats remaining unfilled, an additional round of counselling may be expected. The MCC will take a decision in this regard. "However, it is unclear till now," he added. title: 2027 polls a battle of devpt vs destruction, nationalism vs casteism: Maurya
text: Union Home minister Amit Shah receives a warm welcome from deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya upon his arrival, in Lucknow on Friday Lucknow: Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya on Friday moved a political resolution at the BJP State Working Committee meeting, projecting the 2027 Assembly election as a decisive ideological contest between âdevelopment and nationalismâ on one side and âdestruction and caste politicsâ on the other. The resolution categorically called for an aggressive organisational push, social outreach across communities and a renewed focus on booth-level strengthening even as the party gears up for the state elections due early next year. Maurya asserted that the political environment in Uttar Pradesh remained favourable to the BJP despite the oppositionâs attempts to forge alliances. In an apparent reference to INDIA bloc, Maurya said while â14-15 partiesâ had joined hands with the objective of defeating the BJP, they had failed to dent the partyâs electoral dominance since 2014. The resolution aimed to strike an election-mode pitch, arguing that the 2027 Assembly polls would be much more than a routine political contest. According to the document, the election would be a battle of âvinash versus vikasâ (destruction versus development) and âcasteism versus nationalism.â It accused the opposition of lacking policy, intent and leadership while relying on allegations and divisive politics. The resolution alleged that the Samajwadi Party and Congress were trying to create social divisions by fuelling caste tensions in the state. Maurya argued that opposition parties had repeatedly attempted to unite anti-BJP forces but failed to dislodge the party from power. Referring to the 2022 Assembly election, he noted that the BJP and its allies won 278 seats despite the oppositionâs efforts to build a broad coalition. The document also accused opposition parties of promoting negative campaigns and spreading âmisleading narrativesâ against BJP govt. It urged party workers to counter such campaigns with facts and communicate the achievements of both the Narendra Modi-led Centre and Yogi Adityanath govt in UP. Referring to the recent Cockroach Janta Party stir in Delhi against the NEET paper leak and ECI, the resolution claimed that anti-national and foreign-funded forces were attempting to create unrest by influencing sections of youth and amplifying negative messaging through social media. The resolution called on BJP workers to effectively rebut such narratives. Maurya emphasised that social harmony should not remain merely a slogan but become a behavioural commitment for party workers. He urged BJP cadres to actively engage with all sections of society, including upper castes, Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, OBCs, Extremely Backward Classes, the poor, youth, farmers and women. The resolution focused heavily on organisational preparedness. The document asked BJP functionaries to introspect on whether booth committees were functioning effectively, whether office-bearers were performing their assigned responsibilities and whether district and regional leaders remained accessible to the public. Maurya said election preparation could not begin a few months before polling and had to be a continuous process driven by organisational discipline, public outreach and worker engagement. The resolution described the 2027 election as a test not only of govtâs performance but also of the BJPâs organisational strength and public connect. It called upon party leaders and workers to work collectively, maintain unity and take the achievements of state and central govts to voters. Framing the 2027 contest as a âcollective responsibility,â Maurya urged the organisation to convert the BJPâs social coalition and governance record into electoral support and secure a third consecutive mandate in UP. title: NEET-UG may shift from pen-and-paper to online mode as Centre works on national CBT infrastructure
text: NEET-UG could shift from pen-and-paper to computer-based testing as the Centre prepares a national CBT framework, with rural access, infrastructure and equity among candidates being considered before a final decision. The Ministry of Education is working on a national-level Computer-Based Testing (CBT) infrastructure strategy that could pave the way for NEET-UG to move from its existing pen-and-paper format to an online examination system according to media reports. The proposed shift is being examined as part of the broader effort to strengthen Indiaâs public examination system following the NEET-UG paper leak controversy. However, the government is expected to take a final decision only after receiving the recommendations of the high-level task force headed by Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani . Centre plans national CBT infrastructure for entrance exams A senior Ministry of Education official told PTI that the government is preparing a national examination-grade CBT infrastructure framework. The proposed system is intended to address the uneven availability of suitable test centres across the country, establish common technical standards, and make it possible to shift examinations currently held in pen-and-paper format to computer-based testing. The strategy is also being considered through a multi-model sourcing approach, under which different mechanisms could potentially be used to create and expand examination infrastructure. The move is not limited to NEET-UG. Once the required infrastructure is established, the broader objective is to facilitate the migration of more entrance examinations to the online mode. Several major examinations conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA), including JEE Main, CUET-UG, CUET-PG, UGC-NET and CSIR-UGC-NET, are already conducted in CBT mode. NEET-UG remains one of the major exceptions, with candidates currently taking the examination using pen and paper. NEET online shift to factor in rural and low-connectivity areas Moving an examination as large as NEET-UG to CBT would require more than simply setting up additional computer centres. The government is examining how the transition would affect candidates in rural and remote areas, particularly those living in districts with limited connectivity and access to examination infrastructure. The Ministry official said the proposed NEET transition plan is examining the sequencing of the shift, infrastructure requirements, and its implications for equity among candidates, including rural candidates and women. This aspect assumes importance because NEET-UG is taken by candidates from across the country, including students from areas where access to reliable digital infrastructure may be limited. The government is therefore looking at the infrastructure requirements before making a final decision on the mode of the examination. Nandan Nilekani-led task force report awaited The proposed changes are also linked to the wider examination reforms being considered by the Centre. The NEET-UG paper leak controversy triggered widespread protests and prompted the government to examine vulnerabilities in the country's examination system. Prime Minister Narendra Modi subsequently announced a high-powered task force headed by Nandan Nilekani to recommend measures to strengthen and secure public examinations. The task force's recommendations are still awaited. According to the Ministry official, the final approach to shifting NEET-UG to CBT will take into account the panel's recommendations as well as consultations with the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and the National Medical Commission. The NTA is separately undergoing an overhaul as the government reviews the way major entrance and eligibility examinations are conducted. NEET-UG is taken by nearly 25 lakh candidates The scale of NEET-UG makes the proposed transition particularly challenging. Nearly 25 lakh candidates appear for the examination every year, making it one of India's largest undergraduate entrance tests. NEET scores are used for admission to MBBS programmes as well as undergraduate courses in dentistry, Ayurveda, Unani, and Siddha. There are around 1.08 lakh MBBS seats in the country, including approximately 56,000 seats in government medical colleges and around 52,000 in private institutions. A shift to CBT would therefore require a large and geographically distributed network of examination centres capable of handling the candidate volume while maintaining uniform examination conditions. NEET CBT proposal gains momentum after paper leak The possibility of conducting NEET-UG online is not new. The proposal has been discussed at various points in the past, but the recent examination controversy has given fresh momentum to the idea. For the government, the immediate task is to determine whether the country has, or can build, the infrastructure needed for such a large-scale transition without creating new disadvantages for candidates. For now, NEET-UG continues to remain a pen-and-paper examination. The Centre is working on the infrastructure framework, while the final decision on the transition to CBT is expected after the Nilekani-led task force submits its recommendations and consultations with the health authorities are completed. text: Congress workers celebrate Abhijit Wanjarriâs victory in Nagpur on Thursday Mumbai: The wins from three of the five MLC seats came as a shot in the arm for MVA in the first elections since the Gen Z-led protests over alleged vote theft and paper leaks. title: He is an artist, bro!
text: Diljit Dosanjh Diljit Dosanjh demonstrated this when he performed for around 80,000 people in Delhi on Friday. Despite the initial hiccups over permissions, the singer made sure Delhi was where he began his tour. Welcomed with roaring cheers, Diljitâs concert was like one grand party where different groups came together to have a good time. Families, friends, lovers and solo concertgoers all shared one common thread â Dosanjhawallah. You wanted bhangra, you got it. You wanted him to dance, you got it. You wanted him to climb up the stage and make a grand entry, you got it. You wanted him to address the controversy surrounding his comments during the studentsâ protests; you got that too! âHate me as much as you can; I only have love for you. I love you all,â was the message Diljit kept giving his fans and critics alike. Watch Abhijeet Dipke Apologises To Diljit Dosanjh After Punjabi Singer Slams CJP Over Satluj Mockery Celebrities usually try to steer clear of topics that become controversial for them. But here is an artist who has made a phrase that once invited criticism into something he owns with pride. For the uninitiated, Diljit was asked during an Instagram Live whether he would like to comment on the studentsâ protests at Jantar Mantar over the NEET paper leak. His response was, âKeep me away from all this. Bro, Iâm an artist.â He also said that he did not know enough about the matter to comment, while extending his wishes to both the protesters and those at the centre of the protests. His remark, âI am an artist, broâ, drew criticism from people who felt he was distancing himself from an issue. The issue came up again when Abhijeet Dipke took a dig at Diljit during a protest at Jantar Mantar. He mocked the singerâs âI am an artist, broâ response while referencing his film Satluj. The film, based on human rights activist Jaswant Singh Khalra, had faced years of delays over certification before finally releasing on ZEE5 in July 2026. It was taken down from the platform within two days. Dipkeâs remark pointed to the contrast between Diljit distancing himself from the protests by saying he was an artist and his own involvement in a film about a politically significant subject. Diljit addressed the issue himself at the concert. âDonât poke me when I am not poking you. Punjabiyon nu na sikhao ladayian kidda ladhi jaandiye,â he said. He also reiterated that he supports everyone and loves everyone. Referring to Satluj, he reminded the audience that the film was about Jaswant Singh Khalra and that they had fought for a long time to get it made and released. He didnât wait for someone to bring it up. He addressed it himself, in front of thousands of people, without appearing embarrassed or defensive. He has always been open about issues, and his fans know this side of him. This wasnât a new version of Diljit trying to explain himself. It was the same Diljit being himself. He has even released a playlist titled I Am an Artist, Bro. And the message made its way to the closing moments of the concert, too, with the laser display carrying the same sentiment. It was no longer just a response to a question or a phrase used by his critics. He had made it his own. You can disagree with what Diljit says, question his choices or criticise him. But he gets to decide how he responds. And if he wants to keep saying, âI am an artist, broâ, he can. He doesnât have to say it apologetically or explain himself every time. After all, he is an artist, bro. And he is going to be himself. Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app. Give your child the gift of confidence! title: IISc develops 3D-printed model to study how cancer drugs penetrate tumours
text: BENGALURU: Researchers from IISc have developed a low-cost, 3D-printed device that could help scientists understand why cancer drugs are less effective in deeper regions of solid tumours. The device recreates the nutrient- and oxygen-deprived conditions found inside tumours and allows researchers to examine how cancer cells respond to drugs at different depths. The platform, developed by researchers from IIScâs Department of Chemical Engineering, addresses a longstanding challenge in cancer research: reproducing the complex microenvironment of solid tumours in laboratory conditions while retaining access to cells from different regions for analysis. In solid tumours, blood vessels are often poorly developed and unevenly distributed. Consequently, cells closer to blood vessels receive more oxygen and nutrients, while those farther away experience shortages. These differences can influence how cancer cells grow and respond to treatment. Conventional laboratory methods that grow cancer cells in flat, two-dimensional layers do not adequately reproduce these conditions. One approach to overcoming this limitation is the 'Cells-in-Gel-in-Paper' (CiGiP) model, in which cancer cells embedded in a gel are grown on stacked paper layers. Nutrients and oxygen supplied from one side diffuse through the stack, creating conditions resembling different depths of a tumour. However, existing versions of this technique rely on wax-printed or hydrophobic barriers to contain the cell culture within each paper layer. The discontinuation of solid-ink printers, which were used for this purpose, has made the method less accessible to laboratories. The IISc team has replaced this requirement with a simple press-fit enclosure made using fused deposition modelling (FDM) 3D printers. Designed by Ankit Kumar, a PhD student in the laboratory of Bhushan J Toley, the device holds eight circular paper discs together through gentle, uniform pressure, preventing nutrients and drugs from leaking around their edges. Culture medium is supplied through an inlet at the top. The researchers tested the platform using MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells embedded in Matrigel. After 72 hours, they found that the number of live cells progressively decreased from the topmost to the bottommost layer, while dead cells increased. Expression of HIF-1alpha, a gene associated with low-oxygen conditions, also rose towards the deeper layers, confirming that the model recreated a hypoxic tumour-like environment. The team then examined how the chemotherapy drug doxorubicin penetrated the tissue. Drug uptake declined progressively across the eight layers, indicating that deeper regions received less of the drug. Longer treatment periods partially overcame these diffusion limitations. Using a statistical method called the Bliss synergy score, they found that the two drugs had an antagonistic interaction across all eight layers when administered together. This means their combined effect was lower than what would be expected if the drugs acted independently. Published in Analytical Methods in 2026, the study was led by Toley, with Kumar and Shweta Kumar as co-authors. The researchers have made the deviceâs design files publicly available to facilitate reproduction. They believe the approach could make paper-supported 3D tumour models more accessible for drug screening and studies of treatment response. Get the latest India News and Live updates. title: When institutions fail, a generation pays
text: Over a decade, the weakening of institutional checks has raised questions about accountability and democratic safeguards. The fallout goes beyond politics and education, threatening public trust and the future of Indiaâs youth A young Indian can spend years preparing for an examination, sacrifice a familyâs savings for a degree and acquire skills in the hope of finding work. Yet none of that effort can guarantee a fair chance if the institutions governing these pursuits fail them. The tragedy is not merely that a student may lose an opportunity. It is that the promise on which an entire generation has built its future begins to look unreliable. This is the larger cost of Indiaâs institutional decline over the past decade. When accountability weakens and power becomes increasingly centralised, the consequences do not remain confined to Parliament or government offices. They travel into classrooms, examination halls and workplaces. Indiaâs young may ultimately pay the highest price. The cost of silence Institutions rarely lose their authority overnight. Their effectiveness can erode incrementallyâas independent scrutiny becomes inconvenient, dissent is treated as disloyalty and accountability yields to political expediency. Parliament continues to function, elections are held and constitutional bodies retain their formal powers. But democracy requires more than the survival of its structures. It requires those structures to scrutinise decisions, expose shortcomings and correct mistakes. Consider Parliament. According to PRS Legislative Research, only 16 per cent of Bills in the 17th Lok Sabha were referred to committees for detailed scrutiny, compared with 71 per cent in the 15th Lok Sabha. Legislation affecting millions deserves rigorous examination, expert input and meaningful debate. When scrutiny diminishes, the risk is that shortcomings go undetected until citizens bear their consequences. When students pay The cost of institutional failure becomes painfully tangible in education. Families make enormous sacrifices to educate their children, while students invest years in competitive examinations that can determine their futures. The credibility of those examinations is therefore not a mere administrative concern. It is a public trust. The 2026 student agitation over NEET-UG irregularities, which spread beyond Jantar Mantar and culminated in Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhanâs resignation, brought this trust deficit into sharp focus. Students demanding fairness were asking a fundamental question: what value does merit have if the process measuring it cannot command confidence? A ministerâs resignation is an act of political accountability. It is not, by itself, institutional reform. The real test is whether examination systems become more secure, responsibility is fixed, grievances are addressed promptly and those who lose opportunities through proven malpractice receive justice. The challenge extends beyond examinations. Universities need academic freedom, credible leadership and space for independent thought. Vocational education must equip young people with skills that employers recognise and the economy needs. A country aspiring to global economic leadership cannot afford a generation with qualifications it cannot trust, skills it cannot use or opportunities determined by connections rather than competence. Watching the watchdogs The problem reaches beyond education. A democracy needs independent scrutiny, a free press and institutions capable of questioning the government without fearing political consequences. In 2019, Parliament amended the Right to Information Act, replacing statutory provisions governing Information Commissionersâ tenure and service conditions with provisions allowing the Central Government to prescribe them. The Government defended the change as administrative, maintaining that the commissionsâ independence and citizensâ right to information remained unaffected. Yet, the institutional question is legitimate: when the government being questioned gains control over the terms governing the watchdog, what safeguards ensure that independence is not merely formal? Information Commissions matter to citizens seeking answers about public expenditure, recruitment and administrative decisions. Transparency is not an abstract ideal; it is a means by which the people can demand accountability from the state. The same principle applies to investigative agencies, regulators and the media. Not every investigation is politically motivated, nor does every institutional disagreement establish interference. But public confidence suffers when citizens suspect that standards are applied differently depending on who holds power. Institutions derive legitimacy not from official assurances but from consistent, impartial conduct. The future at stake Indiaâs young are not merely beneficiaries of development. They are its principal stakeholders. Their education, enterprise and ambition will help determine whether the country realises its economic potential. But aspiration cannot indefinitely compensate for institutions that fail to protect fairness and opportunity. This is by no means an argument for despair. Indiaâs institutions continue to function, citizens continue to question authority and public debate continues. That makes reform possible and institutional independence worth defending. The priorities are clear: rigorous parliamentary scrutiny, credible examinations, academic freedom, transparent appointments and impartial enforcement of the law. Institutions must be strengthened not because they serve one political party or another, but because they serve the nation. Governments are temporary custodians of public power. Institutions must outlast them, retaining the capacity to question authority, correct mistakes and protect citizens regardless of who governs. A nation can recover from a governmentâs mistakes. Rebuilding a generationâs lost faith is far harder. If Indiaâs young begin to believe that effort does not guarantee fairness, that merit cannot overcome a compromised process and that power need not answer questions, the damage will extend well beyond any election. The measure of a democracy is not simply who governs, but whether its institutions give every citizen a fair chance. Indiaâs future depends on getting that answer right. title: âTrue character of protests exposedâ: Dharmendra Pradhan attacks Rahul Gandhi over regime change remark
text: Dharmendra Pradhan criticized Rahul Gandhi for allegedly exploiting student protests to undermine India's democratic structure. Dharmendra Pradhan , who had resigned from the post of Union education minister after Cockroach Janta Party protests over paper leaks in July, accused Rahul Gandhi of using students as cover to destabilise India's political system. Citing Bangladesh's Gen Z uprising and calls for âregime changeâ, Pradhan alleged that the protests were part of a deliberate attempt to spread anarchy and challenge the country's democratic order. In his post on X, Pradhan said the âtrue characterâ of protests launched in the name of national interest, fixing the system and studentsâ welfare was no longer hidden. Watch Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan Resigns After Month-Long Protests, Lathi Charge Fury âHowever, these anti-national elements dreaming of power on the strength of foreign forces should understand that in India, change of power is determined only through democratic processes,â he said, adding that the people would never accept what he described as an undemocratic mindset. Targeting Rahul Gandhi, Pradhan accused the Leader of Opposition of repeatedly disrespecting the people's mandate and undermining democratic institutions when electoral outcomes did not favour the Congress. He alleged that the party sought to create distrust in constitutional institutions for political gains, adding that its approach reflected a mentality in which the rights of citizens had been trampled. âRahul Gandhi, the anti-Constitution figure who roams around holding the Constitution, has been repeatedly rejected by the people,â Pradhan said, accusing him of insulting the electoral mandate and questioning constitutional institutions out of a desire for power. He described Rahul Gandhi's alleged attitude towards democracy as âextremely shamefulâ. The Congress, meanwhile, defended its call for âregime changeâ, saying it referred to defeating the BJP through democratic elections rather than destabilising the country. Addressing a press conference titled âAlbert Pinto Ko Gussa Kyoon Aata Haiâ, party leader Pawan Khera questioned defence minister Rajnath Singhâs allegations linking youth-led protests against the Election Commission to a Bangladesh-style political upheaval. âChanging the regime through elections is precisely the Oppositionâs goal, what else would our purpose be?â Khera said, accusing the BJP of having âlost the habit of practising democracyâ. The âregime changeâ remark emerged amid the ongoing protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of irregularities in the electoral process. Student activist Neha Bora invoked Bangladeshâs Gen Z uprising, while senior advocate Prashant Bhushan described the agitation as a âfight for regime changeâ.
