title: Enforcement Directorate reveals Rs 10 crore deal between Sahukar and realtor in Karnataka Public Service Commission scam
text: KPSC suspended chairperson Shivashankarappa Sahukar Bengaluru: The ongoing investigations into the alleged cash-for-job scam at Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) took an interesting turn. Enforcement Directorate (ED) sleuths told a special court that suspended KPSC chairman Shivashankarappa Sahukar had carried out transactions worth around Rs 10 crore with city realtor SP Dayananda. The revelations were made when ED sought the extension of judicial custody of Sahukar, currently lodged in judicial custody at Parappana Agrahara prison. Another accused, BV Geetha, a member of KPSC, is also in judicial custody. According to sources, ED told the court that it had recovered handwritten account sheets from the realtorâs car. The papers had the name and contact numbers of Sahukar. They logged Rs 5 crore allegedly received by Dayananda from Sahukar between Aug and Dec 2025, and the collective transactions between the two men aggregated to over Rs 10 crore. Also, ED explained to the court that Sahukar and Dayananda had financial transactions outside banking channels. Sahukar and Geetha were arrested on Oct 6 in connection with the alleged leak of questions and answers for a KPSC examination held on Jan 8 and 9 for the posts of veterinary doctors. title: Satish Waghole given additional charge as MPSC chairperson during Bhimanwar's leave
text: Satish Waghole given additional charge as MPSC chairperson during Bhimanwar's leave Maharashtra Public Service Commission member Satish Baban Waghole has been given additional charge as the panel's chairperson during the leave of incumbent Vivek Bhimanwar, who has been facing criticism from MPSC aspirants over alleged exam paper leaks and irregularities. Earlier this month, MPSC aspirants staged a 10-day protest in Pune over their various demands, including Bhimanwar's removal as the commission's chairperson. The Maharashtra government subsequently formed a committee, with senior IAS officer Tukaram Mundhe as secretary, to probe alleged irregularities, including paper leaks. The panel will also conduct a probe into the tenure of the present and past chairpersons and members of the state recruitment body, officials said. Bhimanwar later announced that he had proceeded on leave till the inquiry was completed. The state government's General Administration Department issued a notification on October 16, giving Waghole additional charge as MPSC's chairperson with effect from that date. Apart from Bhimanwar's removal, the MPSC aspirants have demanded withdrawal of cases against some representatives of the agitation, recruitment for 70,000 posts over three years, increase in the number of seats in the Group C examination scheduled for January, and background checks on the MPSC chairperson and secretary before their appointment. title: Original certificates lying with Haryana govt, MBBS graduates in the state are in a fix ahead of NEET admissions
text: They have addressed their letter seeking the originals to Dhirendra Khadgata, director of medical education and research, and marked a copy to Sumita Misra, additional chief secretary of health Gurgaon : Around 300 MBBS graduates who cleared NEET-PG and secured postgraduate seats risk losing them because their original documents are with the state govt under its bond policy. The doctors, who are racing against time as they face a Nov 2 deadline to complete admission verification formalities, have written to the directorate of health education for the release of their original documents, saying years of study and a hard-won opportunity to specialise in their subjects anywhere in the country could be jeopardised by an administrative delay. The dispute has affected graduates from four govt medical colleges â PGIMS, Rohtak; Shaheed Hasan Khan Mewati Govt Medical College in Nuh; Kalpana Chawla Govt Medical College in Karnal; and BPS Govt Medical College for Women in Sonipat. The doctors said colleges are retaining not just their permanent MBBS degrees, but also detailed mark cards for all four professional examinations, internship documents, character and attempt certificates, and permanent registration papers issued by Haryana Medical Council. They argued that the bond policy provided for withholding only the permanent degree, not these other documents. A provisional degree, they insisted, could serve in its place. They have addressed their letter seeking the originals to Dhirendra Khadgata, director of medical education and research, and marked a copy to Sumita Misra, additional chief secretary of health. WHY DOCUMENTS MATTER Page 51 of Medical Counselling Committeeâs information bulletin specifies that candidates are required to produce original certificates for physical verification. A sealed certificate or receipt confirming that their documents are held by a govt department may not meet this requirement, the graduates said. Without the originals, candidates risk being unable to complete formalities for MD and MS courses, even after securing seats through All India Quota counselling. âThe bond policy did not provide for withholding all these certificates. Only the permanent degree was to be held back, and students could use a provisional degree instead,â said Dr Akshat Mittal, a 2020-batch graduate of PGIMS Rohtak. WHAT IS BOND POLICY? Introduced in Nov 2020, govtâs undergraduate bond policy seeks to ensure that doctors serve in the stateâs medical system rather than move immediately into private practice. It requires graduates to serve for five years in public service or meet the applicable financial liability. The framework also allows them to pursue higher education in any medical college in the country through NEET-PG. The MBBS batch that took admission in Jan 2021 was the first to be covered under this policy. This batch graduated in Feb this year. But the affected graduates said govt has yet to put the promised employment mechanism in place. According to Mittal, the online portal intended to facilitate recruitment under the policy had not been created even nine months after their graduation. Vacancies, he added, had also shrunk after recruitment through Haryana Civil Medical Services (HCMS). âThe state govt introduced the bond on the premise that doctors were unwilling to serve in public institutions. Yet, more than 12,000 doctors applied for just 450 HCMS vacancies. Doctors are ready to work. The state just needs to provide enough posts,â he said. Mittal said the govt had time until Feb 2027 to fulfil its employment obligation, but the immediate deadline to submit documents for higher studies was Nov 2. âWe understand the bond conditions. But a dispute over employment and documents should not shut the door on higher education,â he added. Dr Tanisha Agarwal, another PGIMS graduate who secured an All India Rank of 8,800 in NEET-PG, said her seat had brought anxiety rather than relief. âOriginal documents are mandatory for verification. Yet, ours remain with the state. We were assured the bond policy would not hamper higher education. Now, our future is on hold,â she added. Dr Agarwal said representations to the college director and Directorate of Medical Education and Research (DMER) had yielded no resolution. Rachit, a graduate of SHKM GMC in Nalhar, who secured an All India Rank of 4,700 and an MD seat, said repeated approaches to the dean, director and DMER had also drawn blanks. Ankit Arora, another graduate of the college allotted an MD seat, said they could approach court if the documents are not released in time. Dr Ritu Ahlawat of PGIMS Rohtak said graduates were willing to fulfil the bond, but the retention of documents was preventing them from exercising their right to pursue higher studies. Indian Medical Association (IMA) has also written to DMER, seeking immediate release of original documents for NEET-PG all India counselling. In a letter signed by its president, Dr Sunila Soni, IMA sought a clear release deadline, uniform implementation across colleges, confirmation that pending bond formalities would not block admissions, and a standard procedure for future batches. In a fresh round of discussions on Thursday, DMER told a student delegation that file work at the directorate was completed and the file sent to the health minister for approval and signatures. The director also assured them that once it returned, deans would be asked to release documents against a prescribed affidavit. Students, however, said they had received no formal communication by the end of the day and were seeking meetings with the health minister and chief ministerâs office. A senior official at the directorate of health education told TOI that govt was working to release the documents. The official said graduates had been given sealed certificates issued in the name of the medical college director as proof that their originals were held by the department. âWe are also working to provide jobs under the bond policy. The process would be completed soon,â the official said. title: BJP's Karnataka sweep, Congressâs Nagpur surprise and Akhileshâs gains: What the MLC polls really tell us
text: TOI Newsletter This week, we are tracking: 28 seats, 4 states, and a Nagpur twist: Who really won the MLC polls ? 21 lakh followers, 33 votes: When Instagram fame meets electoral reality No time to settle: How Team Indiaâs batters are rewriting cricket Jioâs record debut: What it means for your SIPs BJP's Karnataka sweep, Congressâs Nagpur surprise and Akhileshâs gains: What the MLC polls really tell us If you followed Wednesdayâs social media feeds, youâd think we had just held a mini general election. PM Modi posted a taunt with an emoji. Opposition leaders declared that paper ballots had humbled âautocracyâ. All this over 28 Legislative Council seats chosen by teachers and graduates in four states. The scoreboard How MLC elections unfolded in 4 states The BJP-led NDA finished with 15 of the 28 seats. The cleanest result came from Karnataka, where the BJPâJD(S) combine took all four, much to the dismay of Congress. UP was a near tie: BJP six, SP five. The BJP held five of the six seats it won in 2020, while the SP kept all three of its seats and added two more. Bihar threw up the most curious mix. The NDA (BJP + JD-U) won 3 of 8 seats, the RJD got 2 and Prashant Kishorâs Jan Suraaj got 1 seat, and independents secured two seats. A Nagpur surprise And Maharashtra? Thatâs where the real drama was. As results trickled in, PM Modi asked on X: âGuess how many seats Congress won?â Devendra Fadnavis went a step further and declared a âbig fat zeroâ. Then Nagpur sprang a surprise and Congressâs Abhijeet Wanjari won against BJPâs Sudhakar Kohale. Fadnavisâs post vanished; the state Congress gleefully circulated a screenshot. Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma chipped in with a mock apology congratulating Congress on its one seat. The ballot-paper argument, again The opposition was quick to credit paper ballots. âIf the elections are held with ballot papersâ¦ even autocracy is defeated,â said Sena (UBT)âs Sanjay Raut. The BJPâs reply: ballots or not, it still won the most seats. If paper ballots were a magic wand, the Congress wouldnât have been wiped out in Karnataka. Quick take These are not assembly elections in miniature. All 28 seats were elected by graduates and teachers, not the general electorate. The electorate is highly selective. These polls can reveal organisational strength and attitudes among particular professional groups, but they do not represent the pulse of the wider electorate. Read more: Guess how many Congress won: PM Modi 'Commit to ballot paper': Congress dares after PM Modi takes swipe over MLC results MLC election: BJP's gains come with a Nagpur, Varanasi reminder from Congress and SP MLC polls: Nitin Gadkari confidant revolt mayâve hit BJP in Nagpur 21 lakh followers, 33 votes: The astrologer who didnât see it coming Omprakash Bishnoi contested for sarpanch of a village in western Rajasthan with roughly 1,600 voters. He polled 33 votes. This should not be a story. However, Bishnoiâs loss is instructive for several reasons. By internet standards, he is a star. He has about 21 lakh followers across social media platforms. He also calls himself an astrologer and face reader. Clearly, the astrologer could not see this one coming. Can CJP be the next AAP? Bishnoiâs result comes at a time when everyone is watching a far larger attempt to turn online reach into political heft. The Cockroach Janta Party began online as a satire. The CJP has already been instrumental in the resignation of the Union education minister over the NEET paper leak, and its Jantar Mantar 2.0 protest brought Delhi to a standstill. A dispersed online community can converge at a particular place on a given date over some grievance. That is what protest needs, and the CJP has delivered it. Elections, village ones above all, need the opposite: Support concentrated in one place and sustained through years of ordinary favours. CJP founder Abhijit Dipke has said he has no plans to turn the movement into a conventional party. But what if CJP decides to go the AAP way? Can it translate its online reach into votes at the ballot box? Read more: 2 million followers, just 33 votes: Poor poll result shocks Jodhpur astro-influencer Kharge says CJP not coming for rally, latter says yet to take a call HC refuses to entertain PIL seeking compensation from CJP for protests âExtra-terrestrial sent from Neptuneâ: CJPâs Saurav Das mocks claims over his Delhi residence Abhishek and Vaibhav: Meet the generation that wants to hit every ball Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi Abhishek Sharma's 35-ball century and 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's fearless hitting against New Zealand offered a glimpse into future of Indian batting. They are out to change the batting grammar: Get going from the opening ball. Chasing New Zealand's 198 in Wellington, India completed the chase in 13.2 overs, winning by six wickets with 40 deliveries remaining. Why this generation plays differently Young Indian batters now grow up watching the IPL, where 200 runs in 20 overs is perfectly doable. You are supposed to chase 10 runs per over. This forces you to bat aggressively and innovatively. Players increasingly practise range-hitting, bat-speed generation, unconventional scoring areas and situational batting against specialised bowling plans. The result is a generation that arrives at international cricket with a more developed attacking repertoire than its predecessors possessed at the same age. But it also creates difficult choices. Should every batter be encouraged to attack relentlessly? Does a team still need an anchor capable of responding to a collapse? How should players adapt when pitches offer significant assistance to bowlers? The strongest teams will probably need flexibility rather than one rigid philosophy. Read more: Perfect pairing? title: In 2006, an ISS astronaut reported a burning rubber smell near its oxygen generator; later NASA records described a smouldering component
text: AI generated representative image showing an astronaut inspecting life support equipment aboard the ISS, with an inset illustrating a heat damaged component. Credits - GeminiÂ A crew cannot afford to overlook a burning scent inside a spacecraft. An odd smell can indicate anything from an electrical problem to a chemical leak or an impending fire on the International Space Station, where astronauts rely on carefully regulated air circulation and life support equipment. The incident occurred on September 18, 2006, when NASA astronaut Jeff Williams reported a burning rubber smell near Russia's Elektron oxygen generator. The crew initially suspected smoke and followed the station's emergency procedures. Flight controllers declared a spacecraft emergency so communications about the problem could take priority. The generator was shut down while the crew investigated the source of the smell and possible contamination. A NASA technical paper later documented the incident and the air monitoring carried out during the response. The crew shut down the generator and cleaned up a potassium hydroxide leak. NASA's Office of Inspector General later listed the incident as a leak from the Russian-built oxygen generator and recorded that spare parts were delivered, allowing the unit to be repaired and reactivated. Potassium hydroxide is odourless, so the leak should not be presented as the confirmed source of the burning smell. A smell no one could ignore The incident occurred during Expedition 13, which included Russian cosmonaut Pavel Vinogradov, NASA astronaut Jeff Williams and European Space Agency astronaut Thomas Reiter. The Elektron generator had been undergoing troubleshooting and restart attempts. After the unit began operating, the crew noticed an unusual smell and a rise in temperature around the equipment. Williams described the smell as burning rubber, while the crew initially suspected smoke and followed the station's fire response procedures. Flight controllers declared a spacecraft emergency to ensure that communications about the incident took priority. As a precaution, the astronauts wore protective gloves and surgical masks, shut down the generator and took steps to prevent possible contaminants from spreading through the station's ventilation system. The crew was not told to evacuate the station. The source of the smell was not immediately established. Officials initially suspected an overheated rubber gasket, while the potassium hydroxide leak presented a separate contamination risk. The chemical is odourless but can irritate or burn tissue. The crew isolated the problem, cleaned the spill and used a charcoal filter to help remove potential contaminants. Officials reported that air monitoring readings for the compounds of concern remained low. Why the oxygen generator mattered The Elektron system helped maintain the station's supply of breathing oxygen through electrolysis. An electric current passed through water, separating it into oxygen and hydrogen. The oxygen entered the cabin air supply, while the system vented the hydrogen. The NASA technical definition of environmental control and life support systems describes how oxygen generation is a part of the entire system that allows humans to live in space. Making oxygen is only part of that system, which also has to control water, carbon dioxide, cabin pressure, ventilation and pollutants. The ISS had other oxygen sources, including stored oxygen tanks and chemical oxygen generators known as candles. These backup supplies allowed the crew to remain on board while the Elektron was shut down for investigation. The main concern was the combination of overheating and possible chemical contamination in a confined environment. Unlike people in a building, crew members aboard a spacecraft must locate the source, isolate the affected equipment and protect the station's atmosphere without interrupting other critical systems. What later investigations found The initial suspicion of an overheated rubber gasket was not the only description in the records. A later NASA presentation on ISS air quality monitoring listed the September 18, 2006 Elektron overheating incident as involving reported smoke and a solvent-like smell. It also recorded that a polymeric bushing on a bracket was smouldering. These later technical findings provide more detail about the incident, but they do not establish that the potassium hydroxide leak itself caused the smell The presentation also recorded results from the station's chemical monitoring equipment, including carbon monoxide readings of up to 7 parts per million and hydrogen chloride and hydrogen cyanide readings above 1 part per million. These measurements illustrate why the crew and controllers treated an unexplained smell as a possible air quality problem rather than assuming that it was harmless. AI-generated representative image showing an astronaut inspecting oxygen generation and air monitoring equipment inside a spacecraft. Credits - GeminiÂ How the station returned to normal The generator remained shut down while the crew and ground teams investigated the fault. NASA's Office of Inspector General later recorded that spare parts were delivered, the unit was repaired, and it was reactivated. The station's other oxygen sources meant that the loss of the Elektron did not immediately threaten the crew's breathing air.

title: Exam reforms: No contractual staff in exam depts
text: Mumbai: The state govt has directed all public universities to refrain from appointing contractual staff in sensitive examination departments as one of the prime measures to prevent paper leaks and other malpractices. The higher and technical education department has also asked universities to fix responsibilities for examination-related work on designated staff, to increase accountability and action in the event of irregularities. The govt has further decided to adopt the recommendations of the Nandan Nilekani-led central task force on examination reforms as soon as its report is released and implement them across all state-level competitive examinations, mainly the computer-based ones. Among other measures, the use of blockchain technology for the security of academically important certificates of students in the state to prevent forgery was also recommended. Directions have been given to formulate a policy for the same. The directives were issued in a meeting of higher and technical education minister Chandrakant Patil with the vice-chancellors of public universities last week. All universities should issue a notification fixing responsibilities regarding examinations on university officers or permanent employees, directed the minister in the meeting. âThe directive to not appoint contractual staff in examination departments also applies to affiliated colleges,â said an official from the department, citing the Mumbai University final-year BCom paper leak early this year. In the MU case, a temporary staffer, who was assigned examination duties, was found guilty of serious misconduct and was removed from service. The paper had leaked from the universityâs Centre for Distance and Online Education (CDOE). The CCTV footage showed the staff member clicking photographs of the question paper on his phone while the printing process was on. The official added that while the centre-in-charge was a permanent employee, the duties were assigned to a temporary staff member in the case. âNot only will such appointments be disallowed, the permanent employees will also be held responsible if there is a slip-up,â he added. The vice-chancellors have been asked to prepare a uniform statement of purpose (SOP) regarding examinations and also hold a one-day workshop for all examination controllers across universities. Speaking about the Nilekani report, the official added that the state will apply the report of the task force in totality. The task force for exam reforms has been contemplating creating a massive question bank and generating a question paper at the last minute using artificial intelligence (AI) as one of the measures to prevent a paper leak. Such a measure, if finalised, can be adopted in the state too, and is likely to be foolproof for computer-based tests in competitive examinations, said the official. title: Last-minute question papers, more exam centres: Nandan Nilekani's plan to prevent NEET paper leaks
text: Nandan Nilekani proposes AI-generated question papers and wider computer-based testing to tackle exam paper leaks NEW DELHI: Exam reforms task force head Nandan Nilekani on Tuesday suggested generating question papers at the last minute from a large question bank to reduce the risk of exam paper leaks. He also called for expanding computer-based testing across the country. "Question papers create an economic incentive for them to be sold. So, the way to solve this is to really have a massive bank of questions, and only at the last minute generate the question paper for that day, and therefore the question of 'a' question paper goes away, and there's no economic incentive for that. That's one way to think about how to solve this," he said speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum. Asked whether artificial intelligence (AI) could generate exam papers on the day of a test, Nilekani replied, "Yeah. Sure. Yeah," as quoted by news agency ANI. Nilekani also stressed the need to move towards computer-based testing (CBT) for all examinations. He said India already had 150,000 locations where students could take tests, but the network needed to be expanded. title: Jobs are growing in India, but where and what kind matters too
text: From Delhiâs streets to the coaching hubs of Patna and Pune, young Indians are protesting. From Delhiâs streets to the coaching hubs of Patna and Pune, young Indians are protesting. Their anger is about the cost of education, paper leaks, cancelled exams and delayed appointments. These have turned education, and the path from education to a job, into an endurance sport. But behind the anger lies a larger question. Where are the jobs that this generation has spent years preparing for? Indiaâs overall unemployment rate is low, at about 5%. However, among educated youth, it is not. Nearly two in five (39.3%) college-educated 15-24-year-olds in the labour force are unemployed. This is not a paradox. Those who cannot afford to wait take whatever work is available. Others wait for a job worth having. Low headline unemployment therefore masks a deeper deficit in the quality, security and productivity of the jobs on offer. Three patterns explain Indiaâs jobs conundrum: where employment is growing, what form it takes, and which skills are in demand. Where are jobs growing? The share of 15-59-year-olds in work rose from 47.1% in 2018-19 to 56% in 2024-25. Yet the move from farms to more productive non-farm work has stalled. Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) data shows that agricultureâs share of employment in this age group rose from 38% to 39%. Our latest report at Ashoka Universityâs Isaac Centre for Public Policy estimates that agriculture absorbed over 4 crore of the roughly 10.4 crore workers added between 2018-19 and 2025. Manufacturing has not offered an escape. Its share of employment has stayed at around 13-14%. Services added about 3.3 crore workers, manufacturing and related industries 1.6 crore, and construction 1.2 crore. India is trying to move out of farming without the factory floor that carried other Asian economies. In China, by contrast, agriculture employed about 22% of workers in 2023. Its transformation combined export-oriented manufacturing, infrastructure and private investment with the movement of rural workers into industry and services. India needs a similar, sustained expansion of productive work outside farming to meet its young peopleâs aspirations. What form do these jobs take? Leaving the farm does not guarantee a salary. Of the roughly 6.2 crore non-farm jobs added, 2.4 crore were in self-employment, and 1 crore were casual wage work. Fewer than half, about 2.9 crore, were salaried. Even a salary does not guarantee security. Many salaried jobs come without a written contract or social protection. According to ILO estimates, only about 16% of Indiaâs workers are formally employed, compared with about half in China and 40% in Indonesia. Self-employment is often held up as the answer to shortage of salaried jobs. Some of it is genuine enterprise. However, much of it is a small shop, a cart or a home-based business that barely covers its costs. In 2025, salaried workers earned on average about Rs 23,088 a month, while the non-farm self-employed earned about Rs 18,871. A large number of those counted as self-employed are, in effect, underemployed and underpaid. Finally, which skills are in demand? Among wage workers, employment grew fastest in low-skill jobs, with modest growth at the top and little in between. This matters because middle-skill jobs, such as technicians, supervisors and clerks, are how people have traditionally moved up the income ladder. At the top end, high-skill cognitive work is now the most exposed to AI, so even a professional career looks less certain than it did a few years ago. Put together, these trends explain the frustration on the streets. Families spend on education to buy their children a life less precarious than their own. If the private sector cannot offer that security, chasing a govt job is a rational choice. But many young people spend their best years preparing for a handful of govt posts. When selection does not come, they lose not just the job but the years too. A graduate who ends up in insecure, poorly paid work drops out of the unemployment figures, but the discontent stays. Paper leaks and postponed exams make it worse, because they suggest that even waiting in line is no guarantee of a fair chance. So, the question for policy is how India can move workers from low-productivity to high-productivity jobs and narrow the gap between what young people expect and what they get. The way out lies in private-sector job growth, through new firms and the expansion of small ones. For that, firms need predictable regulation, simpler compliance, easy entry and exit, timely approvals and payments, and reliable infrastructure. Labour-intensive sectors like garments, footwear and food processing need stable export markets, domestic demand and inputs at competitive prices. Healthcare, education, logistics and care work offer more room to grow. Schools and colleges, meanwhile, must teach skills that employers actually use rather than degrees on paper. In 1839, Thomas Carlyle, a Scottish historian and philosopher, wrote that âa man willing to work, and unable to find work, is perhaps the saddest sight that fortuneâs inequality exhibits under this sun.â India now faces a sadder sight: the young graduate who did everything asked of her and found the promise hollow. Indiaâs young people have spent years preparing for a better life. They deserve work that gives them a fair chance of building one. Disclaimer : Views expressed above are the author's own.

title: NTA new office under review: Higher Education Secretary checks security, infrastructure ahead of upcoming exams
text: Higher Education Secretary Deepti Gaur Mukherjee reviews the NTAâs new Minto Road office as the agency strengthens infrastructure, access controls and confidential examination safeguards ahead of upcoming tests. Higher Education Secretary Deepti Gaur Mukherjee on Saturday reviewed the infrastructure and administrative arrangements at the National Testing Agencyâs (NTA) newly relocated office in New Delhi, with the government focusing on strengthening examination-related operations ahead of upcoming tests. The review comes weeks after the NTA shifted its confidential and sensitive operations from its previous Okhla premises to a new government facility on Minto Road amid heightened scrutiny over examination security and the NEET-UG paper leak controversy. The Ministry of Education said Mukherjee interacted with senior NTA officials and inspected the operational facilities during her visit. The review was aimed at ensuring that the agency has the necessary infrastructure and administrative systems in place for the smooth conduct of forthcoming examinations. Higher Education Secretary reviews new NTA premises According to the Ministry of Education, Mukherjee carried out a comprehensive assessment of the new infrastructure and administrative setup during her visit. âSecretary, Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education, Smt. Deepti Gaur Mukherjee visited the new NTA office,â the ministry said in a post on X. It added that she interacted with senior officials, inspected operational facilities and reviewed the arrangements to ensure the seamless conduct of upcoming examinations. The visit assumes importance as the testing agency prepares to conduct several major national-level examinations, including tests such as JEE Main, NEET-UG, CUET and UGC-NET. NTA shifts operations from Okhla to Minto Road The NTA has moved its headquarters from Okhla to the Government of India Press Building on Minto Road in central New Delhi. The new facility has been allotted more than 55,000 square feet of space, covering the fifth floor and portions of the fourth and sixth floors of the building. The relocation was ordered after a review of the agency's examination systems and security arrangements. In August, Union Education Minister Pralhad Joshi directed the NTA to shift to the new premises and strengthen security infrastructure. The agency subsequently announced a broader restructuring of its examination operations. The NTA had earlier operated from its office in Okhla. Its shift to a government premises is part of the measures being undertaken to strengthen the handling of confidential examination material and tighten access to sensitive operations. CISF deployed at confidential areas Security arrangements at the new premises have also been strengthened. The Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) has deployed 39 personnel at the facility to regulate access to confidential areas and conduct security screening. According to officials cited by PTI, CISF personnel are stationed at entry and exit points and are responsible for access control, frisking and baggage screening. X-ray baggage screening machines and Door Frame Metal Detectors are also part of the security arrangements. Confidential areas have been separately demarcated, with movement and operations within these sections subject to tighter monitoring. The Centre has also been working on strengthened security protocols for the facility. Air-gapped systems, restricted access part of security overhaul The physical relocation is accompanied by tighter controls over digital and confidential operations. The new setup includes secluded rooms for sensitive work, air-gapped systems and mandatory device-deposit protocols intended to limit unauthorised access to examination-related information. The Centre has also said that standard operating procedures covering key NTA processes are being implemented across the examination cycle. Security arrangements for confidential operations have been consolidated as part of the agency's broader restructuring. The NTA has further strengthened its information-security structure, with the Centre stating that a dedicated Chief Information Security Officer has been designated and recruitment for additional information-security expertise is under way. NEET paper leak brought NTA's examination systems under scrutiny The latest security measures follow intense scrutiny of the NTA after the NEET-UG paper leak controversy. The issue triggered protests by students and raised questions over the agency's examination and confidentiality protocols. The CBI's investigation into the leak highlighted specific shortcomings in the handling of confidential material. According to the chargesheet, subject experts accused of being involved in the leak were not checked or frisked while entering or leaving the confidential section of the NTA's earlier office. The investigation also pointed to the absence of a dedicated control room for monitoring live CCTV feeds. The controversy subsequently prompted the government to initiate a wider examination-system overhaul. The Centre has been examining changes involving infrastructure, staffing, security protocols and the handling of question papers. NTA strengthens examination team and question-paper checks Alongside the office relocation, the NTA has begun restructuring its examination team. In August, the agency announced that around 600 experts associated with question-paper setting were being removed and that new experts would be brought into the system. The agency has also proposed a four-tier question-paper checking mechanism, while plans were announced to induct additional officials to strengthen its examination operations. The measures are being implemented as the NTA seeks to tighten its examination infrastructure and processes before the next round of major national-level tests. With the new premises now operational and additional physical and digital safeguards being put in place, Saturday's review by the Higher Education Secretary marks another step in the government's ongoing monitoring of the agency's preparedness for upcoming examinations. text: Chennai: The state selection committee began the first round of counselling for postgraduate medical students on Saturday. The committee conducts counselling for state-quota seats in govt colleges, self-financing medical colleges, and state private universities. At least 12,084 doctors applied for admission, which will be based on merit in NEET-PG 2026 and reservation . Tamil Nadu has 2,358 postgraduate seats in govt medical colleges. After sharing 1,115 seats for admission through the all-India quota, the state will open 1,243 seats for admission. title: Another ex-employee of defunct paper mill dies, toll up to 134
text: Cachar Paper Mill in Panchgram and Nagaon Paper Mill in Jagiroad were shut after the units entered a financial crisis Silchar: Another former employee of Cachar Paper Mill has died, taking the total number of deaths of employees and former employees of Assam âs two defunct Hindustan Paper Corporation mills to 134. Bhupendra Chandra Singh (64), a former Cachar Paper Mill employee, died of kidney failure at his home in Janaki Bazar, Hailakandi district, on Saturday, said Manobendra Chakraborty, president of the Cachar Paper Project Workersâ Union and the Joint Action Committee of Recognised Unions. Chakraborty said Singh actively participated in the workersâ strife for outstanding salaries and other dues. According to the union, 134 employees and former employees of Cachar Paper Mill in Panchgram and Nagaon Paper Mill in Jagiroad have died since the mills entered a financial crisis. The figure includes four suicides. Cachar Paper Mill stopped production in Oct 2015, while Nagaon Paper Mill shut in March 2017. Both were owned by Centre-run Hindustan Paper Corporation, which later went into liquidation. Chakraborty alleged that prolonged non-payment of salaries and statutory dues, including provident fund benefits, caused severe financial hardship and mental stress. He said workers were denied salaries and other entitlements for 113 months. Though the Assam govt announced a humanitarian assistance package after acquiring the millsâ assets through liquidation, workersâ organisations continue to demand settlement of dues and rehabilitation for affected families. Chakraborty held the Centre responsible and appealed for support for the workersâ demand for justice. title: A California homeowner found a hot-water pipe leaking beneath his kitchen in 2020; six years later, an appeals court questions State Farmâs denial of his claim
text: Image AI generated A California homeowner whose kitchen floor tiles turned unusually warm in June 2020 discovered a leaking hot-water pipe beneath his house, triggering an insurance dispute that has now been before an appeals court. Levon Nargizyan's claim was rejected by State Farm General Insurance Company, which argued that the water damage resulted from continuous or repeated leakage excluded under his policy. However, California's Second Appellate District has reversed a lower court ruling in the insurer's favour, finding that unanswered questions about how long the pipe had leaked and whether the insurer properly investigated the claim must be examined further. How the 2020 kitchen floor leak became an insurance dispute According to the court's judgment, Nargizyan discovered the problem on June 6, 2020, when he noticed that the tiles on his kitchen floor felt warmer than usual. After investigating, he found water dripping from the ceiling of the crawl space beneath his house. He described seeing water dripping from numerous places, with some drops falling faster than others, although he said it was "not pouring like a faucet". He contacted a plumber, who identified a damaged hot-water pipe in the crawl space. The plumber explained that water was spraying upwards from the pipe, soaking the insulation, wooden structures and flooring above it. The damaged section was removed and replaced, stopping the leak. Nargizyan subsequently contacted ServPro, a restoration company, on June 8 to begin cleaning and assessing the damage. He reported the water loss to State Farm on June 9. According to information provided to the insurer during its investigation, the crawl space contained approximately one and three-fourths inches of hot water, while the insulation, wooden joists and plywood subfloor had become saturated. Marble kitchen tiles were also discoloured, and the damage assessment indicated that sections of the kitchen flooring and the hardwood floor in the adjoining living room would need to be removed and replaced. Why State Farm questioned the homeownerâs water damage insurance claim Nargizyan's homeowners insurance policy covered accidental direct physical loss to the dwelling and personal property. However, it also contained an exclusion for certain types of water damage, including loss caused by "continuous or repeated seepage or leakage" from a plumbing system. The policy stated that the exclusion applied regardless of whether the event occurred suddenly or gradually and whether the damage was isolated or widespread. State Farm relied on this provision when assessing the homeowner's claim. During its initial investigation, State Farm received photographs and information from the restoration company and arranged an inspection of the property on June 24, 2020. Claim specialist John Foster observed that a pipe beneath the raised foundation had burst and sprayed water into the surrounding framework, where it was absorbed by the insulation. His inspection notes also referred to limescale buildup and black compression repair tape on the pipe. After reviewing a video supplied by Nargizyan, Foster described the water as spraying out at a rapid rate, estimating that it was releasing more than three cups per minute. Importantly, his notes stated that the incident did not appear to involve continuous or repeated leakage and that the policy provided coverage for the resulting damage. On June 30, another State Farm representative emailed Nargizyan stating that coverage appeared to have been extended for the necessary repairs and clean-up, although the investigation remained open and subject to a reservation of rights. Forensic engineering report identifies possible cause of the pipe leak State Farm subsequently commissioned an inspection of the damaged pipe by 4X Forensic Engineering Laboratories. The firm inspected the removed pipe on August 6, 2020, and issued its report on August 18. Engineer Bruce Agle concluded that the leak had originated from a pinhole perforation that was most likely caused by a screw or nail. The report suggested that the pipe initially experienced no leakage or only minor leakage, which increased as the screw or nail corroded. It also recorded that the pipe released water at a rate of 0.3 gallons per minute when tested at a water pressure of 65 pounds per square inch. On September 11, State Farm informed Nargizyan that it was rejecting his claim, attributing the damage to faulty workmanship and continuous or repeated leakage. The homeowner's public adjuster, William Musakhanyan, challenged the engineering findings, arguing that the inspection had not identified any screw, nail or other sharp object that could have punctured the pipe. He also questioned the report's stated water-release rate, pointing to a video of the inspection in which the engineer had reportedly referred to a rate of 2.3 gallons per minute. The adjuster further questioned the conclusion that the hole had been caused by a screw or nail, noting that the photographs did not show the expected signs of such a puncture. State Farm maintained its denial after reviewing the objections and sent a further denial letter on November 10, 2020. Homeowner disputes State Farmâs claim of long-term water leakage When Nargizyan challenged the insurance decision, one of the central issues became the duration of the leak. State Farm argued that the pinhole had developed gradually and that water had been escaping for a period before the homeowner noticed the warm kitchen tiles. The insurer relied on the engineering report and the extent of the damage to support its position that the incident fell within the policy exclusion. Nargizyan disputed that interpretation. He maintained that June 6 was the first time in the ten years since he had built the house that he had noticed a temperature change in the kitchen floor. He also argued that he had acted immediately after discovering the problem, contacting a plumber who repaired the pipe. His evidence included photographs and video showing water spraying from the damaged section, as well as the absence of pooled water, muddy soil and mould in the crawl space. His mechanical engineering expert, Richard Mumper, also questioned whether a screw or nail had caused the hole. Mumper identified a chemical reaction on the pipe's surface as another possible explanation, stating that the formation of a pinhole through chemical etching would not necessarily take a long time. He also criticised the forensic investigation for failing to establish how long the leak had existed. State Farm fails to establish how long the hot-water leak had existed The Los Angeles County Superior Court had previously granted State Farm's motion for summary judgment, finding that the insurer had established that the water damage resulted from continuous or repeated leakage. Although the trial court acknowledged that Nargizyan had challenged the engineering report, it concluded that his evidence did not sufficiently establish that State Farm had acted unreasonably in denying the claim. Nargizyan appealed that decision. The Second Appellate District disagreed with the decision to grant summary judgment. It explained that the insurer had to establish that the policy exclusion applied and that the evidence presented by Nargizyan raised a genuine factual dispute about the duration and nature of the leak. The court noted that the engineer who examined the pipe could not identify when the leak began, how long it had existed or the rate at which water had previously escaped. The court also distinguished the case from earlier insurance disputes in which evidence of months-long leakage, extensive mould or other signs of prolonged water damage had supported the application of similar exclusions. In Nargizyan's case, there was no comparable evidence establishing an estimated duration for the leak. Why the appeals court overturned the ruling in State Farmâs favour The judges concluded that a reasonable jury could find that the pipe had released water suddenly rather than leaking gradually over an extended period. The opinion stated that "a triable issue of material fact remains" regarding whether the leak lasted long enough to fall within the continuous or repeated leakage exclusion. Consequently, the court reversed the summary judgment ruling on the breach of contract claim. The appeals court also considered Nargizyan's claim that State Farm had breached the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing by failing to investigate the water damage adequately. State Farm argued that it had conducted a full investigation, consulted the homeowner, plumber, restoration company and public adjuster, and relied on an independent engineering report before making its decision. It maintained that a genuine dispute over coverage existed and that its decision was therefore not unreasonable. Why State Farmâs claims investigation and denial faced further legal scrutiny However, the appellate judges found that questions remained about whether the investigation had been sufficiently thorough and fair. They noted that the engineering report did not estimate the likely duration of the leak, despite the insurer relying on the continuous leakage exclusion. The court also considered the objections raised by Nargizyan's public adjuster and mechanical engineering expert concerning the proposed cause of the pinhole. The judges concluded that a reasonable jury could find that State Farm had failed to investigate the likely duration of the leak adequately and had ignored available evidence and alternative explanations before denying the claim. The court further found that factual disputes remained concerning Nargizyan's request for punitive damages. He argued that Donna Blazewich, the claims team manager overseeing the claim, had directed claim specialist Jennifer Gilman to deny coverage. Evidence presented during the proceedings indicated that Blazewich had supervisory authority over claim specialists and could direct whether claims should be covered, denied or settled. She had also testified about overseeing thousands of claims during her time as a team manager. The appeals court found that the evidence raised a triable issue about whether Blazewich qualified as a managing agent and had ratified the conduct in question. It therefore declined to dismiss the punitive damages claim at this stage. California homeowner wins appeal, but State Farm is not yet required to pay In its final disposition, the California Court of Appeal reversed the judgment in State Farm's favour and directed the superior court to vacate its order granting summary judgment and enter a new order denying the insurer's motion for summary judgment and its alternative motion for summary adjudication. The court also ruled that Nargizyan was entitled to recover his costs on appeal. The opinion was filed on April 15, 2026, and subsequently modified and certified for publication on May 14, 2026, without changing the appellate judgment. The ruling leaves the underlying insurance dispute open for further proceedings. It does not determine whether the leak was ultimately sudden or gradual, nor does it establish that State Farm must pay the claim. Instead, it establishes that the conflicting evidence and unresolved questions surrounding the investigation must be dismissed through summary judgment. You use AI every day. title: SP scores big win in Alld-Jhansi graduate MLC seat
text: Attachment Jhansi : Samajwadi Party âs Man Singh Yadav retained the Allahabad-Jhansi graduate constituency seat, defeating his nearest rival, Ashok Kumar Rathaur, by 27,663 votes and securing a 55% vote share. The final result was declared here on Wednesday afternoon by the divisional commissioner and returning officer Bimal Kumar Dubey after two days of hectic counting procedure. Out of total casted ballots 1,09,482, Yadav secured 60,358 votes, while Rathaur received 32,695 votes. Shivshankar Patel finished third with 3,949 votes. Other ten candidates could not even reach four-digit figures while 9596 votes were termed as invalid. Yadav has secured 55.13 percent of total casted ballots. Yadav, after receiving the winning certificate from the divisional commissioner proceeded for Prayagraj amidst tight security. Before leaving, he credited the win to the relentless efforts of the party workers and visionary leadership of SP national president Akhilesh Yadav . âPeople have voted on issues such as pendency of teachers recruitment, Shiksha Mitra, restore old pension scheme, paper leak, advocate protection law and issues of outsourced workers for which Akhilesh Yadav has promised that these issues will be taken up in priority once their govt is formedâ, Yadav said. In the previous election in 2020, Yadav had defeated BJP stalwart Yug Dutt Sharma by a margin of 4333 votes after the latterâs dominance over the seat for 24 long years. The constituency covers seven Bundelkhand districts along with Fatehpur, Kaushambi and Prayagraj. The overall voter turnout stood at 41.40%, while Jhansi recorded a higher turnout of 49.43%. title: 'Don't try to bulldoze another Constitutional Amendment Bill': Kharge writes to PM Modi
text: NEW DELHI: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Friday wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi over the delay in proroguing the Monsoon Session of Parliament, which ended in August, describing the situation as âunprecedentedâ. Urging PM Modi not to âbulldozeâ another âfar-reachingâ Constitutional Amendment Bill, Kharge reiterated his demand for an all-party meeting to discuss the governmentâs proposals in detail before they are finalised for consideration in Parliament. "It has already been 64 days since the Monsoon Session of Parliament was adjourned sine die on August 13 and both Houses of Parliament are yet to be prorogued. This scenario is unprecedented," Kharge said in his letter, which Congress MP Jairam Ramesh shared on X. Watch 14 Defects: Supreme Court Flags Rahul Gandhiâs Plea Against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, EC | INDIA Bloc The Rajya Sabha leader of opposition recalled writing to the prime minister on April 11, seeking an all-party meeting before the government introduced the Constitutional Amendment Bill on Delimitation, which subsequently failed to pass in the Lok Sabha. âYou may kindly recall that I had written to you on April 11 to convene an all-party meeting before bringing any Constitutional Amendment Bill on Delimitation. You did not do so. Thereafter, you made the bills public on the late evening of April 14 and convened a special session on April 16. The Constitutional Amendment Bill on Delimitation failed to muster the necessary two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha on April 17 by a decisive margin,â Kharge said. title: MPSC judicial panel to probe Drug Inspector paper leak, Rohit Pawar seeks wider inquiry
text: Rohit Pawar at the protest site with MPSC aspirants Pune: MPSC aspirants, led by NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar , have sought an expansion of the judicial inquiry into irregularities in Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) exams to include the PSI Divisional Limited Exam. They also demanded that engineering recruitment across key state departments be brought under the commission to ensure a uniform and transparent selection process. The aspirants submitted a representation to chief secretary Rajesh Agarwal on Friday, seeking action on multiple recruitment-related issues, including exam paper leaks, objections to recruitment results and delays in filling technical posts. The aspirants stated that the judicial inquiry commission set up to investigate MPSC exam irregularities should also probe the alleged paper leak in the Drug Inspector recruitment examination, along with nine other examinations. They also sought an update on the inquiry into objections raised by candidates over the results of the Maharashtra Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) Recruitment Exam 2026. A committee headed by Johnny Joseph has been constituted to examine the objections, and the candidates submitted a representation seeking details of its report and the ongoing special investigation team (SIT) investigation. In a separate demand, Pawar sought the inclusion of civil engineering posts in the public works, water resources, soil and water conservation departments and municipal councils under the MPSC recruitment process. He said, âSeparate departmental recruitment exercises were often affected by administrative delays, irregularities in exam arrangements and technical errors, leaving candidates facing uncertainty and govt departments struggling with vacancies. â Pawar added, âMany engineers in the state are consistently studying and working hard to secure opportunities in govt service. However, uncertainty and delays in the recruitment process are creating confusion about their future.â The candidates proposed to the commission that civil engineering assistants be included in the MPSC Group C combined exam and junior engineers (civil) in the Group B non-gazetted recruitment process. Pawar said, âBringing these posts under a common recruitment framework would make the process transparent, regular, faster and merit-based. The prolonged vacancies in technical posts could affect the implementation of govt development works. â He also urged the govt to stop filling regular posts in the land records department through contractual or outsourced appointments and instead recruit permanent staff through transparent, merit-based procedures. Pawar requested the chief secretary to consider the proposals positively and provide relief to aspirants preparing for govt recruitment exams. title: MPSC paper leak: Mumbai court rejects bail plea, says accused canât be treated as whistleblower
text: The case concerns the alleged leakage of questions for Maharashtra Public Service Commission examination for 154 posts of Drug Inspector, advertised on July 29, 2025 and conducted on March 22, 2026 Mumbai: A special court has rejected the bail plea of Gaurav Rajendra Patil (26) in the 2026 Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) drug inspector paper leak case, observing that he could not be treated as a whistleblower at this stage as he allegedly retained leaked questions for four months and discussed their possible sale. Special judge Shayana Patil said the investigation was still in progress and Gauravâs alleged role required further scrutiny. The court held that the material collected so far showed the case was ânot a matter of mere exchange of any expected question bank on WhatsAppâ, but part of a wider transaction to favour candidates for pecuniary benefit. The court also held that the alleged offence struck at the confidentiality and sanctity of competitive examinations. âIt has adversely affected the youth honestly contesting the public competitive examinations with dreams of securing good employment,â the judge said. Watch Paper Leak Law Passed, But Can Tougher Punishment Alone Stop India's Endless Exam Leak Crisis? The judge further stated that the offence adversely affected the public interest and eroded societyâs faith in institutions like MPSC. âIt is the offence of misuse and manipulation of the competitive exam-system at the hands of responsible persons/public servants inside the system with the help of private persons outside the system like the present accused,â the judge said. The case concerns alleged leakage of questions for MPSC examination for 154 drug inspector posts advertised on July 29, 2025, and conducted on March 22, 2026. According to the prosecution, Vishveshvar Nakate, an MPSC-appointed examination coordinator, allegedly stole 294 questions prepared by experts and handed them to Abhijeet Lendve, an under secretary, in MPSC buildingâs parking area. Lendve allegedly passed the question bank to Gopal Marathe, who gave it to Pravin Patil. The set allegedly reached candidate Rutuja Patil through her father and co-accused, and she forwarded it to Gaurav on WhatsApp two days before the examination. Gaurav emailed MPSC on July 21, alleging he had received 294 questions from a friend on March 20, and that about 78 appeared in the exam. He also alleged that Rutuja, who sent him the question set, ranked seventh in the merit list. The court noted that Patil later withdrew the complaint, saying no paper had been leaked and that his earlier allegation was made âfor sake of mischief or funâ. The judge said the contradictory stand was prima facie indicative of lack of veracity and sincerity. Patil argued that he was the original complainant and a whistleblower. He claimed he was only a passive recipient of WhatsApp messages, and was neither a candidate nor a beneficiary and had no role in any conspiracy. The prosecution opposed the bail, citing chats containing phrases such as âPaper bhetlaâ, â80 questions fix yetilâ, âPaper devu ka tulaâ, âViral kuthe karu nakoâ and âViku ka miâ â(Got the paper. 80 questions are guaranteed to come. Should I give you the paper? Donât make it viral anywhere. Shall I sell it?â The court said the exchanges indicated possible misuse. It said Patil waited four months to complain and could be treated as a whistle-blower only if he had immediately reported receipt without discussing circulation or sale. title: NTA holds four-day 'Chintan Shivir' to strengthen exam systems, candidate experience
text: NTA holds four-day 'Chintan Shivir' to strengthen exam systems, candidate experience The National Testing Agency ( NTA ) has concluded a four-day Chintan Shivir at its new premises on Minto Road, with discussions focused on how the agency conducts examinations, strengthens its systems and rebuilds trust among candidates. The exercise comes at a crucial point for the testing agency, which has faced scrutiny over alleged irregularities in major examinations, including the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET) UG. The controversy had triggered nationwide protests and led to the resignation of former Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan . The Chintan Shivir brought NTA teams together to review its examination processes and discuss what needs to change as the agency looks to build what it described as a âNew NTAâ. Integrity, inclusion and innovation at the centre The discussions were built around three priorities: integrity, inclusion and innovation. According to the NTA, teams examined how examinations are conducted, where existing systems can be strengthened and how the experience of candidates can be improved. Technology and improved processes were also discussed as tools to strengthen examination systems and build greater trust. âHow are exams conducted? How can systems be strengthened? How can technology and better processes build trust?â were among the questions considered during the four-day exercise. The agency said the discussions were open and the questions were candid, with teams focusing on practical ways to improve its functioning. NTA looks to strengthen examination systems The Chintan Shivir is part of a broader effort to review how the NTA operates after a period of intense scrutiny. The agency has recently shifted its operations to a new office on Minto Road. The Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) has also been deployed at the premises, including to secure confidential areas and strengthen arrangements around sensitive examination-related work. Against this backdrop, the discussions at the Chintan Shivir focused not only on individual examination processes but also on the systems supporting them. The NTA said the exercise was not limited to reviewing its current position. It was intended to define the direction in which the agency wants to move. Focus on candidate experience and trust Candidate experience emerged as another key area of discussion. For an examination agency handling some of the country's largest entrance and eligibility tests, the process extends beyond conducting an examination. The systems around registration, examination centres, technology, communication and grievance handling also shape how candidates experience the process. The NTA said the discussions examined how these areas could be improved and how stronger processes could help restore confidence in the examination system. The agency described the Chintan Shivir as an important step towards building a new NTA that is âstronger in its systems, transparent in its processes, responsive to candidates, and trusted by students and families across the country.â Get the latest Education News and Live updates. title: No leak alarms at Saraca Labs, Telangana PCB orders closure after two deaths
text: No leak alarms at Saraca Labs, Telangana PCB orders closure after two deaths Hyderabad : Saraca Laboratories lacked chloroform leak-detection alarm sensors and equipment to arrest vapour emissions, the Telangana Pollution Control Board found while ordering closure of its Sangareddy unit after a leak killed two people, identified in reports as workers from Andhra Pradesh. The Oct 23, 2026, order directed the bulk-drug and intermediates manufacturer at Gaddapotharam village, Jinnaram mandal, to stop industrial activities immediately. TGPCB also ordered power disconnection, citing safety failures, consent violations and risks to public health and the environment. Leak during layer separation According to the boardâs order, chloroform vapours escaped around 11.30 pm on Oct 22 in Production Block No. 2 during layer separation from a first-floor reactor to a ground receiver. General manager Madhu and deputy general manager Yogeshwar Rao told inspectors that vapours rapidly accumulated and spread. Around 1,750 litres of chloroform separation layer were reportedly in the reactor; the order does not establish how much leaked. Two people became unconscious and were declared dead at Narayana Hospital. Patancheru DSP Prabhakar informed the TGPCBâs RC Puram office. Police identified the deceased as Sudarshan Rao, 27, and Balaji, 44, both from Andhra Pradesh. Police have been investigating the cause and the safety arrangements. Broken vent, missing equipment Inspectors found the scrubberâs HDPE vent line and valve broken and fallen, spillages near the duct and a lingering chloroform smell. VOC readings reached 20 ppm at the incident point and 0.1 ppm outside the block. These were not identified as chloroform-specific concentrations. Besides missing leak alarms, the unit lacked a sub-cooler condenser followed by an activated charcoal bed, despite having a double-stage scrubber. TGPCB ordered closure without a hearing. Previously, the unitâs consent for operation (CFO) had been auto-renewed in Mar 2026 until Mar 31, 2031. Previous directions The order records complaint-related and non-compliance directions between 2020 and Aug 2026. It also cites requests to the collector for an inquiry into buffalo deaths in previous incidents to assess compensation payable by industries. Closure compliance was sought within 24 hours and power-disconnection compliance within 48 hours. No implementation report accompanies the orders. Continued operation, including through generators, would attract prosecution. Wastewater and debris disposal directions refer to a âfire accidentâ, although the incident narrative establishes only a leak. Police said six additional workers became seriously ill, and the Telangana Human Rights Commission sought the collectorâs report by Nov 26. title: 'Taking down Instagram accounts won't make questions disappear': Abhijeet Dipke accuses Centre of digital crackdown
text: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke NEW DELHI : Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Wednesday criticised the Centre over an alleged crackdown on anti-government posts and accounts on Instagram. He warned that silencing citizens by taking down content would not address the public grievances. On Wednsday, in a post on X, Dipke wrote, âThe Instagram crackdown is not going to work! âThe government is taking down thousands of posts and accounts every day, but it seems to be missing a fundamental point. âInstagram is just a platform where people are raising their questions. The reasons behind those questions exist far beyond social media, and taking down accounts won't make them disappear,â Dipke wrote, warning that the alleged censorship could further erode trust among the very people the government is supposed to answer to. His remarks come amid wider scrutiny of online content restrictions and freedom of expression. Activists and political groups have raised concerns over account suspensions and takedown directives, including those reportedly issued under Section 69A of the Information Technology Act. According to PTI, social media platforms including Meta and X have been asked by the Centre to restrict posts and handles raising questions on youth unemployment, governance, and public infrastructure. Critics argue that restricting online content does not address underlying concerns over unemployment, examination paper leaks, governance and public infrastructure. The issue has also reached the courts. On October 27, the Delhi High Court issued notice to the Centre and the concerned department on a petition challenging the withholding of the Instagram handle @bring_back__ballot in India. The account is associated with the âBring Back Ballotâ initiative of Mission Save Constitution and advocate Mehmood Pracha, its national convenor. The petition stated that the handle was withheld on October 10, the day organisers held a protest at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi. It displayed the message: âAccount not available in India. title: NEET-UG to shift online? Centre works on nationwide CBT infrastructure strategy
text: NEET-UG may shift online as Centre develops nationwide CBT infrastructure strategy NEW DELHI: The ministry of education is developing a nationwide Computer-Based Testing (CBT) infrastructure strategy to enable the transition of NEET from its current pen-and-paper format to an online examination, officials said. While NEET has so far been conducted in pen-and-paper mode, the National Testing Agency (NTA) conducts several other examinations, including JEE-Main, Common University Entrance Test (CUET)-UG and PG, UGC-NET and CSIR UGC-NET, in computer-based mode. Once the infrastructure strategy is in place, the plan is to shift all entrance examinations to the online mode. "A national examination-grade Computer-Based Testing infrastructure strategy is being formulated to close the geographic gap in test-centre availability, standardise centre-level examination-grade specifications and to permit the migration to CBT from the pen-and-paper mode examinations. The strategy is under active consideration based on a multi-model sourcing architecture," a senior Ministry of Education official was quoted as saying by PTI. The move comes amid an ongoing overhaul of the National Testing Agency (NTA), the nodal autonomous body responsible for conducting NEET-UG and other entrance examinations for higher educational institutions. "The possible migration of NEET (UG) from the pen-and-paper mode to CBT, including the design of the transition, the sequencing, the infrastructure prerequisites, and the equity implications for rural, women and low-connectivity-district candidates, is being worked upon. However, the recommendations of the High-Level Task Force on exam reforms in structured consultation and concurrence of the Health Ministry and National Medical Commission, are awaited," the official said. Following the NEET paper leak earlier this year, the Centre announced that the medical entrance examination would be conducted in Computer-Based Test (CBT) mode from next year. Officials aware of the development said the plan is under active consideration, but a final decision will be taken only after the report of the Nandan Nilekani-led task force set up to overhaul Indiaâs public examination system is received. The leak of the NEET-UG medical entrance examination paper earlier this year triggered nationwide student protests and led to the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan. A day after Pradhanâs resignation, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the formation of a high-powered task force headed by Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani to recommend reforms aimed at making the examination system leakproof. title: Akhilesh calls BJP MLC poll performance a âflop showâ, says results signal political shift
text: Lucknow: Samajwadi Party (SP) president and former Uttar Pradesh chief minister Akhilesh Yadav on Friday claimed that the BJP âs losses in five seats in the recently concluded Legislative Council elections reflected a much larger political setback, alleging that the ruling party had lost ground in nearly 50 districts and cities across the state. Addressing a conference at the Samajwadi Party headquarters after meeting newly elected MLCs and party candidates, Akhilesh described the election outcome as the beginning of a political shift in Uttar Pradesh. He termed the BJPâs performance a âflop showâ and accused the ruling party of relying on state machinery, money power and administrative influence to secure victories. âThe BJP has money power, but the Samajwadi Party has people power. Had the BJP govt not resorted to manipulation, it would never have won those six seats,â Akhilesh said. He alleged that attempts were made throughout the night to influence the counting process, forcing party workers and supporters to defend the electoral mandate. Taking a swipe at the BJPâs celebrations, Akhilesh said those who had prepared to celebrate victories after the results were declared had instead faced disappointment. He also claimed that chief minister Yogi Adityanath âs involvement in the Gorakhpur contest had adversely affected the BJPâs prospects. The SP chief said the results had disrupted the BJPâs political calculations and underlined the growing influence of the partyâs PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) social coalition. Highlighting the partyâs electoral gains, he cited the victories of Sanjay Nishad, Akash Agrawal, Kanti Singh, Ashutosh Sinha, Lal Bihari Yadav and Dr Man Singh Yadav, saying support for the SP was expanding among traders, women and the Kayastha community. Akhilesh described Akash Agrawalâs victory from the Agra teachersâ constituency as a special achievement and said voters in Varanasi had delivered a setback to the BJPâs âdouble-engineâ govt. He, however, alleged that SP candidate Sanjay Tripathi failed to win in Gorakhpur due to irregularities in the election process. Akhilesh targets BJP over education policies Riding on victories in key teachersâ and graduatesâ MLC constituencies, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Friday termed the results a verdict against the BJP govtâs âanti-educationâ policies, alleging that it shut 26,000 primary schools while opening 27,000 liquor shops. He credited teachers, graduates and women voters, especially female teachers, for the outcome. He alleged large-scale attempts to influence the elections, irregularities in voter rolls, and the deletion of voters through fraudulent applications. He also accused the govt of facilitating repeated examination paper leaks, reducing teaching jobs, denying over 11,000 reserved recruitment posts, and failing to act against the vandalism of 151 Ambedkar statues. The SP chief renewed his demand for ballot-paper voting, questioned data collection practices, attacked the BJP over farmers and infrastructure, and predicted a bigger setback for the ruling party in the 2027 Assembly polls. title: Trumpâs DHS hit by data breach as hackers expose records of 41,000 employees
text: The officers have faced scrutiny for wearing masks and sunglasses during operations and for failing to clearly identify themselves. More than 41,000 employees and contractors of the US department of homeland security (DHS), including thousands of immigration and border enforcement personnel, have had their work details exposed in a major data leak amid growing protests and criticism over President Donald Trumpâs immigration crackdown. The officers have faced scrutiny for wearing masks and sunglasses during operations and for failing to clearly identify themselves. The leaked information includes names, work addresses, phone numbers and job descriptions of personnel working across several agencies, including Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Customs and Border Protection (CBP), a BBC report reveals. The leaked records were published in a searchable online database called âIcepickâ on Wednesday. The activist group department of peace said it accessed the information through a single sign-on service used by DHS employees, while cybersecurity researcher Maia Arson Crimew and the nonprofit Distributed Denial of Secrets helped make the data public.
