title: Bandai Namco data breach: Over 300,000 users affected by third-party leak
text: Bandai Namco data breach affects over 300,000 users (Image via Bandai Namco) Bandai Namco, the publisher behind Tekken and a long list of other popular games, has confirmed a data breach that exposed customer information. The company wasn't hacked directly, and the problem came from a third-party email service provider called YmirLink. YmirLink's systems were compromised in a much larger leak, resulting in Bandai Namco's details also being leaked. In the section below, we take a detailed look at the Bandai Namco data breach. Bandai Namco data breach details Bandai Namco says the breach exposed the data of roughly 346,000 members of The GUNDAM base, its Gundam-focused membership service. The company announced the incident on October 28, 2026. The notice has since been taken down from its site. The root cause lies with YmirLink, which handles email distribution for multiple organizations. Bandai Namco is one of several customers affected, so the incident is an example of supply-chain risk: a breach at a vendor spreads to every company relying on it. What data was exposed The exposure is limited, which is the good news. According to Bandai Namco, the leaked information includes only: Email addresses Internal Bandai Namco ID numbers The company says the following were not leaked: Passwords Credit card details Names Addresses Purchase history This sets the incident apart from Sony's recent So-net and plala breach, where names, phone numbers, and some bank account records were exposed. The larger YmirLink leak The Bandai Namco numbers are a small piece of a much bigger problem. Japanese broadcaster NHK reports that YmirLink first disclosed about 9 million leaked records on October 19. Further investigation raised the total to more than 51.62 million records. The data is mostly email addresses, and it affects other organizations that use YmirLink. Japanese railway operators JR Central, JR West, and JR Kyushu have also reported possible leaks. Bandai Namco's response The company has taken several steps: Suspended the affected email distribution service Reported the breach to Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission Begun investigating alongside YmirLink to determine the full impact Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines Bandai Namco says it hasn't confirmed any secondary damage, such as misuse of personal information, as of its announcement. Even without passwords or payment details, exposed email addresses carry risk. Attackers can use them for phishing or impersonation, particularly if they can pair the address with an internal ID that looks official. Bandai Namco has warned affected users to be careful with suspicious messages. It added that any emails it sends about the incident will not contain URLs in the body, so a message about this breach that includes a link should be treated as a red flag. What users should do Don't click links in unexpected emails claiming to come from Bandai Namco or The GUNDAM base. Check the sender address closely before opening anything. If you reuse a password across accounts, change it as a precaution, although passwords weren't part of this leak. Consider using a unique email alias for gaming accounts. The investigation is ongoing, so the count could still change. The breach also follows Capcom's disclosure last week and Sony's earlier this week, which makes for a rough stretch for the gaming industry's data security. For now, the practical advice is simple: stay alert and don't trust links in unsolicited emails. Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

title: NEET PG 2026: NBEMS revises first-year course fee rules for candidates seeking seat upgradation, check complete details here
text: NBEMS has allowed NEET PG 2026 candidates opting for seat upgradation to defer first-year course fee payment until final allotment. Round 1 reporting and joining began on October 26 and will continue until November 2. The National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS) has revised the first-year course fee payment rules for candidates allotted postgraduate medical seats through NEET PG 2026 counselling. Under the revised procedure, candidates opting for seat upgradation in subsequent counselling rounds will not have to pay the first-year course fee while awaiting their upgraded allotment. The change comes as reporting and joining for Round 1 begin on October 26, 2026. The Medical Counselling Committee (MCC) has published the Round 1 final allotment result for the admission session. Under the revised rules, candidates who choose to retain their allotted seats must pay the first-year course fee directly to the NBEMS-accredited hospital where they secure admission. They are no longer required to deposit the fee into NBEMS accounts during counselling. NEET PG 2026 counselling: What has changed in the fee payment rules? The revised NBEMS advisory distinguishes between candidates who want to retain their allotted seats and those who wish to participate in subsequent rounds for a possible upgrade. Candidates who select the âfreezeâ option to retain their allotted seats must pay the first-year annual course fee directly to the allotted NBEMS-accredited hospital. They must also complete the reporting and joining formalities within the prescribed deadline. Candidates who select the âfloatâ option to remain eligible for upgradation in subsequent counselling rounds will not have to pay the first-year course fee while waiting for the outcome. If their seats are upgraded, they must pay the applicable fee directly to the institute they finally choose to join after freezing the upgraded allotment. The revised procedure allows candidates seeking upgradation to defer the first-year course fee payment until their final seat is decided. However, it does not exempt them from the counselling rules or the applicable reporting and joining requirements. NEET PG 2026: Round 1 reporting begins today Candidates allotted seats in Round 1 must complete their reporting and joining formalities between October 26 and November 2, 2026, according to the published MCC counselling schedule. Candidates who intend to retain their allotted seats must report to the respective institutions within this period. Those opting for upgradation should carefully follow the applicable counselling instructions and ensure they meet all prescribed requirements. NBEMS has clarified that the revised fee procedure does not extend the reporting or joining deadline. Candidates must adhere to the schedule issued by MCC and monitor the official counselling website for any changes. NEET PG 2026 counselling schedule: Important dates The published MCC schedule lists the following dates for the upcoming counselling rounds. Counselling event Date Round 1 reporting and joining October 26 to November 2, 2026 Round 2 result November 14, 2026 Round 2 reporting and joining November 16 to 23, 2026 Round 3 result December 4, 2026 Round 3 reporting and joining December 5 to 12, 2026 Online stray vacancy round result December 24, 2026 Stray vacancy round reporting December 24 to 31, 2026 Candidates should refer to the official MCC PG counselling website for the latest schedule and any subsequent revisions. What happens if a candidate's seat is upgraded? The training commencement date will depend on the seat a candidate ultimately joins. If a candidate receives an upgraded seat in a subsequent counselling round, the training period will be counted from the date of reporting and joining at the upgraded seat. If the candidate does not receive an upgrade, they must join the seat already allotted to them within the prescribed reporting window. In such cases, the training period will be counted from the date of joining that seat. Candidates should therefore consider their counselling options carefully and ensure that their decisions are consistent with the applicable MCC rules. NBEMS registration portal to remain inactive until counselling ends NBEMS has also clarified that its Online Portal for Joining and Registration (OPJR) will remain inactive until all rounds of NEET PG 2026 counselling conducted by MCC have been completed. The portal will be activated subsequently to allow candidates and hospitals to submit joining details and the required documents to NBEMS. The board will issue a separate notice explaining the submission procedure. Candidates must distinguish between reporting to their allotted institutions within the prescribed counselling window and submitting joining-related documents through the OPJR portal at a later stage. The revised fee rules provide relief to candidates waiting for a possible seat upgrade by removing the requirement to pay the first-year course fee in advance. However, candidates must continue to follow the prescribed counselling schedule, reporting requirements and admission procedures. Candidates are advised to check the official NBEMS and MCC websites regularly for further instructions regarding NEET PG 2026 counselling and admission formalities. title: Congress cites 'sting operation', says Prayagraj students sell blood to fund education, hostel costs
text: The party asserted that it would never forgive the BJP for this "sin". (AI Image) NEW DELHI: The Congress on Wednesday cited a "sting operation" to allege that students facing financial hardship in Uttar Pradesh's Prayagraj are being forced to sell their blood to meet the expenses of their education and hostel accommodation. The party said it would never forgive the BJP for this "sin". Congress's Uttar Pradesh in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam said a Hindi daily had conducted a sting operation at the blood bank of the Allahabad Medical Association. "The sting has revealedâ the area around the Allahabad Medical Association Blood Bank is a hub of coaching centres. Here, a very large number of students are selling their blood to continue their studies. There can be nothing more shameful than this," Gautam said at a press conference here along with party colleague Abhay Dubey. Questioning the government's ability to support students, he asked what purpose a government served if it could not ensure education for children or provide them with hostel accommodation. Citing the sting operation, Gautam alleged that brokers operated at the Allahabad Medical Association blood bank and targeted students in financial distress. "These brokers know which students living in hostels are financially strained and which ones are in need of money. These brokers arrange fake documentation for the students and then their blood is sold. The desperate students do all this just to continue their studies and pay the hostel fees," he claimed. Gautam further claimed that the sting operation had revealed that some students were selling blood up to four times a month and receiving Rs 4,000-5,000 for one unit. The Congress leader also claimed that 132 students die by suicide in Uttar Pradesh every month, while 14,488 students died by suicide across the country in 2024. title: In AYUSH admission âgoof-upâ, students in Maharashtra allotted two seats, denied college upgrade
text: Maharashtra medical admissions: students get duplicate seat allotments (AI image) MUMBAI: At a time when thousands of NEET aspirants are struggling to secure one medical seat, Deepali Raut* (name changed) has landed two. Both at the same homeopathy medical college in Chinchwad. She is not alone. Several AYUSH aspirants across Maharashtra have been allotted two seats, either in the same college or different institutions, following what appears to be a botched admission exercise that has left some students spoilt for choice and others deprived of a chance to upgrade to better colleges. A senior official of state CET Cell acknowledged the problem, but said little could be done at this stage, given the deadline for completing admissions. The anomalies surfaced in the third merit list released on Oct 30. Under admission rules, candidates allotted seats through the 15% quota administered by the AYUSH Admissions Central Counselling Committee (AACCC) cannot simultaneously claim seats under the 85% state quota. But an Oct 26 order from AACCC changed the equation. Candidates who had failed to secure an upgrade between rounds one and three were permitted to surrender their seats, exit central counselling and participate in the state admission process. The order came too late for the state to accommodate the cancellations before finalising its allotments. The result: candidates appearing on both lists, with some securing two seats. Parent representative and admission counsellor Kailash Tosniwal said the last-minute decision had created confusion and placed candidates in a financial bind. Those who surrender seats allotted through the central quota in private colleges risk forfeiting substantial security deposits. Reserved-category students who give up their state quota seats, meanwhile, could lose the benefit of govt fee concessions at the start of the academic year. But the bigger casualty may be students who were waiting for an upgrade. Candidates holding two allotments must surrender one seat. These seats will now become available in the fourth round, from which students already allotted seats in the first three state counselling rounds are excluded. This creates a peculiar situation: candidates with lower NEET scores who remained unallotted could secure better colleges in the fourth round, while higher-scoring students who accepted seats earlier will have no opportunity to compete for them. Had the admissions been processed in accordance with the original rules, these seats could have been available for upgrades in the third round itself, Tosniwal said, blaming AACCC for the last-minute change. For students who have played by the rules, the consequences may be difficult to accept. Some have two seats to choose from. Others have lost their chance at a better one, said Tosniwal. title: COD parcel you never ordered? Watch out! It could be a scam
text: Unexpected cash-on-delivery parcels are being sent to shoppers using their personal information without their consent (AI image) A new form of online fraud is targeting shoppers through unsolicited cash-on-delivery parcels. The packages carry the recipientâs name, phone number and address, and often appear to come with familiar e-commerce labels. Victims usually pay because the parcel looks genuine. But when they open it, they find scrap clothing, paper, low-value items or products they may have only browsed online but never ordered. Since there is no matching order in their shopping account, getting a refund becomes difficult. TOIâs Lipi Joshi explains how the scam happens and what you can do to protect yourself. What is the scam? The scam involves sending fake cash-on-delivery (COD) parcels using peopleâs genuine personal details. Packages may carry the recipientâs full name, mobile number, address and an e-commerce-style shipping label. The COD amount typically ranges from Rs 500 to Rs 5,000. Since many households regularly shop online, family members may assume an unexpected parcel is genuine and pay the delivery agent. On opening it, they may find scrap clothing, paper or an unrelated item. How does the scam work? Fraudsters use leaked customer information to generate fake shipping labels and dispatch bogus COD parcels in bulk. They upload names, phone numbers and addresses to digital shipping platforms, print labels and send packages through regular delivery networks. The delivery agent collects the cash without necessarily verifying whether the recipient placed an order. Victims often discover the fraud only after opening the parcel and finding that no corresponding order exists in their shopping account. Why do people fall for it? The parcels appear genuine because they carry accurate personal details. In households where several people shop online or accept deliveries for one another, recipients may assume that someone in the family placed the order. How do scammers obtain personal details? Experts say personal information can leak through routine delivery and service systems, not just sophisticated cyberattacks. Software engineer Piyush Surolia, who has worked with third-party delivery services such as Shiprocket and Blue Dart, said shipping labels carry recipientsâ names, phone numbers and addresses. Rogue workers at warehouses, shipping centres or local courier contractors could photograph or scan these labels to collect information in bulk. âYou donât need a high-tech bank hack to lose your personal information; it usually leaks right from everyday package shipping,â Surolia said. How are fake COD parcels sent in bulk? According to Surolia, fraudsters exploit the ease of creating bulk shipments through digital shipping services. They can upload spreadsheets containing stolen addresses and generate thousands of shipping labels. âThe delivery worker showing up at your door has no way to check if you actually ordered the item on an app like Amazon or Meesho. They are simply paid to collect cash for the printed label,â he said. Are shopping apps the only source of leaked data? No. Personal information may also be exposed through food delivery apps, medical diagnostic laboratories, utility bills, online loan applications, shipping labels and discarded packaging. Private cybercrime investigator Dinesh Jain said data brokers compile such information into spreadsheets and sell it through encrypted messaging platforms such as Telegram or online black markets. While some buyers may use the information for advertising, scammers can also exploit it. Why are refunds difficult? Since the fake parcel does not appear in the victimâs shopping account, there may be no order record against which to raise a return request or refund claim. Victims can struggle to establish that the transaction was linked to an e-commerce platform, particularly after paying the delivery agent in cash. Who is most vulnerable? Frequent online shoppers, people who regularly use COD, families that accept parcels on one anotherâs behalf, and households where elderly parents or domestic staff receive deliveries may be particularly vulnerable. What should you do before paying? Check your shopping app to verify whether the order appears in your account. Contact the named recipient and confirm that the parcel was expected before handing over any money. Treat unexpected COD deliveries with caution. Instruct family members, elderly parents, domestic staff and neighbours not to pay for parcels without confirmation. The simplest precaution is to follow one rule: never pay for a COD parcel unless someone in the household confirms the order. How can you reduce your exposure to data leaks? Jain advised consumers to be cautious about the personal information they share online. Review saved addresses on shopping and delivery apps and remove those that are no longer needed. Avoid sharing unnecessary personal details and exercise caution when submitting phone numbers and addresses to online services. Consumers should also remove or destroy shipping labels containing personal information before discarding delivery boxes and packaging. title: In 2023, golfer Sergio Garcia and his wife Angela turned an Austin golf-and-gala event into $2 million for childrenâs causes, including a childrenâs hospital and foster care
text: Professional golfer Sergio Garcia | Wikimedia Commons Professional golfer Sergio Garcia and his wife, Angela, raised $2 million through the first FORE Kids ATX fundraiser in Austin, Texas, in March 2023. The two-day event combined a golf tournament, a charity gala and appearances by professional golfers and entertainers, with proceeds supporting organisations working in childrenâs healthcare, foster care and youth golf programmes. The fundraiser brought together golfers including Dustin Johnson, Bryson DeChambeau and Brooks Koepka. LIV Golf analyst David Feherty hosted the gala, while country singer Chris Lane performed. FORE Kids ATX reported the $2 million total in its account of the event, Four organisations shared the eventâs focus The inaugural fundraiser partnered with Dell Childrenâs Medical Center, Foster Village and The Muny Conservancyâs Austin Golf Academy, and the Garciasâ own UGLI Foundation was also among the organisations that were supported by their broader charitable work. Dell Childrenâs Medical Center provides specialised paediatric healthcare in Central Texas, and Foster Village supports children and families involved in the foster care system, while the Austin Golf Academy works to expand access to golf and youth programming. The UGLI Foundation, founded by Angela Garcia, focuses on bullying prevention and promoting respect for people who may be treated differently because of their appearance or identity. The eventâs mix of beneficiaries meant that the proceeds were not restricted to a single medical cause; instead, the fundraiser supported programmes spanning healthcare, family services, youth development and anti-bullying work. The University of Texas alumni publication The Alcalde reported that the Garcias returned with a second annual FORE Kids ATX fundraiser in 2023, and that the two-day event included a golf tournament featuring 120 professional golfers and raised money for Dell Childrenâs Medical Center, Foster Village, The Muny Conservancy and the UGLI Foundation. Golf provided the centrepiece FORE Kids ATX was built around a multi-day format rather than a single dinner or auction, and golf gave professional players and other guests a way to participate directly, while the evening gala brought donors and supporters together away from the course. Garcia, a Masters champion, has a long record of charitable work through golf, and his foundation, established in 2002, has supported children and young people through social assistance and sports programmes. The Sergio and Angela Garcia Foundation also backs initiatives in the Austin area, where the couple lives, and the coupleâs official foundation website identifies Dell Childrenâs Medical Center, Foster Village, the Austin youth golf programme and the UGLI Foundation as beneficiaries of FORE Kids ATX. It also describes the event as part of their wider work supporting children and families. Garcia, a Masters champion, has a long record of charitable work through golf | Wikimedia Commons A recurring fundraiser in Austin The 2023 event was the first FORE Kids ATX fundraiser hosted by Sergio and Angela Garcia, and its $2 million result gave the organisers a substantial fundraising base for their work with local organisations. The event also relied on the involvement of professional golfers and public figures, whose participation helped attract attention and donors. FORE Kids ATX has since continued to develop as a multi-day fundraiser, with golf, a gala and additional activities built around its charitable partners. The original $2 million figure refers to the 2023 event, not the coupleâs total lifetime charitable giving, and their broader foundation work extends beyond FORE Kids ATX and includes other programmes and partnerships. title: Few takers for physical science, commerce; 46% UG seats vacant
text: Students during UG admissions Bhubaneswar : Even as the state govt added over 10,000 more undergraduate (UG) seats across major streams this year, it is now struggling to fill up over 79,000 seats after the second phase of admissions for the 2026-27 academic session. The UG classes have already commenced in July-end. According to the higher education department's Student Academic Management System data, 79,113 seats across seven streams have remained vacant after the second phase of admissions this month, with physical science and commerce having the highest proportion. There are seven streams in UG â self-financing courses, Sanskrit, law, arts, physical science, biological science and commerce â with a combined seat strength of 2,88,128 in 1,058 colleges. Phase II was conducted after three admission rounds under Phase I. Of the 79,113 vacant seats, 72,717 were in arts, physical science, biological science and commerce. The remaining 6,396 vacancies were in self-financing courses, Sanskrit and law. Arts accounted for the largest number of vacancies, although its vacancy rate was lower than that of science and commerce. Of the 1,66,196 arts seats available, 1,38,919 had been filled, leaving 16.4% of them vacant. Physical science, meanwhile, has the highest number of vacant seats, with 21,590 of the 46,197 remaining unfilled. Admissions stood at 24,607, leaving 46.7% of the total capacity vacant. Commerce recorded a similar trend. Of the 32,085 seats available, 17,181 had been filled, leaving 14,904 vacant. The vacancy rate stood at 46.5%. Biological science has 8,946 vacant seats against a total of 28,992. With 20,046 admissions, 30.9% of the seats are vacant. This is not the first academic year in which such a huge number of seats have remained vacant. While around 88,000 seats went vacant at UG level in 2024-25, 80,000 seats found no takers in 2025-26. Education expert R N Panda said students today are increasingly looking beyond conventional degree programmes towards technical and professional courses that offer specialised skills and clearer career pathways. âSubjects such as computer science, data analytics, healthcare, management and emerging technologies are attracting interest because students want their education to translate into employment opportunities. While traditional courses continue to have academic value, colleges may need to rethink their course offerings and strengthen industry linkages to match changing aspirations,â he said. title: Trump scraps Biden-era methane rules, says move will save $45 billion, unlock oil supplies
text: US President Donald Trump. US President Donald Trump on Tuesday announced that his administration was terminating a Biden-era regulation aimed at curbing methane emissions from oil and gas operations, arguing that the move would reduce costs for energy producers and consumers while boosting domestic oil production. Speaking at a rally in Lubbock, Texas, Trump said the rollback of what he called âexpensive and unnecessaryâ regulations would save $45 billion and unlock an additional 210 million barrels of oil, equivalent to around 10 days of US petroleum consumption. The move comes as Trump faces criticism over high fuel prices amid the war in Iran and seeks to encourage domestic oil and gas production. His administration has been rolling back climate policies introduced under former President Joe Biden. The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), led by Administrator Lee Zeldin, said the proposed revisions would ease restrictions on the oil and natural gas industry. The agency estimates the changes could also unlock 1.41 trillion cubic feet of additional natural gas. The Biden-era rule, finalised in 2024, required oil and gas operators to reduce methane leaks and limit the release of other harmful pollutants. It also introduced nationwide requirements covering existing oil and gas facilities, expanding on earlier regulations that largely focused on new and modified operations. One key provision was the EPAâs Super Emitter Program, which required companies to investigate major methane leaks detected by third parties using approved remote-sensing technology. The Trump administration has proposed eliminating the programme and easing standards for smaller oil and gas wells. Environmental groups warn of health and climate risks Environmental organisations criticised the rollback, arguing that weaker restrictions would allow oil and gas companies to release more methane into the atmosphere and avoid the costs of repairing leaks. Darin Schroeder, methane legal and regulatory director at the Clean Air Task Force, said the EPAâs proposal violated the Clean Air Actâs responsibility to protect public health and welfare. He urged the agency to withdraw the proposal and implement the 2024 rule. The American Lung Association also warned that methane leaks can release volatile organic compounds and carcinogens such as benzene and formaldehyde, which can worsen air quality and pose health risks to communities near oil and gas facilities. Environmental Defense Fund president Fred Krupp said the rollback gave polluting companies a âfree passâ at the expense of consumers. The organisation has estimated that oil and gas operators leaked, vented or flared about $7 billion worth of natural gas after the EPA announced in March 2025 that it would stop enforcing the regulations. Methane is the main component of natural gas and a potent greenhouse gas that contributes significantly to global warming. It escapes from oil and gas equipment through leaks and can also be released or burned off during drilling operations. Cutting methane emissions has become a major focus of global efforts to slow climate change. Trump administration argues rules burden energy industry The Trump administration has maintained that the Biden-era restrictions imposed excessive costs on energy producers and hindered domestic production. Zeldin has argued that the regulations would have cost the industry billions of dollars. The EPAâs latest proposal is part of a broader effort to reverse climate policies introduced under Biden, including measures targeting greenhouse gas emissions from power plants and vehicle fuel economy. The Biden administration had projected that its methane rule would prevent an estimated 58 million tons of methane emissions by 2038 and generate billions of dollars in public health and environmental benefits. The regulation also required operators to address leaks from smaller wells, which account for a relatively small share of US oil and gas production but can contribute disproportionately to methane emissions. The rule was designed to work alongside a methane fee introduced under the 2022 climate law. The fee, which would have charged energy producers for emissions above specified limits, was repealed by Congress after Trump took office. The rollback has also drawn attention to the oil and gas industry's efforts to influence the regulations. Records obtained by watchdog group Fieldnotes showed that industry representatives and companies met with the EPA to discuss methane rules at least 38 times during the Trump administrationâs first year. Environmental advocates say the changes could allow companies to continue wasting natural gas that could otherwise be captured and used, while increasing pollution in communities near drilling sites. title: 5 things to check before leaving your house for a long weekend
text: 5 things to check before leaving your house for a long weekend A long weekend usually means one thing: a few days away from work, a change of scenery and some much-needed time to relax. But the excitement of leaving can make it easy to overlook the little things waiting back home. A forgotten appliance, an unsecured window or a small leak can turn a relaxing trip into an unnecessary worry. Before locking the door and heading out, take a few minutes to check these five things. 1. Are all electrical appliances switched off? You might remember to switch off the lights but forget about appliances that do not need to run while you are away. Check your iron, room heaters, hair straighteners and other electrical devices before leaving. Unplug appliances that do not need to stay connected, following their safety instructions. Keep essential devices, such as refrigerators, running as required. 2. Have you checked the kitchen and bathroom taps? A tap that drips occasionally may not seem like a major concern when you are home. But a leak that goes unnoticed for several days can waste water or cause damage. Check the kitchen sink, bathroom taps and visible pipes for leaks. Make sure the washing machine is not running unnecessarily, and turn off the main water supply if appropriate for your home. 3. Are your doors and windows properly secured? Locking the main door is not enough if a balcony door or a bedroom window has been left open. Walk through the house once before leaving and check every accessible entry point. If you live on the ground floor or have windows that open towards a shared space, pay particular attention to them. 4. Will your home look unoccupied for days? An overflowing letterbox, newspapers outside the door or parcels left unattended can indicate that nobody is home. If possible, arrange for someone you trust to collect deliveries and check on your home. Avoid posting your exact travel dates or sharing that your house is empty with a wide audience on social media. 5. Have you taken care of things that could spoil or smell? Coming home to a refrigerator full of spoiled food or a foul-smelling kitchen can quickly spoil the post-holiday mood. Check what is likely to expire while you are away, dispose of rubbish and clear food scraps from the sink. If you are leaving for several days, make sure perishable food is stored appropriately and that nothing has been left out. Image: Canva (for representative purposes only)

title: State Cong leaders meet Kharge, Rahul; discuss 2027 poll strategies
text: Dehradun : Top Congress leaders from Uttarakhand, including state unit chief Ganesh Godiyal, leader of opposition Yashpal Arya and senior leader Pritam Singh, met party national president Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi in New Delhi on Monday to map out strategy for the 2027 assembly elections. The high-level strategy session, held at Khargeâs residence, was also attended by Congress general secretary (organisation) KC Venugopal and state in-charge Kumari Selja. Escalating its attack ahead of the 2027 Uttarakhand assembly polls, Congress accused the BJPâs âdouble-engineâ state govt of betraying public trust, citing failing law and order, rampant corruption, and environmental mismanagement. In a post on X, Kharge slammed BJPâs 10-year rule for collapsing law and order, compromising womenâs safety, and evading accountability. âThe people of Uttarakhand are now demanding accountability and seeking change... Our resolve is to win the trust of the people and give Devbhoomi Uttarakhand a secure, sensitive, and accountable govt,â Kharge stated. Venugopal targeted Dhami govt over exam paper leaks, Rishikesh resort murder case, temple donation mismanagement and corporate land grabs in ecological zones, calling the BJP regime a âtrouble engine model.â âIn 2027, the people will unseat BJP and ensure a thumping majority of Congress that will bring back a peopleâs regime in these states,â Venugopal claimed, referring to Uttarakhand and Manipur where elections are due early next year. He said âhatred, loot, land-grab and total misgovernanceâ symbolise BJPâs âtrouble engine modelâ in these states. âDevbhoomi Uttarakhandâs temples have also not been spared from the chanda chori (theft of donations) that the BJP has mastered in Ayodhya and all across India. Not only the holy temples, but BJPâs greed in Uttarakhand is seeing vast mountains being handed over to corporates despite clear warnings from Mother Nature against such wanton destruction,â Venugopal added. title: AU Bank probes potential data leak

title: BSP sounds 2027 poll bugle in UP, names Anoopshahr candidate
text: Bulandshahr: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) on Wednesday launched its campaign for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, with national coordinator Akash Anand addressing his first election rally in the state at Anoopshahr in Bulandshahr district. At a rally at a stadium in Khalor village of Jahangirabad, Anand announced Manoj Pradhan, who recently joined the BSP after leaving the BJP, as the partyâs candidate from Anoopshahr. He also declared Mukesh Pandit as the partyâs nominee from Shikarpur constituency. Addressing supporters gathered amid blue flags and caps, Anand urged them to bring the BSP back to power and make party chief Mayawati the chief minister of Uttar Pradesh for a fifth term. Beginning his speech with the slogan âJai Bhimâ, Anand recalled the contributions of BSP founder Kanshi Ram and Mayawati, saying they had dedicated their lives to the party and the cause of social justice. He said Mayawati had advised him to place the partyâs mission above family interests and added that he would work to strengthen the BSP and help it return to power. Anand targeted the BJP, Samajwadi Party (SP) and Congress over inflation, unemployment, alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations and the law-and-order situation. He accused the BJP govt of failing to provide employment to young people and burdening households with rising prices. He raised the issues of LPG cylinder prices, vacancies in govt departments and alleged paper leaks in recruitment examinations, claiming that the future of job aspirants was at risk. He also questioned the condition of govt schools and vacancies among teachers. Referring to the free ration scheme, Anand said the vision of Dr BR Ambedkar was to make people self-reliant and appealed to young voters to support the BSP. Targeting SP chief Akhilesh Yadav over the partyâs PDA slogan â referring to Pichhda, Dalit and Alpsankhyak â Anand alleged that the party was trying to attract the Bahujan community despite its past policies. He also referred to the renaming of districts during previous SP govts. He criticised Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over the partyâs record on reservation and its role during protests by young people. Anand accused the Congress and BJP of pursuing policies that had failed to address the concerns of marginalised communities. He also questioned the quality of infrastructure projects, alleging that damage to expressways during rainfall exposed shortcomings in construction. Citing the Lucknow-Agra Expressway, built during the Samajwadi Party govt, Anand said development claims should be backed by durable construction. BSP western UP n-charge and former Rajya Sabha MP Munkad Ali spoke about the partyâs founding principles, social justice and the welfare of the Muslim community, and urged people to strengthen the organisation. title: Govt directs colleges, univs to complete UG subject allocation by Nov 5
text: The admission process under phases I and II for the 2026-27 academic session has been completed Bhubaneswar: Odisha govt has asked all degree colleges and public universities under the higher education department to complete pending subject allocation for undergraduate students on the Student Academic Management System portal by 11.45 pm on Nov 5. In a letter to institutions, joint secretary Mousumi Nayak said the admission process under phases I and II for the 2026-27 academic session has been completed, but several higher education institutions have not yet assigned subjects to the students admitted under the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020. The department said subject allocation is compulsory for all undergraduate students in the first, second and third years. Colleges and universities with pending entries have been directed to complete the allocation within the stipulated time so that academic and examination-related processes under the NEP structure are not affected. The notification clarified that the major subjects allotted to the students at the time of admission will remain unchanged. Institutions have been instructed to allocate minor subjects, Multidisciplinary Course (MDC), Ability Enhancement Course (AEC), Value Added Course (VAC) and Skill Enhancement Course (SEC) in accordance with the guidelines issued by their respective affiliating universities. The department also advised the colleges to use the course master section of the SAMS portal if the required subjects are not visible in the drop-down menu. In cases where new subjects need to be added, institutions must coordinate with their affiliating universities. The universities have already been provided access through designated logins to update course details on the portal. The directive has been sent to govt, autonomous and non-govt degree colleges as well as the public universities for timely implementation of the NEP curriculum. Admission for first-year undergraduate students was completed by Oct 7, and classes have begun in degree colleges and universities across the state. The department said completion of subject allocation is necessary to streamline academic records and ensure students are mapped to their course combinations under the NEP. title: Lights that make a statement: Paper, fabric step into the spotlight
text: Ashni Studio / Oorjaa / Name Place Animal Thing Paper and fabric have long been used in lighting, but designers are finding new ways to work with these familiar materials. Through handcrafted techniques, unconventional forms and experiments with texture, they are creating pieces that go beyond the traditional lampshade. The emphasis is as much on the material and the form it takes as on the light it casts, allowing lighting to become an integral part of the design of a space. Amrita Nambiar, artist and founder, Olie, says, âWhile materials such as paper, fibre and textiles have long been used in lighting, today we see enormous possibilities in how they can be transformed through new techniques, unexpected forms and painstaking hand processes.â The result is lighting that explores the relationship between material, form and illumination. Rethinking familiar materials Olie From oversized installations to smaller sculptural pieces, paper and fabric are being used to create a range of forms. Jenny Pinto, founder, Oorjaa, says, âWe are seeing a shift from treating paper and fibre as secondary materials to exploring them as materials that define an entire form or spatial experience. We allow their inherent qualities to inform the structure, scale and character of a lighting piece.â Priti Mehta, founder, Ashni Studio, explains, âMaterial exploration is central to the design process. Natural materials such as banana fibre paper, banana bark, banana rope, washi paper, jute, cane and fabrics like raw silk and poplin each offer unique textures and possibilities. While banana fibre paper creates a soft, diffused glow, textured papers add depth through light and shadow, and woven fibres introduce intricate patterns. Techniques such as moulding, layering, weaving, fabric mounting, crochet and macramÃ© allow us to experiment with form and texture.â Texture is also influencing the way designers approach fabric lighting. Priyam Doshi, founder and principal designer, Name Place Animal Thing, says, âPeople want something other than just wood and metal. They want something more tactile that feels raw, cosy and soft. Today, we are working with more textured fabrics featuring embroideries, hand-painted motifs, and also using dyeing techniques. Even in fabrics, we try to use layered and crushed fabrics, moving away from just simple fabrics which are used to make classic lampshades. â Handcrafted techniques further add to the appeal of these lights. âMaterial research, prototyping, shaping, assembly and finishing involve close collaboration between designers and artisans,â says Pinto. âArtisanal skill is particularly important when working with paper and natural fibres, as these materials require a sensitive approach to shaping, joining and maintaining consistency across a piece.â Much of the innovation lies in rethinking familiar materials and exploring how they can behave in unfamiliar ways. The intention is not simply to make lighting bigger or more expressive, but to understand how form, material and light can work together to shape an environment Jenny Pinto, founder of Oorjaa Nature as a source of inspiration Oorjaa From honeycomb-like installations suspended from ceilings and mushroom-shaped lamps beside sofas to winged, illuminated forms hanging in bedrooms, nature is a recurring influence in these designs. Mehta says, âWe translate natural contours, textures, and fluid forms into organic lighting designs that go beyond conventional lampshades.â Pinto adds, âWe are increasingly interested in lighting as a sculptural element rather than an object defined by its shade alone. This opens possibilities for forms inspired by botanical structures, organic growth patterns, and the geometries found in nature. Think leaves, mushrooms, mycelial networks, and spider webs. We study the underlying structures and rhythms of these natural forms and translate them into contemporary lighting through material experimentation and handcrafted processes.â Why consumers are drawn to these lights Name Place Animal Thing Consumers are increasingly looking for distinctive pieces that tell a story and reflect their personality. Often made in limited numbers or on commission, fabric and paper lights feel personal and one of a kind. Doshi says greater exposure to different cultures through social media and travel has also shaped consumer preferences. âAdding these unique pieces to your home also becomes conversation starters, leaving a lasting impression on guests. â Comfort is another part of their appeal. Doshi notes, âPost the Covid-19 pandemic, people are prioritising comfort in their busy lives. After a long day at work, they want to return to a home where they can relax. These lights make a space feel soft, comforting and cosy." That, Doshi adds, is what draws people to them. It doubles as art Ashni Studio Considering the artistic nature of these lights, Nambiar says, âAudiences are approaching lighting as collectable design and art. We see these works as pieces to live with, experience and return to, rather than simply as fixtures within an interior. Besides simply illuminating a room, a sculptural light introduces a sense of movement, materiality and atmosphere, becoming an integral part of the architecture. â The choice of lighting depends on the space and the environment one wants to create. Oversized sculptural pieces can make a striking addition to stairwells, entrances and double-height living rooms, while smaller designs can bring warmth and character to bedrooms and dining areas. These lights also make an impression when switched off. Doshi says, âSince they are made from translucent materials, they look equally beautiful even when not illuminated. During the day, these pieces have their own unique charm, and in the evening, they are equally appealing but have a different feel.â Safety and maintenancePaper and fibre lights are not unsafe. However, they require careful consideration of heat management and electrical components. Material selection, structural planning and appropriate testing are essential to ensure these lights remain safe, durable and functional without compromising their sculptural form. Maintenance, however, need not be complicated. Doshi says, âYou donât necessarily have to use a wet cloth to keep the structures clean. A simple delicate brushing with a dry cloth does the work.â You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test Get the latest Lifestyle News and more. Download the TOI app.

title: JEE aspirant found hanging in Kota PG room; another student's death sparks negligence allegations
text: JEE aspirant found hanging in a PG room in Kota Two separate incidents of student deaths here have once again stoked concerns regarding students' health and safety in coaching hub Kota, with the family of one of the deceased accusing hostel authorities of negligence. A 16-year-old JEE-aspirant from Madhya Pradesh was found hanging at his paying guest accommodation on Sunday night, while another student from Bihar -- preparing for NEET -- was found unconscious in a bathroom at his hostel on Saturday night, and died during treatment on Sunday. In the latest incident, which police termed suicide, a 16-year-old JEE aspirant from Madhya Pradesh's Shivpuri district was found hanging inside his room at a paying guest accommodation located in Mahaveer Nagar-I under Jawahar Nagar police station area, on Sunday night. The victim had arrived in Kota six months ago to prepare for the Joint Entrance Examination (JEE), Circle Inspector Mukesh Meena said. The deceased student appeared for a routine mock test at a coaching institute on Sunday afternoon, and after returning to his PG room, he stopped responding to calls and did not open the door to his room despite repeated knocks, Meena said. The PG operator subsequently peered through a window and discovered the student hanging from a noose. Police arrived at the spot after being informed, shifted the body to MBS Hospital, and informed the family. No suicide note has been recovered from the deceased's room, and the reason behind the extreme step is yet to be ascertained, Meena said, adding that post-mortem is underway and the body would be handed over to the family after completion of formalities. Police have registered a case under relevant sections and investigation is underway, he said. In the second incident, a 19-year-old NEET aspirant -- Gautam Kumar from Bihar's Darbhanga -- was found unconscious in the bathroom of his hostel room in Landmark area under Kunhari police station on Sunday night. He was shifted to MBS Hospital, where he succumbed during treatment on Sunday noon. The deceased student had been living in Kota for nearly two years and had taken two attempts to clear the National Entrance-cum-Eligibility Test (NEET), police said. The grieving family members voiced suspicions regarding the circumstances of the death. "Nobody here is taking responsibility -- neither the hostel nor the coaching centre. "We do not know what happened -- whether he fell in the bathroom, accidentally consumed some poisonous substance, or something else happened to him," deceased's cousin Akhilesh told mediapersons outside the mortuary. He alleged that the hostel authorities took no notice of the student's absence during the four meals that are served in a day, and the incident was only discovered after the family contacted another cousin, living in a nearby hostel, to check on him on Saturday night. The family said Gautam was doing well in studies and not under any study-related stress. Citing alleged lapses in hostel management and lack of timely intervention, the family filed a complaint alleging negligence by the hostel authorities. Police have lodged an FIR under relevant sections, Circle Inspector Devesh Bhardwaj said. The officer said police are yet to reach a conclusion regarding the cause of death. title: NEET-UG paper leak: NTA withholds result of Latur coaching centre owner's son, bars him from exam for 2 years

title: Are banks cyber-ready? RBI seeks proof of compliance amid rising attacks
text: India's RBI tightens cyber checks on lenders after spate of hacks NEW DELHI: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has asked banks to step up their cybersecurity measures and demonstrate compliance with existing rules amid a rise in attacks on financial institutions. According to three people familiar with the matter cited by Reuters, the central bank also asked banks to check their application programming interfaces (APIs) for security gaps. These software links connect banks with non-bank lenders and fintech companies, making them a key area of concern, the sources said. The RBI has also sought information on how banks are preparing for risks associated with artificial intelligence (AI), as hackers increasingly use sophisticated tools to target financial infrastructure globally. Such attacks threaten both customer information and funds. One of the sources, a person aware of regulatory thinking, said hackers consider smaller lenders, non-bank lenders and their third-party service providers to be "softer targets". Although the RBI has already laid down directives for banks to manage cybersecurity risks, their implementation remains inadequate, said a second source, a consultant working with top banks. The regulator is now pressing banks to ensure stronger implementation of these requirements, the person added. Recent cyber incidents put lenders under scrutiny The concerns come against the backdrop of several cyber incidents reported in India's financial sector in recent weeks. State Bank of India, the country's largest lender, recently reported a data leak involving around 3,900 customers. The bank said last week that it was investigating the incident but had not yet identified the vulnerability responsible. In another incident, two Mumbai-based non-bank lenders suffered losses of around $2 million following more than 700 unauthorised instant transfers from accounts maintained with ICICI Bank on October 8 and 9, Reuters reported. According to the complaint, hackers had compromised the API connection through which loan disbursal instructions were sent to ICICI Bank. The threat has also drawn attention from India's cybersecurity agency CERT-In. In an advisory issued on October 9, the agency warned that hackers were stealing banks' API credentials to move money out of lenders' own systems, potentially with the assistance of AI-based tools. CERT-In also conducted cybersecurity training earlier this week for 300 officials from more than 55 financial institutions, according to a post shared by the agency on its social media handle on X. The RBI's actions come as financial regulators globally are increasing their efforts to address the cybersecurity risks associated with AI. Authorities in the United States and Britain are among those stepping up measures to contain these threats, Reuters reported earlier this month. You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. title: Headmaster injured after cylinder catches fire during midday meal preparation
text: The cylinder continued to burn for nearly 30 to 45 minutes before the fire died out after the gas was exhausted Koderma: A major mishap was averted at Upgraded Middle School, Samaldih, in Satgawan block of Koderma district on Wednesday after an LPG cylinder caught fire while the midday meal was being prepared, leaving the headmaster with minor burn injuries. The incident occurred around 11.30 am while cooking was under way for students. In the absence of a dedicated kitchen shed, the meal was being prepared on the school verandah. Officials said the fire broke out after a cook detected a gas leak while attaching the regulator to a cylinder. Before the leak could be contained, the gas came in contact with a coal stove burning about 1.5 metres away, engulfing the cylinder in flames. Headmaster Sunil Kumar suffered minor burns on his hands while trying to extinguish the fire using wet jute bags. Teachers safely evacuated all 188 students present on campus. The school has a total of 224 students. The cylinder continued to burn for nearly 30 to 45 minutes before the fire died out after the gas was exhausted. Administrative officials, including the BDO, rushed to the spot, while Kumar received first aid at Satgawan Hospital. Deputy commissioner Utkarsh Gupta said the district superintendent of education had been asked to submit a detailed report, and functioning fire extinguishers would be provided to schools. title: Fired US general admits leaking classified Iran, Ukraine information to journalists: Report
text: File photo: Fired Lt Gen Brett Sylvia The US Army general fired by defence secretary Pete Hegseth admitted to leaking classified information about the wars in Iran and Ukraine to journalists over a period of roughly a year, according to an internal investigation report reviewed by Axios. Lt Gen Brett Sylvia, who headed the Joint Chiefs of Staffâs Strategy, Plans and Policy Directorate, known as the J5, acknowledged sharing classified information with two reporters from separate media outlets, according to the report. A US official told Axios that Sylvia made the admissions on video after failing multiple polygraph tests during the investigation. Sylvia was dismissed by Hegseth on Wednesday over what the Pentagon described as severe misconduct. The investigation, which has been referred to the Department of Justice for further action, remains ongoing. According to the report, the disclosures began as early as June 2025 and continued after the Pentagon tightened restrictions on media access. Sylvia allegedly communicated with reporters through the encrypted messaging application Signal and also met one journalist in person at a Silver Diner in Arlington, Virginia. The report said the diner meeting took place after the journalistâs access to the Pentagon had been revoked. During the meeting, Sylvia relied on notes he had made while reviewing a classified report to orally share information about US assistance to Ukraine. The journalist was working on a book and met Sylvia twice, the report said. Sylvia did not coordinate the meetings with the Pentagonâs public affairs office or seek clearance before sharing the information. Investigation points to deleted messages The investigation also raised questions about Sylviaâs handling of communications with one of the reporters. According to the report, he received a Signal message sometime in June or July that he believed concerned Iran. Sylvia said he could not recall its precise contents and claimed he had deleted the message, believing he had accidentally erased the entire conversation thread. This also removed Signal messages and calls that could otherwise have been recovered from his personal phone. US officials suspect Sylvia deliberately deleted the communications and presented the action as accidental. The report also said he admitted to being one of 20 officials cited in a media story critical of Pentagon leadership. Another US official told Axios that Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle and his office had lobbied the Joint Staff to issue a statement supporting Sylvia in an effort to limit the damage from any future allegations of leaks. The Joint Staff later withdrew the statement after someone in the Defence Department informed it of the reasons behind Sylviaâs dismissal. US president Donald Trump, asked about the firing on Thursday, said Sylvia had âbig problemsâ and that the administration was âvery much looking for leakersâ. Trump appeared to refer to Sylvia using female pronouns. Separately to the Axios report, a defence department official also confirmed to Al Jazeera that Sylvia was under investigation for leaking classified information concerning the Iran war, Russiaâs war against Ukraine and other matters. The official said he had failed three polygraph tests and accused him of putting national security at risk. The official also stressed that Sylvia was not a central planner for the Iran war, saying that responsibility rested with Centcom and its commander, Adm Brad Cooper. Hegsethâs wider crackdown on leaks Sylviaâs dismissal is the latest action in Hegsethâs campaign against unauthorised disclosures to the media. In July, the Pentagon announced a joint task force with the Justice Department to identify leakers and directed its Office of General Counsel to prioritise prosecutions over the unauthorised release of classified information. The Pentagon had also introduced restrictive rules governing journalistsâ access and reporting in October 2025, prompting several news organisations and defence reporters to surrender their press credentials. title: No UP govt jobs for those involved in violent activities seeking âregime changeâ
text: UP govt has clarified, however, that political ideology alone cannot be a ground for declaring a candidate ineligible for a government job. LUCKNOW: The Uttar Pradesh government has revised its recruitment guidelines to make candidates associated with organisations advocating violent changes to the established system ineligible for state government jobs. The new rules also permanently bar candidates implicated in certain serious offences from government employment. The guidelines were issued on Wednesday by Principal Secretary (Appointment and Personnel) M Devaraj, following directives from the high court. They apply to all state government departments, public sector corporations, boards, and urban and rural local bodies. According to the circular, membership of an organisation that seeks to alter the âvidyaman vyavasthaâ (established system) through violent methods will make a candidate ineligible for government employment. The order, however, distinguishes between political beliefs and support for violence. â(One's) political ideology won't serve as a ground for disqualifying anyone from holding government jobs,â the order reads. It, however, adds that those âassociated with organisations whose 'sankalpit uddeshya' or avowed purpose is to force a regime change through violent means will be considered ineligible.â The revised rules also permanently disqualify candidates implicated in serious offences, including murder, dacoity, rape, outraging modesty, corruption, acts of terror, recruitment examination paper leaks and organised âsolver gangâ rackets. The guidelines set out a three-year period for assessing a candidateâs involvement in activities related to violent changes to the established system. If an applicant has participated in such activities within three years before the verification date, after attaining 21 years of age, authorities will presume that the person remains actively involved. However, officials may consider documented evidence showing a genuine positive change in the candidateâs conduct and mindset during this period. The government has also clarified that a first information report (FIR) or an ongoing police investigation will not, by itself, lead to disqualification. Candidates who have been acquitted, resolved cases through lawful compromises, or whose cases fall under the Juvenile Justice Act will not face automatic rejection. Existing state government employees will not need fresh character verification. However, authorities may seek relevant service records from their previous parent departments. The new guidelines also seek to prevent delays in recruitment caused by pending verification reports. Appointment letters will not be withheld solely because character verification is incomplete. Appointing authorities may issue provisional appointment letters on the basis of a candidateâs self-declaration and prescribed undertakings. If any information is subsequently found to be false, the appointment will be cancelled and criminal proceedings initiated. Under the revised procedure, district police and the Local Intelligence Unit (LIU) must submit character verification reports within 30 days of receiving a request. The state home department will directly monitor compliance with the deadline. The guidelines also place restrictions on verification procedures to prevent harassment of applicants. Police and intelligence officials have been instructed not to visit candidatesâ homes for questioning, and applicants will not be required to appear physically at police stations. If a verification report is adverse, the district magistrate must give the candidate an opportunity to present their side, either in person or online, before forwarding a final adverse recommendation, the order said. title: Pipeline breaches trigger massive wastage; citizens slam PMC over leaks as stricter supply cuts loom
text: DOWN THE DRAIN Pune: As Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) prepares to impose stricter water cuts, residents have criticised its failure to promptly repair damaged pipelines, fix leaks and seal seeping storage tanks, allowing thousands of litres of water to spill onto city roads. The latest incident unfolded in Kothrud on Monday, where a PMC water distribution pipeline was ruptured during road excavation work, resulting in significant water wastage. The incident is far from isolated. Similar breaches and leakages have surfaced across Hadapsar, Kothrud and Bavdhan over the past month, exposing what residents described as a ârecurring and costly failureâ in the cityâs water distribution network. Civic activists claimed that such incidents had become alarmingly routine, with pipeline damage being reported almost every other day in some parts of the city. Narhe-based activist Vikram Gaikwad said, âLeakages are serious and such wastage is not acceptable when the city is reeling under a water crisis. Most merged areas are already not receiving adequate water, but on the other hand, PMC is not able to curb the water losses from leakages.â While PMC has undertaken replacement of aging and leaking pipelines in several localities, particularly in the older central parts of the city, the problem remains stubbornly persistent. Beyond underground distribution lines, concerns are now mounting over leakages from overhead water storage tanks as well. Former corporator Yogesh Sasane said PMCâs overhead storage tank in Hadapsar had been leaking continuously for several days. Echoing similar concerns, Balewadi corporator Amol Balwadkar said he and his team had inspected the overhead tank in the Pashan area a few months ago after complaints about water seepage. âPMC will have to be proactive in curbing all sorts of water wastage to deal with the increasing water crisis,â he said. Officials from PMCâs water supply department admitted that unplanned and unsupervised excavation works had emerged as one of the biggest threats to the cityâs pipeline network. An official said, âOn many occasions, sudden and unplanned digging damaged the pipeline. The pipelines were damaged recently in areas of Kothrud, Paud Road, Balewadi, Hadapsar and Shivajinagar. title: Polytechnic exam papers emailed after portal glitch
text: Higher education minister Roji M John Thiruvananthapuram : Higher education minister Roji M John told the assembly on Wednesday that an alternative system was used to distribute question papers for polytechnic diploma exams after technical glitches affected the state board of technical education portal. The arrangement was put in place to ensure that exams across the state were conducted without disruption, following concerns over the distribution of question papers at polytechnic colleges. Normally, question papers are uploaded to the portal, from where exam centres download them an hour before the start of each exam. However, an alternative system was in place for years under which the papers are sent to institutions through official email if the portal develops technical glitches. The portal encountered technical problems on Oct 14. The issue was immediately reported to the National Informatics Centre but it was not resolved on time. Question papers were subsequently sent securely to the official email addresses of all institutions 30 minutes before the start of each exam. John said the method was used during similar portal disruptions in 2019, 2022 and April 2026. Question papers for exams conducted under the old scheme continue to be sent by mail. He said neither the department of technical education nor govt had received complaints from students or heads of institutions over the distribution of question papers. title: 'Ballot paper, still we ask': Kharge dares BJP to dissolve Parliament after MLC poll setback
text: NEW DELHI: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Thursday reiterated the opposition's demand for voting using ballot paper despite the party's lacklustre performance in the Karnataka MLC elections, which were held using ballot papers. Reacting to the Karnataka MLC results, Kharge said the opposition would not give up its demand for ballot paper voting simply because BJP won the elections. He also challenged the BJP to dissolve Parliament and contest elections using ballot papers. "Ballot paper, still we ask. It doesn't mean that we should leave because they are winning. Once upon a time they won only two Parliament seats. Sometimes it happens, that doesn't mean that party has no hold," Kharge said. "That ego should not be there in BJP that they have done very well. If that is the case, let them dissolve the Parliament and go on ballot paper," he added. Kharge's remarks came after Prime Minister Narendra Modi took a dig at Congress for "drawing a blank" in recent MLC elections. The grand old party had won zero seats till Wednesday night. The party, however, opened its account after retaining Nagpur Division Graduates' constituency seat. "MLC elections in 28 seats across 4 big states - Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar and Karnataka. Elections held using ballot papers. Guess how many seats Congress won?" PM Modi said in a post on X. BJP national president Nitin Nabin also targeted Congress, saying the party would continue to struggle for survival under Rahul Gandhi's leadership. title: Satish Waghole gets additional  charge as MPSC chairman
text: Satish Waghole Mumbai: Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) member Satish Waghole was on Friday given additional charge as chairman after Vivek Bhimanwar proceeded on leave pending a judicial inquiry into alleged paper leaks and the commissionâs functioning. Waghole, a former principal secretary of state law and judiciary department, joined MPSC as a member on Sept 9. His term ends on April 24, 2030. State govt on Friday issued a notification for conducting an inquiry under the Commissions of Inquiry Act, 1952 into the paper leaks and other irregularities in MPSC. The notification said the govt had received representations alleging leaks in MPSC examinations and considered the matter of definite public importance. Officials said governor Jishnu Dev Varma had approved the notification. The five-member inquiry committee is headed by former Chief Justice of Allahabad High Court Dilip Bhosale. Members include former judge P D Naik, former IAS officer Ganesh Patil and IPS officer Lakhami Gautam, with IAS officer Tukaram Mundhe as secretary. The panel has been given two months to complete its probe. The state notification stated that the committee will enquire and fix the responsibility for malpractices or leakage of question papers or answer keys in MPSC exams and also determine whether misconduct or misbehaviour by serving or former members, including the chairman, âso as to proceed for their removal under Article 317 of the Constitution of Indiaâ. Bhimanwar announced on Monday that he would remain on leave until the inquiry was completed. âThe state govt has announced a judicial inquiry into the MPSC paper leak case. Throughout my entire life, I have always prioritized ethics. Therefore, I have decided to go on leave during this period instead of continuing to serve in the post until this inquiry is completed. The autonomy, credibility, and interests of students of the MPSC have always been my priority, and they will continue to be so in the future,â Bhimanwar said in a post on X. His announcement prompted aspirants to end their 11-day agitation in Pune. NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar , who had led agitation, welcomed the inquiry. He alleged that MPSC member Abhay Wagh was also a âbig playerâ and students have a strong sentiment that he too should be sent on leave. âFinally, a judicial commission has been established under the Commissions of Enquiry Act-1952 to thoroughly cleanse the entire commission through investigations into the paper leaks of various MPSC exams and from constables to chairpersons. The commission will also investigate the drug inspector position exam along with Group B, Group C, and other suspicious exams. Given the powers vested in the commission, a complete purge from bottom to top is expected, along with recommendations for further action on the 317, this is the hope! The current member Abhay Wag is a big âplayerâ and students have a strong sentiment that he too should be sent on leave just like Bhimanwar. The govt should pay attention to this matter, this is the request! Regarding Group B, we will be meeting the judicial commission next week and we need to submit as much evidence as possible to them, so students should collect all evidence with student representatives or with us, we will ensure not a single guilty person escapes! Until we send them home... we wonât let go,â Rohit said in a post on X. text: Jodhpur panchayat polls marred by clashes Jodhpur panchayat polls marred by clashes Jodhpur panchayat polls marred by clashes Jodhpur panchayat polls marred by clashes Jodhpur panchayat polls marred by clashes Jodhpur panchayat polls marred by clashes Jodhpur panchayat polls marred by clashes 1 2 3 Jodhpur: Clashes, stone-pelting and allegations of bogus voting and ballot paper theft disrupted the second phase of panchayat elections in Jodhpur district Friday. title: Sony data breach: 2.58 million users affected as bank details and passwords exposed
text: Sony Data Breach has affected over 2 million users (Image via Sony) Sony has confirmed a major data breach affecting customers of its Japanese internet services. The incident hit So-net and plala, two providers owned by Sony Network Communication, and exposed more than 2.58 million customer records. The company says the breach doesn't touch PlayStation Network accounts, but the scale and the type of data involved make it worth understanding. The section below takes a detailed look at the Sony data breach. Sony data breach: What actually happened According to Sony, an unauthorized party gained access to its systems on October 19, 2026. The company confirmed that 2,585,481 customer records were affected. The data was reportedly leaked a few days later, on October 24. Sony disclosed the incident on October 27. So-net and plala are internet service providers in Japan. They offer broadband, email, and related connectivity, so the breach mainly affects customers in that market rather than gamers on PlayStation. How many records were exposed The total breaks down like this: So-net: 2,141,986 records plala: 443,495 records Email and password combinations: 54,401 identified within the exposed data The exposed data includes a mix of personal details: Names User IDs Dates of birth Phone numbers Email addresses Other customer information 16 bank account records, including account numbers Despite the headline, the bank-related exposure is limited to those 16 records. The larger concern is the volume of personal information, which could be used for phishing or social engineering. The 54,401 email and password pairs also matter, since stolen credentials are often tried on other sites. It is worth noting that Sony says its investigation found no sign that credit card numbers or expiration dates were taken. The company also says bank PINs aren't stored in its systems, so they weren't part of the leak. Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines Sony's response Sony says it took the following steps: Shut down the affected servers Blocked the unauthorized access Reset passwords for the impacted email accounts on October 27 Reported the incident to Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission The investigation is still ongoing, so the numbers and details could change as more is learned. What affected users should do Sony advises customers not to click suspicious links while it works out the full scope of the breach. Beyond that, sensible precautions include: Watch for phishing emails or texts that use your name or phone number. Change the password on any other account that shares credentials with your So-net or plala login. Use a unique password for each service, ideally through a password manager. If you were among the 16 bank account records, contact your bank and monitor your account. PlayStation players aren't directly affected, but changing your PSN password is a cheap precaution if you want extra peace of mind. The breach arrives soon after Capcom disclosed its own incident on October 22. Sony has also dealt with an unrelated security issue involving unauthorized child accounts on PSN.
