title: Seven Italian students built a paper aircraft with a 20-metre wingspan and successfully flew it inside a hangar
text: Image Credit: Guinness World Records A paper aircraft measuring more than 20 metres across its wings has set a Guinness World Records title after successfully flying inside an aeroplane hangar in Bologna, Italy. Created by students from the University of Pisa, the giant aircraft, named Icarus, was made entirely from paper and glue. Its successful flight on 25 June 2026 marked the end of months of planning, testing and construction. According to the University of Pisa, the aircraft travelled 59 metres, surpassing a record that had remained unbroken since 2013. How did seven Italian students build the record-breaking paper aircraft According to Guinness World Records, the project began with a simple idea shared by engineering students during their university lectures. The group discovered the existing record while studying for exams and decided to attempt something that had previously seemed difficult to achieve on such a scale. The previous record belonged to the Braunschweig Institute of Technology in Germany, whose paper aircraft had a wingspan of 18.21 metres. That achievement had stood since 2013, giving the Italian students a clear target to beat. The University of Pisa reported that the project was developed by its engineering students with support from science communicator and content creator Jakidale. What started as an informal idea developed into a substantial engineering challenge involving design, calculations, testing and construction. The team eventually expanded its efforts beyond the original seven students, bringing in 16 additional helpers to contribute to the technical and production work. The collaboration helped turn the idea into an aircraft large enough to challenge the existing world record. Icarus is different from an ordinary paper plane The finished aircraft measured 20.04 metres from one wingtip to the other and approximately seven metres in length. Guinness World Records lists its weight at around 28.5 kilograms, making it a substantial structure despite being constructed using only paper and glue. The scale of Icarus presented a different challenge from making a conventional paper plane. A small model can be folded and thrown by hand, but a structure measuring several metres requires careful planning to maintain its shape and travel through the air successfully. According to Guinness World Records, the students used computer simulations to predict how their design might perform before committing to the final construction. These simulations helped them explore the aircraft's proportions and consider how the finished structure could be made to fly. The University of Pisa confirmed that the final aircraft was built by hand using paper and glue. Keeping to these materials was central to the challenge, as the team needed to produce a record-breaking aircraft without relying on a conventional frame or other structural materials. How did the team develop the aircraft before its record attempt The journey towards Icarus involved several stages rather than one successful design from the beginning. Guinness World Records reported that the team built two earlier prototypes before arriving at the final version. The first large model was named Prometheus, after the figure from Greek mythology associated with bringing fire and technology to humanity. It helped the students explore the structural elements needed for a much larger paper aircraft. Their next attempt, Daedalus, measured 8 metres in length and was also constructed from paper and glue. Although it did not perform perfectly, it gave the group practical experience with the materials and highlighted areas that needed improvement. The team then developed a smaller model measuring four metres. This version successfully glided through the air, offering an important demonstration that their approach could work. These experiments allowed the students to learn from earlier designs before committing to the final aircraft. The final aircraft was named Icarus, after the mythological son of Daedalus who attempted to fly. The name reflected the project's central ambition, although the students approached the challenge through careful preparation rather than relying on a single attempt. What happened when the giant paper aircraft finally flew The record attempt took place on 25 June 2026 at the We Make Future event at BolognaFiere in Bologna. The event, associated with the European Institute of Innovation and Technology's business and entrepreneurship activities, provided a public setting for the aircraft's first major flight. According to Guinness World Records, the team positioned Icarus on scaffolding before preparing to launch it across the hangar. One of the students carried the aircraft into position and prepared to throw it towards the opposite side of the indoor space. The launch required a coordinated effort because of the aircraft's size. Once it was ready, the student ran along the scaffolding and released the plane. The aircraft briefly caught the air before gliding forwards and gradually descending towards the concrete floor. Its movement resembled that of an ordinary paper plane, although its enormous dimensions made the flight a unique sight for the watching crowd. The University of Pisa confirmed that Icarus travelled 59 metres during the successful attempt. Guinness World Records lists the achievement under the title of largest paper aircraft, with the record officially established in Bologna on 25 June. Importance of the achievement for the University of Pisa The successful flight brought an end to a 13-year wait for a new holder of the largest paper aircraft record. According to the University of Pisa, the achievement returned the title to Italy after the previous record had remained with the German institution since 2013. Guinness World Records adjudicator Lorenzo Veltri presented the team with its record certificate after the aircraft's successful launch. He praised the combination of engineering knowledge, teamwork and technological creativity that had made the achievement possible. You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

title: A 117-year-old North Carolina basilica battled leaks and storm damage, then underwent a $7.7 million first phase of restoration; it reopened daily to visitors, while the full preservation effort could top $30 million
text: A century-old architectural landmark in Asheville, North Carolina, has reached a major milestone after years of deterioration threatened its distinctive dome and historic masonry. The Basilica of Saint Lawrence completed the first phase of a $7.7 million restoration and marked its reopening with a ceremony on October 10, 2026. According to Catholic News Herald, local outlet HERE Asheville and public radio station BPR News, the project focused on stopping water leaks, repairing storm damage and protecting the building for future generations. The restoration is part of a much larger preservation effort that could eventually cost more than $30 million. While the latest work has addressed some of the buildingâs most urgent problems, further repairs will depend on funding and the progress of subsequent phases. A historic landmark threatened by water damage Located in downtown Asheville, the Basilica of Saint Lawrence is known for its distinctive elliptical dome and intricate tile construction. Designed under the supervision of Spanish architect Rafael Guastavino Sr., the church was completed in 1909 and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places. Over the years, leaks and deteriorating building materials made extensive repairs increasingly urgent. Hurricane Helene, which struck western North Carolina in September 2024, added to the damage and reinforced the need to protect the structure. The restoration began in October 2025 after years of planning, assessments and fundraising. Preservation specialists and construction teams were tasked with addressing water intrusion while safeguarding the architectural features that make the basilica distinctive. The first phase was budgeted at approximately $7.7 million, with contributions from parishioners, donors and grants helping fund the work. What the $7.7 million restoration included The initial phase concentrated on the buildingâs exterior and structural protection, particularly areas vulnerable to water damage. Work included replacing the copper covering on the iconic dome, installing new storm drains and gutters, repairing cornices and restoring the domeâs oculus skylight. Crews also stabilised masonry above the Marian Chapel and addressed damage associated with Hurricane Helene. These repairs were intended to prevent further water from entering the building and to stabilise vulnerable sections of the historic structure. Stopping the leaks was particularly important because continued moisture exposure could threaten masonry, interior finishes and other architectural details. The project involved specialist preservation work rather than routine maintenance. Guastavinoâs distinctive tile-and-mortar construction requires care to retain the buildingâs historic character while improving its long-term durability. The completion of the first phase therefore represents an important step, rather than the end of the basilicaâs preservation needs. An architectural legacy worth preserving Guastavinoâs work is known for its distinctive tile vaulting, a construction technique that uses layers of thin tiles and mortar to create strong, elegant structures. His work can be seen in prominent American landmarks, including Grand Central Terminal and Ellis Island in New York. The Asheville basilica is particularly significant because it represents one of his most ambitious architectural projects. Construction began in the early 1900s, but Guastavino died in 1908, before the church was completed. His son, Rafael Guastavino Jr., helped bring the project to completion in 1909. Preservation efforts have been under consideration for years, with assessments and fundraising campaigns laying the groundwork for the current project. The Basilica Preservation Fund, a nonprofit organisation established in 2008, has helped raise money to protect the building and its architectural features. Reopening marks a milestone, not the finish line The October 10 ceremony brought together Bishop Michael Martin, parishioners, donors and preservation specialists to mark the completion of the first phase. The reopening was a significant moment for a church that continued to hold Masses and sacraments during construction, even as weekday visitor access was restricted. However, the restoration remains a multi-stage undertaking, with the overall cost potentially exceeding $30 million. Future work will depend on continued fundraising and the condition of the building as further repairs are planned. There is also an important distinction between the ceremonial reopening and unrestricted daily access. The basilicaâs official website, updated October 22, lists limited visiting hours during the ongoing restoration and announces a revised schedule beginning November 2. Visitors should check the official websiteâ  before planning a visit. For Asheville, the completed work is more than a construction milestone. It is an investment in a historic structure that has shaped the cityâs skyline for more than a century. By addressing the most urgent threats first, the restoration team has taken a crucial step towards ensuring that the basilicaâs architectural and cultural legacy can endure for generations to come. title: Man dupes finance firm of Rs 2L with forged papers
text: Investment fraud Panchkula : A woman working as a branch head at a finance company in Panchkula was allegedly duped of Rs 2 lakh by a man who approached her with a proposal to transfer a gold loan using forged documents. According to the FIR, the complainant, Sandhya Devi, a resident of Haripur, Sector 4, is employed as a branch head at the companyâs Sector 9 office. The alleged fraud took place on Oct 23 between 11am and 4pm. The complainant told the police that a man had been contacting her on phone for four to five days regarding the transfer of a gold loan. He allegedly offered to get a Rs 2 lakh loan transferred from another finance company. On Oct 23, the man visited her office and submitted documents, including two cheques in the name of the company, an Aadhaar card, a PAN card, a Rs 100 stamp paper and a gold loan slip. Based on the documents, the complainant initiated the loan takeover process and forwarded the relevant details to the companyâs head office for approval. Following approval, Rs 2 lakh was transferred to the Adampur branch of a bank in Hisar district. The complainant subsequently accompanied the customer to collect the pledged gold from the other finance companyâs Sector 9 branch in Panchkula and verify his local address in Sector 10. However, when they reached a hospital in Sector 4, the man allegedly got out of the vehicle on the pretext of attending to something and fled. On checking, the complainant allegedly discovered that the documents submitted by the man were forged and that no genuine gold loan had been taken over. She alleged that the accused had cheated the company of Rs 2 lakh by transferring the amount into his bank account. Following the complaint, an FIR was registered on Oct 31 under relevant section of BNS against an unidentified accused. title: Protesters in Mumbai get show-cause notices to sign peace bonds
text: Protesters in Mumbai get show-cause notices to sign peace bonds Mumbai: Mumbai police have issued show-cause notices to some activists who participated in multiple protests and allegedly mobilised others over the last four months asking them to state why they should not be directed to execute a bond of Rs 50,000 promising good behaviour for one year, backed by a suitable surety, and why proceedings should not be initiated under Section 126 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). A notice by itself does not establish guilt. Section 126 empowers executive magistrates or special executive magistrates to take preventive measures to maintain public peace and tranquillity. One of the allegations mentioned in a notice concerned an appeal to gather near Ashoka Pillar at Chaityabhoomi in Dadar on July 20 in support of demands linked to exam paper leaks and calls for the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan . The notice also referred to a purported appeal to mobilise supporters at Shivaji Park on Oct 11 to demand the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged electoral fraud. It claimed that these activities had the potential to create law and order problems and threaten public safety. Another allegation related to a protest on Oct 10 near Nana Chowk, close to August Kranti Maidan, where Progressive Students Unionâs Samya Korde and Tushar Gandhi , president of Hum Bharat Ke Log, allegedly gathered around 350-400 protesters without permission. The notice to Korde, seeking preventive action over her alleged involvement in organising protests without permission at multiple locations in Mumbai, was issued on Oct 23 by Anurag Jain, special executive magistrate and DCP, central zone-II, Matunga. Wadala TT police submitted a report alleging that she used her social media accounts to mobilise people for protests without obtaining the requisite permissions. The notice claimed the gathering involved sloganeering, obstruction of traffic and inconvenience to commuters, in violation of prohibitory orders issued by the state govt. It also referred to a case registered at Gamdevi police station for unlawful assembly and other offences. Korde told TOI that she had merely exercised her constitutional right to protest. âI will seek legal opinion and respond to the show-cause notice. Social media is a tool that can be used to mobilise people for a protest. How does that make it unconstitutional?â she asked. She said organisers had always informed police before holding protests but had never received permission. âIt is policeâs responsibility to maintain law and order during a protest. â Korde alleged selective action by police and cited an instance of an effigy of an opposition party functionary being burnt in the past. She said no action was taken and no one was detained in that case. The notice issued to her said after examining the police report and supporting material, there were grounds to believe that she could engage in similar activities in the future that might disturb public order. It directed her to appear before the court at Matunga police station on the date specified in the notice and submit her explanation within seven days of receipt. Special executive magistrates in Delhi had recently issued notices to Cockroach Janta Partyâs Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, and Neha Bora of All India Studentsâ Association to sign peace bonds following their calls for protests into alleged poll fraud. title: CBFC data leak: Unreleased scripts, 500 film titles, censor cut exposed in security breach - Reports
text: The Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) has reportedly faced a data security scare after confidential documents linked to more than 500 film titles were allegedly exposed through its e-Cinepramaan portal. The reported incident has raised concerns within the film industry about the security of sensitive material submitted for certification, including unreleased scripts, censor cut orders and distribution agreements. According to reports, the documents remained accessible through digital archiving platforms for several days before the alleged breach came to light. While the actual film files were reportedly not leaked, the security breach and leaking of confidential documents have prompted questions about the safeguards in place to protect filmmakers' intellectual property and commercially sensitive information. Unreleased scripts and censor details among documents reportedly exposed The documents allegedly exposed include scripts of unreleased films, details of cuts and modifications ordered during the certification process, and other confidential material associated with film submissions. The reported exposure of scripts is a particular concern for filmmakers, as the premature disclosure of storylines, plot developments and key scenes could compromise projects before they reach audiences. Details of scenes marked for deletion or modification could also become public knowledge. What is e-Cinepramaan? The e-Cinepramaan portal is the CBFC's online system through which filmmakers and production houses submit applications for film certification before their projects are released. The alleged breach has raised concerns about the safeguarding of information shared as part of the process. Distribution agreements and licensing details exposed The alleged leak reportedly includes private distribution contracts and licensing fee details associated with domestic and international film projects. Such documents may contain commercially sensitive information, including revenue-sharing arrangements, intellectual property clauses and other contractual terms negotiated between production houses, distributors and licensing partners. title: Scientists tested 27 people against one trained dog in New Mexico's desert; the dog detected bird carcasses 87% of the time, while people averaged just 49%
text: AI Representation: A trained conservation detection dog searches for bird remains in the desert. Image credits: Chatgpt Bird counting is harder in the open desert than it may seem. Wildlife managers rely on bird mortality counts to determine the impact of human activity on birds and a count can only be as accurate as the person doing it. A new study has put that to the test by pitting human surveyors directly against a conservation detection dog. The U.S. Geological Surveyâs record of the paper lays out how the two compared. The paper describes paired searches in desert habitat, with each surveyor type working the same carcass placements so the team could compare detection under identical conditions. It also reports that detectability varied sharply with carcass size and ground cover, with larger birds and sparser substrate giving both humans and the dog their best odds. Two years of trials in the desert of Southern New Mexico The study, Carcass size and ground substrate drive detection rates of avian carcasses by human surveyors and a dog team, was led by Kelley C. Boland and published in 2026 in Global Ecology and Conservation . Co-authors of this paper are: Abigail Jean Lawson, Dylan M. Osterhaus, Patricia L. Culter, Gregory A. Davidson and Martha J. Desmond. In the study, the authors analysed carcass-search data from wind-energy surveys in southern New Mexico and tested whether detection changed with carcass size, substrate and weather. They found that both humans and the dog were strongly helped by larger carcasses and less visually complex ground cover and they note that the same field factors influenced survey performance more than the choice of search alone. The research was conducted in the semi-arid high desert of southern New Mexico for two years using detection trials. According to the USGS record of the paper, 27 human surveyors and one conservation detection dog took part in 1,096 trials with 238 carcasses representing 50 bird species. The dog found 87% of carcasses; people found 49% According to the paperâs abstract on the USGS website, the dog had an average detection rate of 87%, compared with 49% for human participants, a difference of 38 percentage points. There was quite a variation among individual humans: humans' detection rates were between 25% and 71%. The study took place over two years in theÂ  semi-arid high desert of southern New Mexico. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons Even the best human searcher, at 71%, still fell below the dogâs 87% average. The dog also missed 13% of carcasses, a reminder that detection dogs improve carcass recovery but cannot guarantee every dead bird is found. The authors point out that the extent of the difference is similar to the results obtained previously by other researchers. Carcass size and ground substrate affected both searchers The title specifies the two variations that impacted the outcomes. Detection for both humans and the dog depended on carcass size and ground substrate. The chances were greater when dealing with large carcasses and less complicated surfaces. The study adds an important caveat: detection depends on carcass size and ground substrate. Why the number matters for conservation As the abstract provided by the USGS notes, correct estimation of bird mortalities is necessary to understand human impact on birds and to develop effective conservation efforts. However, if carcass surveys fail to account for a significant number of carcasses, mortality estimates will fall short of the actual figures. In addition, the research is described as being insightful in relation to wildlife mortality estimates.

title: Dead on paper, but breathing: The people who had to prove they were alive
text: (AI Image) A heart rate monitor displays a renewed life sign amid the shadows of a medical room. Instances of people being declared dead but later found alive have repeatedly raised questions about medical negligence, identification errors and lapses in hospital procedures. From a woman who was reported murdered seven years ago but was found alive to patients who regained consciousness moments before cremation or burial, several such incidents across India have left families shocked and prompted investigations. While some cases involved alleged clerical errors at hospitals, others raised questions about the procedures followed before declaring a person dead. Here is a look at some incidents in which people pronounced dead were later found alive. Woman declared murdered seven years ago found alive in Rajasthan In a bizarre case, Mehandipur Balaji police on Saturday detained a woman who had been declared dead seven years ago, while two men accused of her murder had served imprisonment in connection with the case. The police traced the woman, Aarti, after receiving information from the victims, who alerted them about her whereabouts. According to Mehandipur Balaji police station officer Ajit Singh Badsera, Sonu said he had married Aarti in 2015 through a court marriage. However, after the marriage, Aarti allegedly demanded that land and money be transferred in her name. When Sonu expressed his inability to meet her demands, she allegedly left the house after eight days and disappeared. Despite searching for her, he could not trace her. Meanwhile, Uttar Pradesh Police found the body of an unidentified woman in the Magorra canal in Mathura. As a post-mortem examination was not conducted, the police had the body cremated. Around six months later, Aarti's father, Suraj Prasad Gupta, approached the police to inquire about his missing daughter. The police showed him photographs and clothes recovered from the deceased woman, following which he identified the body as that of Aarti. Her father subsequently accused Sonu Saini and Gopal Saini, residents of Mehandipur Balaji, of murdering his daughter. The two accused were arrested and served imprisonment in the case. However, the latest development, with Aarti being found alive, has brought a fresh twist to the case. Woman found alive- Aarti Rajasthan man declared dead shows signs of life before cremation In another shocking incident, a 25-year-old deaf and mute man, Rohitash Kumar, who was declared dead by doctors at a hospital in Rajasthan's Jhunjhunu district, showed signs of life just before his cremation. Kumar, who lived at a shelter home and had no family, was taken to the emergency department of BDK Hospital in Jhunjhunu on Thursday after his health deteriorated. After he reportedly failed to respond to treatment, doctors declared him dead at around 2pm and shifted his body to the mortuary. Following the necessary documentation, the police transported the body to a crematorium. However, just as the body was placed on the funeral pyre, Kumar reportedly began showing signs of breathing, according to police reports. An ambulance was immediately called, and he was rushed back to the hospital, where he was admitted to the intensive care unit. Officials later confirmed that his condition was stable. The incident prompted the district administration to take action. District collector Ramavtar Meena suspended three doctors â Dr Yogesh Jakhar, Dr Navneet Meel and principal medical officer Dr Sandeep Pachar â on Thursday night. An investigative committee was also constituted, and the medical department secretary was informed about the incident. Revenue officer Mahendra Mund and Deputy Director of the Social Justice Department Pawan Poonia subsequently visited the hospital. Kolkata patient declared dead, later found alive in hospital In another case involving an alleged hospital error, a patient who had been declared dead and whose death certificate had been issued was found alive at Chittaranjan National Medical College Hospital in Kolkata. Sabir Molla had been admitted to the hospital on April 11 after complaining of chest pain. On Thursday evening, his family received a call from the hospital informing them that he had died. The following morning, his relatives reached the hospital morgue to collect his body. However, in an unexpected turn of events, Molla spotted one of his relatives from a bathroom in one of the hospital buildings and called out to him. When the family informed hospital authorities, they were initially told that they might have mistaken someone else for Molla. The family also alleged that the hospital had earlier refused to hand over the body, citing his positive Covid test. Molla was subsequently discharged from the hospital later that morning. The hospital authorities initiated an inquiry into the incident. Agra man declared dead by hospital found alive at home In a case that left both the police and a family bewildered, a man who had been discharged from a hospital after treatment for a snake bite was later declared dead by the same medical college. Kush Chaurasia had been admitted to SN Medical College after a snake bite on Sunday morning. Following a medical examination, doctors discharged him a few hours later. However, the hospital authorities reportedly informed the police that he had died. When the police visited his residence to inform the family and collect details, they were shocked to find Chaurasia alive. "It was a funny situation. I didnât know how to react. I gave all the documents to prove that Iâm alive and informed the police that it might be a mistake by the hospital authorities," Chaurasia said. His wife, Richa Chaurasia, said the family was having tea when a police officer arrived and informed her that her husband had died, even as he was standing beside her. "We believe it was a clerical mistake by hospital staff and they misinformed police about someone else who might have died at the hospital," she said. Following the incident, medical college principal Dr Saroj Singh ordered an inquiry. A committee headed by Dr P K Maheshwari of the medicine department was formed to investigate the matter and submit a report within two days. "We believe it was a clerical mistake. The doctor might have wrongly written the name of another patient instead of the actual deceased one," Dr Saroj Singh said. Vinay Kumar Mishra, station officer of Shahganj, also confirmed that Chaurasia was alive and said the incident appeared to have resulted from a clerical error by hospital staff. Siddharthnagar man found alive before burial, dies during treatment In Siddharthnagar district of Uttar Pradesh, a man who was presumed dead by his family after suffering a heart attack was found alive just before his burial. The incident took place in Sikhara village in Dumariyaganj, where Akram had fallen seriously ill in Mumbai after suffering a severe heart attack. He was admitted to a hospital, where he received treatment for around 24 hours before doctors referred him for further medical care. However, his family mistakenly believed that he had died and informed relatives in his native village. Preparations for his burial began, and an ambulance was arranged to transport him home. At around 3am on Wednesday, when the ambulance reached the village, some residents noticed signs of life and suspected that Akram was still breathing. The suspicion continued for nearly six hours. When preparations were being made to bathe the body, an onlooker noticed slight movement in Akram's lips. He was immediately taken to a doctor, who confirmed that he was alive. Akram was first rushed to a nearby private hospital and later referred to a hospital in Basti because of his critical condition. However, he died during treatment at the hospital, a villager, Shakeel, said. Beed newborn declared dead, found alive a day later, dies In Maharashtra's Beed district, a newborn who was declared dead by doctors at a government hospital in Ambajogai but was found alive 24 hours later died on Friday night. The baby had been placed on ventilator support after being brought back to Swami Ramanand Teerth Rural Government Medical College and Hospital. The newborn was admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU), where doctors continued treatment. Dr Ganesh Tondage, head of the obstetrics and gynaecology department, said the baby died due to cardiopulmonary arrest. "The baby was born after only 27 weeks of pregnancy. The newborn was struggling for breath and was kept on life support. Despite all measures, the baby could not survive," he said. Doctors said the newborn had exhibited Lazarus syndrome, a rare phenomenon in which a person declared dead shows spontaneous signs of life after unsuccessful cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and other resuscitation measures. The incident also involved what doctors described as suspended animation, in which vital body functions, including the heart, may temporarily cease. Dr Shankar Dhapate, dean of the hospital, said a five-member committee had been constituted to investigate the incident, but its report was still awaited. "It was not even a pre-term delivery as the baby was born only after 27 weeks of pregnancy. Vital organs, including the heart and lungs, fail to develop in such partially incomplete pregnancies, leading to a low survival rate of the babies," he said. The family could not be reached for comment. Earlier, the family had said it had no complaints against the doctors at the government hospital. title: Teen stages abduction to extort â¹5L from family, traced to Haryana
text: Lucknow : Police on Sunday traced a 17-year-old NEET aspirant from Sonepat in Haryana , who had allegedly staged his own abduction to extort Rs 5 lakh from his family to fund outings with his girlfriend and clear online gaming debts. The teenager, a resident of the Para area, was found safe within 48 hours of the complaint being filed. Investigators later found that he had allegedly fabricated the kidnapping plot. According to DCP (West) Jitendra Kumar Srivastava, the boy had been staying in a rented room and attending coaching classes in Alambagh while preparing for NEET. He had earlier lived with his uncle but was asked to move out following repeated disputes over his online gaming habits and mounting debts. The teenager went missing on Oct 20, prompting his family to search for him. After they failed to locate him, a missing-person complaint was filed at Para police station on Oct 22. The case took a dramatic turn when the boyâs parents, brother and maternal uncle began receiving WhatsApp messages demanding Rs 5 lakh for his release. The messages threatened to kill him if the ransom was not paid. In one message, the family was told to search for his body in the forests of Chennai, triggering panic among relatives. Following the ransom threats, police activated surveillance and cyber-tracking teams. Investigators analysed digital evidence and eventually traced the teenager through an online payment trail. Police said the boy had switched off his phone after disappearing and later used another personâs mobile hotspot to send ransom messages and make WhatsApp calls while posing as a kidnapper. To make the story appear genuine, he also contacted a cousin, claiming he was stranded, did not know where he was and lacked money even for food. He then persuaded her to transfer Rs 2,000 using a QR code he shared. That transaction proved to be the breakthrough. Using the payment details and other digital leads, the surveillance team tracked down the teenager, who was found staying with his girlfriend, police said. âDuring questioning, he allegedly admitted that no kidnapping had taken place and that he had orchestrated the entire drama himself. Police have initiated legal action against him for allegedly misleading investigators, creating panic and spreading false information,â DCP Srivastava said. title: Cramped truck, no food or water: 25 cattle being taken to Keralam for slaughter rescued
text: The animals have been moved to a govt-run shelter, while police are awaiting a veterinarianâs certificate before taking further action. CHENNAI: Police and animal welfare activists rescued 25 cattle being transported to Keralam for slaughter in cramped conditions and without proper documents near Maraimalai Nagar on Saturday. The animals have been moved to a govt-run shelter, while police are awaiting a veterinarianâs certificate before taking further action. The rescue followed a complaint by animal welfare activist Sai Vignesh, who spotted the truck parked near Maraimalai Nagar on Saturday evening. âCow dung and urine were leaking from the vehicle and I could see that the animals were cramped inside. There was no provision for food or drinking water, no adequate ventilation, and the animals were struggling to breathe, contrary to govt rules for slaughter transport. I informed the police, and filed a complaint,â he said. A senior police officer confirmed that the drivers did not have a âfit-to-transferâ certificate issued by the Animal Husbandry Department. âThe drivers admitted that the cattle were being transported for slaughter. The truck was then raided by a police team, and all 25 cattle were sent to a govt goshala for immediate care. A certificate from a veterinarian, after examining the animals, the wound and their age, is required for further action, against the driver and the employer,â the officer said. title: SSC announces November 2026 exam dates: Check CGEPT, departmental tests and Delhi Police SI Paper-II schedule

The Coast Guard recruitment examination will be conducted through a Computer-Based Examination (CBE), while departmental candidates will appear for their respective skill tests. The Delhi Police and CAPFs Sub-Inspector recruitment examination will cover Paper-II. Candidates preparing for these examinations can refer to the official notification for the announced schedule. Examination Tier/mode Examination dates Coast Guard Enrolled Persons Test (CGEPT), Batches 01/2027 and 02/2027 CBE November 17 to 18, 2026 Annual Departmental Typing Test (English/Hindi) and Stenographer Skill Test (English/Hindi) Examination, 2025 Skill Test November 20 to 21, 2026 Sub-Inspector in Delhi Police and CAPFs Examination, 2025 (Paper-II) Paper-II (CBE) November 28, 2026 The CGEPT for the two batches will be held over two days, November 17 and 18. SSC advises candidates to check official website In its notice, the commission has advised candidates to visit the official SSC website at regular intervals for further updates regarding the examinations. Any additional instructions or changes to the announced schedule will be communicated through the commission's official channels. â¢ Candidates can access the examination notice directly through the official PDF: Download SSC examination schedule notice SSC examination calendar 2026-27: What candidates should know The SSC conducts recruitment examinations to fill vacancies across various ministries, government departments and subordinate offices. Its annual examination calendar provides candidates with information about upcoming recruitment examinations, including notification releases, application deadlines and examination schedules. The tentative calendar for 2026-27 covers recruitment opportunities across different categories, including clerical, inspector-level and engineering posts. title: 25 cattle transported for slaughter without proper documents rescued near Maraimalai Nagar
text: Cattle being transported illegally to Keralam for slaughter were rescued. 25 cattle transported for slaughter without proper documents rescued near Maraimalai Nagar near Chennai. Chennai: As many as 25 cattle being transported to Kerala for slaughter in inhumane conditions and without proper documents were rescued by police officers and animal welfare activists near Maraimalai Nagar on Saturday. The animals have been sent to a govt-run shelter and police are awaiting a certificate from the veterinarian for further action. The seizure was carried out on a complaint from animal welfare activist Sai Vignesh, who stumbled upon the truck parked near Maraimalai Nagar on Saturday evening. âCow dung and urine were leaking from the vehicle and I could see that the animals were cramped inside. There was no provision for food or drinking water, no adequate ventilation, and the animals were struggling to breathe â contrary to govt rules for slaughter transport. I informed police and filed a complaintâ he said. A senior police officer confirmed that the drivers did not possess a âfit-to-transferâ certificate issued by the animal husbandry dept. âThe drivers admitted that the cattle were being transported for slaughter. The truck was then raided by a police team, and all 25 cattle were sent to a govt goshala for immediate care. A certificate from a veterinarian, after examining the animals, the wound and their age, is required for further action â against the driver and the employer,â the officer said. A police constable said the veterinarianâs report was likely to be submitted on Monday. title: OCS aspirants seek postponement of Main exams
text: Odisha Public Service Commission Bhubaneswar: Candidates appearing for Odisha Civil Services (OCS) Main Examination 2025 have sought postponement of remaining papers beyond Nov 7, questioning the practicality of the revised schedule announced by Odisha Public Service Commission (OPSC) amid the threat of the cyclonic storm and the forecast of heavy rainfall in southern Odisha. The commission, in a notification issued on Monday, rescheduled the Odia and English language papers from Oct 29 to Oct 31. The Odia paper will be held from 9 am to noon and the English paper from 2 pm to 5 pm. The essay paper, originally scheduled for Oct 30, has been shifted to the morning session on Nov 5. The general studies papers I and II on Nov 2, papers III and IV on Nov 4, and both optional subject papers on Nov 7 will, however, be held as scheduled. Candidates, particularly those from southern Odisha, said the revised dates could create difficulties in travelling to exam centres and appearing for the tests if heavy rain disrupts transport and other essential services. They have urged the commission to defer the remaining papers until weather conditions improve. The exam is being held at 31 centres across six zonal locations â Balasore, Berhampur, Bhubaneswar, Cuttack, Jeypore and Sambalpur. Candidates pointed out that Berhampur in Ganjam district and Jeypore in Koraput district, two of the examination locations, fall in areas facing the threat of severe weather. Several aspirants took to social media platform X on Tuesday to flag their concerns with the chief ministerâs office and OPSC, describing the revised schedule as impractical. âThe state govt declared holidays till Oct 31 due to cyclone, yet OPSC schedules OCS Mains on the same day. Aspirantsâ safety has to be also taken into consideration,â said Dusmanta Mangaraj, an aspirant. Candidates also cited the India Meteorological Department âs red warning for Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri districts. They said candidates travelling from these areas could face difficulties reaching their exam centres if heavy rain disrupts road connectivity. âThere are also many govt employees who would write the exam. The state govt has cancelled all leaves till Oct 31 for the cyclone. How would these candidates fulfil their official duties and exercise their right to appear for the examination on Oct 31? We are just demanding a fair and practical schedule,â said another candidate, Sameer Kumar Pradhan. The commission officials said the changes were made in view of the impending landfall and the heavy rainfall expected in some parts of Odisha, with candidatesâ safety being a key consideration. title: Prank call on Delhi blast plan lands UPSC aspirant in police net
text: Kanpur: Delhi Police arrested UPSC aspirant Suraj Verma (23) for allegedly making a hoax call claiming that an organisation operating from Pakistan had selected his former roommate for a bomb blast in Delhi. Suraj allegedly called his former roommate, Rohit Kumar , a fellow civil services aspirant, claiming he was speaking from Lahore. During the call, he said that an organisation called Jannat-e-Firdaus had been monitoring him and had chosen him to carry out the blast before abruptly disconnecting. During questioning, Suraj told police that he had made the call as a prank to scare Rohit. Suman Kumar, a civil services aspirant from Bihar living in Indra Vikas Colony, Mukherjee Nagar, complained to police after his roommate Rohit received the call from an unknown landline number. Investigators traced the number to a private telecom fibre connection registered to Manoj Kumar Verma, a resident of Naveen Nagar in Kanpurâs Kakadev area. A Delhi Police team, coordinating with local police, raided the identified location. Kanpur police commissioner Raghubir Lal said that, following an alert from Delhi Police, Kakadev policeâs surveillance team found Manojâs son, Akshat Verma, a NEET aspirant, at the house. Akshat said his nephew Suraj, a resident of Dibiyapur in Auraiya who is preparing for the UPSC examination, had recently visited them. Surajâs aunt, who has cancer, is undergoing treatment at a private hospital in Kanpur. Police said Suraj allegedly used the landline at his relativeâs house and modulated his voice to suggest that he represented a Pakistan-based organisation. Lal said the local intelligence unit also questioned Suraj before Delhi Police took him into custody. Intelligence officials are investigating his possible links. title: SEBI plans to remove inactive companies from stock exchanges, says chairman
text: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has announced steps to delist companies without meaningful economic activities from stock exchanges, aiming to safeguard investor interests. (Pic Credit: IANS) KOLKATA: The securities and exchange board of India (SEBI) is taking steps to remove companies with no economic activity from stock exchanges, as their continued listing could expose investors to potential risks, chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said on Saturday. Chairman Pandey pointed out that several companies remain listed despite having no economic activity, making them vulnerable to misuse by market manipulators, according to the news agency PTI. "They pose a potential danger to investors, and therefore, it is necessary to remove them from the listed space. We are making efforts towards their delisting," he said at a programme in Kolkata. He stressed that addressing the presence of such companies was important for maintaining market integrity. Their continued listing could put more investors at risk, particularly through social media groups used to promote questionable stocks. According to Pandey, some manipulators use these stocks for "pump and dump operations". SEBI is deploying artificial intelligence (AI) tools to identify and scrutinise suspicious accounts, alongside several other measures aimed at protecting retail investors from such schemes. Changes proposed for SME listing framework On the small and medium enterprises (SME) listing platform, the SEBI chairman said the regulator had proposed a series of changes through a consultation paper to strengthen the existing framework. However, he acknowledged that some older companies on the platform continued to be a concern. SEBI to ease certain FPI norms On foreign portfolio investors (FPIs), Pandey said SEBI would soon release another consultation paper proposing relaxations in certain regulatory requirements, particularly those concerning disclosures and concentration limits. The paper is expected to be issued in the coming weeks, rather than months, he said. Pandey noted that FPIs operate across international markets and assess investment opportunities based on post-tax returns in dollar terms. Their decisions are influenced by factors such as corporate earnings prospects, the emergence of new sectors, currency movements, US Federal Reserve interest rates and global bond yields. He added that SEBI was working to make the Indian market more accessible for FPIs by simplifying processes related to their onboarding as well as their continued operations in the country. title: AIIMS organises bike rally for breast cancer awareness
text: Participants hold placards with breast cancer awareness messages Nagpur: A breast cancer awareness bike rally emphasising the importance of early diagnosis, thereby encouraging women to seek timely counselling for treatment and positive outcomes was organised by Department of Surgery, AIIMS Nagpur, with the guidance of executive director AIIMS Nagpur, Prof Dr Prashant P Joshi. This was in collaboration with âPink partnerâ, a unit of central India NAVODAY alumni association, IMA Nagpur, Association of Surgeons Nagpur, and health department, Nagpur Municipal Corporation (NMC). The initiative witnessed enthusiastic participation from over 300 participants. The rally was flagged off by the organising chairperson Prof Dr Siddharth P Dubhashi, Professor and head, Department of Surgery, AIIMS Nagpur, at IMA Hall, Nagpur. Several distinguished guests graced the occasion, including Dr Sachin Gathe, president IMA, Nagpur, Dr Deepa Jahagirdar, president, ASN, Dr Deepak Selokar, chief officer of health, NMC, Dr Sangita Renge, dermatologist and homoeopathic practitioner, Dr Anirudh Deoke, Professor and head, Department of Community Medicine, NKPSIMS Nagpur, past ASN presidents, past IMA presidents and officers from RST Cancer Hospital Nagpur. Participants carried placards displaying awareness messages. The purpose of the rally was to create awareness about early diagnosis and how complete treatment can save lives and bring happiness to families. The rally witnessed the active participation of all faculty, PG students of Department of Surgery and several UG students of AIIMS Nagpur, members of the general public, and Navodaya alumni from Nagpur, IMA and ASN members. The highlight of his presentation was the need to âBecome a BREAST CANCER FRIEND.â Breast cancer survivors, whose courage and determination served as inspiration, were felicitated. The survivors shared their personal experiences and expressed heartfelt gratitude to the doctors and healthcare team at AIIMS Nagpur for their treatment, care, and support. A short educational film reinforcing the importance of compassion, awareness, and collective responsibility in supporting breast cancer patients, prepared by Dr Sangita Renge, was played. The programme was anchored by Dr Divish Saxena. The enthusiastic involvement of participants from different sections of society reflected the growing recognition that cancer awareness is not solely the responsibility of healthcare professionals but a collective social responsibility. The programme concluded with a renewed commitment to spreading awareness about breast cancer and promoting early detection and complete treatment. title: A roughly $13 roll of duct tape beat 54 sandbags in flood tests, cutting water leaks through doors by up to 98%
text: AI-generated representative image showing duct tape sealing the outside edges of a residential front door as floodwater collects against the threshold. Credits - GeminiÂ For many years, sandbags have been a familiar sight at the front doors of homes threatened by flooding. The Environment Agency withdrew its public guidance on sandbags and their use in June 2020. New laboratory tests at the University of Hull have since examined whether readily available tape can provide a temporary way to reduce water entering through doorways. The withdrawal of the guidance did not make tape a complete replacement for professionally designed flood protection. Researchers at the University of Hull's Property Flood Resilience laboratory, working on a study commissioned by Flood Re , found that wide duct tape applied to the outside of a standard door reduced water leakage by 97 to 98% compared with an unprotected door. A barrier made from 54 sandbags reduced leakage by up to about 70%. A roll of duct tape cost about Â£10, or $13, while the sandbag arrangement cost roughly Â£250. The results apply to water entering through tested doorways, not every possible route into a home. Tape is a temporary measure, not a replacement for professionally designed flood doors or barriers. How the tests worked The experiment was conducted at the University of Hull's PFRlab, a purpose-built laboratory developed with support from Flood Re and the Environment Agency. Researchers tested six types of external doors, including composite, wooden, uPVC and fire-rated designs. They increased the water depth in increments of 5 centimetres up to a maximum of 60 centimetres (about two feet), collecting the water that passed through each door and continuously measuring the leakage rate. For comparison, researchers placed plastic sheeting between each door and a barrier of 54 sandbags stacked in interlocking rows. The barrier reached the intended water depth and took 20 to 30 minutes to assemble, even when the bags were already filled and stored nearby. To make the comparison more consistent, the same person applied the tape in each test. Applying tape took roughly 10 to 20 minutes per door, according to an account by researcher Stuart McLelland published in The Conversation. The baseline data demonstrate why the stakes are considerable. An unprotected door leaked up to around 10,000 litres per hour for every metre of width at 0.6m. That rate means water might rise about 11 centimetres in an hour for a 100 square metre home. The tests were aimed to replicate shallow flooding similar to that which struck Hull in 2007 when more than 8,600 houses and 1,300 businesses were affected. What the numbers showed The University of Hull investigation found that the top performer was flexible synthetic rubber tape, often known as flood putty tape, which reduced leakage by nearly 99%. The high-quality broad duct tape (97% to 98%) was the most pliable and easiest to move and work around hinges and thresholds. Aluminium tape and yellow plastic tape were more difficult to apply and, at shallow depths, decreased the leakage by only 80 to 90%. But the weakest tape was better than the sandbags. Of the main choices, sandbags were the worst. They only cut leakage by less than half up to 0.2 metres, and after the water was deeper than 0.3 metres, they reduced it by 60% to 70%. The sandbag-protected doors leaked, on average, about 370 litres an hour per metre at 0.2 metres. The paper points out that a normal UK bath holds roughly 180 litres, so a household would have to drain two baths an hour simply to stand still. The modern sandless sandbags were a lot better, cutting leakage by 98% to 99%. But they had to be soaked for at least three minutes before use, were cumbersome to stack and would cost around Â£410 for 48. The team utilised branded duct tape that cost between 50p and Â£1 a metre. Representative image of a person using sandbags to keep floodwater out of the house. Credits - Wikimedia Commons Where tape falls short Where the tape was applied mattered. It worked best on the outside of a clean, dry door before floodwater arrived. When researchers applied it to the inside of a door, it peeled away as water pressure increased. On one uPVC door, the leakage rate rose from about 550 to about 2,000 litres per hour per metre during the test. Silicone sealant around some frames also made it harder for the tape to adhere, so the tape needed to bridge those areas and reach solid surfaces on either side. Hinges, thresholds and weather bars were particularly difficult to seal. The tests also involved simple doors. Tape wonât stop water coming through walls, floors, drains or airbricks, and lab results donât automatically apply to every real flood. Flood Re and the researchers are keen to underline that tape is not a replacement for professionally built flood doors or barriers. Three temporary barriers were trialled at a cost of between Â£400 and Â£700 each. The finest one blocked all detectable leakage but required a recessed entryway. One other did not fit most of the doors. Door opening direction also appeared to affect leakage. Under the test conditions , outward-opening doors allowed less water through than inward-opening doors. However, only two outward-opening doors were examined, so the researchers cautioned against drawing a broad conclusion from this comparison. PFRlab plans further tests on airbricks and a wider range of doors. The study recommends choosing a flexible tape, practising its application in dry weather and keeping it accessible as part of a wider flood preparation plan. The University of Hull's PFRlab reports that about 6.3 million homes across the United Kingdom are at risk from flooding by rivers, the sea and surface water, and that this figure could rise to 8 million by 2050. BBC News also previously reported advice given during an earlier flooding incident in Bradford on Avon to use gaffer tape on doors. Duct tape could be a low-cost addition to an emergency flood kit, but it cannot protect a whole home from flooding. Water may still enter through walls, floors, drains and airbricks. The tests show that correctly applied tape can reduce leakage through a doorway, but homeowners should use it only as a temporary measure alongside flood warnings, an evacuation plan and any professionally recommended protection.

title: Ahmedabad: Orders for green gifts light up waste-picker womenâs co-op whose 2025-26 turnover was Rs 1.6 crore
text: Virtuous recycling Ahmedabad: At a Saraspur unit, machines hum with green productivity, turning paper waste into notebooks, files, and pens; the recycling enterprise is powered by a cooperative of the cityâs waste-picker women, Gitanjali, whose 2025-26 turnover was Rs 1.6 crore. Few understand the value of recycling better than the women on the shopfloor, many of whom once collected waste paper from dumpsites. With Diwali round the corner, order sheets are full. The cooperative, part of the larger Sewa organisations, is supplying notebooks, ledgers, diaries, planners, files, gift boxes, pens and other items to corporates such as Adani, Tata , Cisco, Mindtree, and to various govt arms in Assam and Ladakh. Private schools in Gujarat and elsewhere are also Gitanjali clients. Having registered on the Govt e-Marketplace portal, the cooperative is also reaching out to more govt bodies. Paliben, the master trainer at the Saraspur facility, said, âOver the past three years, we have consistently kept the turnover above Rs 1 crore, and the earnings from the enterprise go to the hardworking women.â She added, âWe constantly innovate based on observing other products available in the market, train women on different production machines, and also teach them skills such as identifying the right recycled paper and material based on orders.â What started with 50 members now has over 45,000. The final result, which came after more than 40 hours of counting, forced Fadnavis to delete a tweet he had posted the previous day, mocking the Congress for failing to win any seat in the MLC polls. Congress candidate and sitting MLC Abhijeet Wanjari defeated BJP's Sudhakar Kohale in the Nagpur Graduatesâ constituency by 3,271 votes, securing 67,231 votes against his rival's 63,960. Also read - 'Commit to ballot paper': Congress dares PM Modi after his 'how many seats' swipe over MLC results Fadnavis had posted the tweet in response to Prime Minister Narendra Modiâs dig at the Congress on X. âBy deleting the tweet, Fadnavis has once again preserved Savarkar's legacy! Even before the full results were in hand, in a show of firing a big arrow, Fadnavis tweeted. But that very arrow turned back and pierced straight into his chest! In the end, he was forced to delete the tweet,â the Maharashtra Congress said on X. âMr. Fadnavis, scared already at this stage? This is just the trailer! In 2029, the people of Maharashtra will drop such a political bombshell on you that even this tweet of today will come back to haunt you! All the best, Mr. Fadnavis! Get ready for the next jolt,â it added. Wanjari, the sitting MLC, secured 67,231 votes against Kohale's 63,960. The result dealt a setback to the BJP in Nagpur, the hometown of Fadnavis and Union minister Nitin Gadkari, both of whom had campaigned extensively for Kohale. Congress hits back at PM Modi over ballot paper remark The Congress also targeted Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his remarks on the party's performance in the Legislative Council elections held across four states. Modi had questioned the Congress's tally, pointing out that the polls were conducted using ballot papers. "MLC elections in 28 seats across 4 big states - Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar and Karnataka. Elections held using ballot papers. Guess how many seats Congress won?" Modi wrote in a post on X. Congress Rajya Sabha MP Pawan Khera responded by challenging the prime minister to commit to using ballot papers in future Lok Sabha and assembly elections. "If Narendra Modi is so confident that EVMs have no bearing on election results, let him prove his confidence in the BJPâs electoral prowess through action, not rhetoric," Khera wrote on X. He also demanded the suspension of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, the restoration of what he alleged were 13.3 crore illegally deleted voters, and action against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar also criticised Fadnavis over the deleted post, pointing to the BJP's defeat in Nagpur, where the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) headquarters is located. "Respected Devendra Fadnavis Saheb, In the Nagpur Graduates Constituency, where you yourself took personal interest and went door-to-door to persuade the rebels to withdraw, in that very Nagpur constituency, in the area where the RSS headquarters is located, the BJP had to face defeatâthe meaning of this is clearâ¦â¦ It is indeed regrettable that you had to delete your tweet; but the immense ego of power evident in your deleted tweet is not good at all. Anyway, I can understand. Perhaps you forgot that the election was held via ballot, so the tweet might have been made prematurelyâ¦ Congratulations to the victorious candidate Abhijit Wanjarri, thanks to the graduates who gave their blessings in the form of votes, and best wishes to all the contesting candidates as well!" Pawar wrote on X. MVA wins three of five Maharashtra MLC seats With Wanjari's victory, the opposition Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA) won three of the five Maharashtra Legislative Council seats contested on October 23, while the BJP-led Mahayuti secured two. NCP (SP) candidates Harshada Deshmukh-Jadhav and Pratapsinh Patil won the Pune Graduatesâ and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Graduatesâ constituencies, respectively. Shiv Sena candidate Kiran Sarnaik won the Amravati Teachersâ constituency, while BJP candidate Kaustubh Gawade secured the Pune Teachersâ seat. Kohale had led Wanjari after the second round, but neither candidate secured the required quota through first-preference votes. Wanjari eventually overtook his rival during the subsequent elimination rounds as preferential votes were transferred. The outcome dealt a setback to the BJP in a constituency it had traditionally held. Gadkari represented the Nagpur Graduatesâ constituency in the Maharashtra Legislative Council for 24 years, from 1990 to 2014. The results have triggered a political exchange between the BJP and opposition parties over electoral performance and the use of electronic voting machines. title: Eminemâs former employee pleads guilty to copyright infringement after selling unreleased music for $50,000; leaked tracks streamed 8 million times, $750,000 in losses; faces 5 years in prison
text: Eminemâs former employee Joseph Strange has pleaded guilty to criminal copyright infringement over the unauthorised sale of unreleased music. Joseph Strange, a former employee of rapper Eminem , has pleaded guilty to criminal copyright infringement for copying and selling the artistâs unreleased music without his knowledge or permission. According to the US Department of Justice, Strange sold at least 10 audio files online for approximately $50,000. The leaked tracks were subsequently made available on public streaming platforms and had been accessed more than eight million times as of November 2025. Strange, 48, from Holly, Michigan, entered his guilty plea in the Eastern District of Michigan on a charge related to the unauthorised reproduction and sale of music created by Eminem, whose real name is Marshall Mathers. He is scheduled to be sentenced on January 27, 2027, and faces a maximum penalty of five years in prison. Watch Kate Winslet Spills Secret Eminem Moment On Graham Norton Show Eminemâs former employee copied unreleased music from studio hard drives According to court documents, Strange worked for Mathers from approximately 2007 to 2021. During his employment, he worked at a studio in Ferndale, Michigan, which the rapper used to create and develop music for future sale and distribution. Strange also helped set up and operate a computer system that stored Mathersâ music. As part of his work, he had access to password-protected hard drives containing tracks and other material in various stages of development that were not yet intended for public release. At some point during his employment, Strange copied 10 or more audio files from one or more of these drives without authorisation, according to the Justice Department. Between July and August 2024, he sold and transmitted at least 10 of the files to buyers over the internet, receiving approximately $50,000. The transactions took place without Mathersâ knowledge or permission. Leaked Eminem tracks were accessed over 8 million times The music files sold by Strange eventually appeared online and became available on various public streaming platforms without Mathersâ prior knowledge or consent. According to facts cited by the government, the material was not necessarily going to be commercially released, and no release was imminent or certain. However, professional efforts had been made to prepare some of the tracks for possible commercial distribution, with some having undergone studio mastering. Data provided by several streaming services showed that, as of November 2025, the infringing audio files identified by the government had been accessed more than eight million times. The estimated infringement amount associated with the stolen files was at least $750,000. Joseph Strange abused a position of trust Joseph Strange sold unreleased Eminem music for approximately $50,000, with the estimated copyright infringement amount reaching at least $750,000. Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Departmentâs Criminal Division said Strange had abused his position of trust by unlawfully copying and selling Eminemâs unreleased music for personal profit. âHis conduct undermined both legal and artistic rights,â Duva said, adding that the Criminal Division remained committed to protecting intellectual property, holding accountable those who profit from stolen creative content, and working with law enforcement partners to deter such crimes. US Attorney Jerome F. Gorgon Jr. for the Eastern District of Michigan also emphasised the importance of protecting property rights, including intellectual property. He said his office would work to hold accountable those who steal the physical or intellectual property of Americans. FBI praises investigation into the unauthorised sale of Eminemâs music Jennifer Runyan, special agent in charge of the FBI Detroit Field Office, said Detroit had a strong creative culture and that no one had the right to profit from another artistâs work without permission. Runyan described the guilty plea as a reminder that those who compromise the integrity of another personâs creative work can be held accountable. She also commended the FBIâs Oakland County Resident Agency and the wider investigative team for their work on the case. The FBI official acknowledged the cooperation of Mathers Music Studio during the investigation, adding that protecting intellectual property also meant safeguarding the time, talent and livelihoods invested in creative work. No, it should not be available. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion Eminemâs former employee faces up to five years in prison Strange has pleaded guilty to criminal infringement of a copyright. His sentencing is scheduled for January 27, 2027. He faces a maximum prison term of five years, although the final sentence will be determined by a federal district court judge after considering the US Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors. The FBI investigated the case. Senior Counsel Vasantha Rao of the Justice Departmentâs Computer Crime and Intellectual Property Section (CCIPS), along with Assistant US Attorneys Timothy Wyse and Alyse Wu for the Eastern District of Michigan, are prosecuting it. The Justice Department said CCIPS investigates and prosecutes cybercrime and intellectual property offences in coordination with domestic and international law enforcement agencies, often with assistance from the private sector. Since 2020, the section has secured the convictions of more than 180 cybercrime and intellectual property offenders and obtained court orders for the return of more than $350 million in victim funds. title: Govt, aided school heads warned against collecting fee for exams, question paper
text: Chennai: Heads of govt and aided schools must no longer collect exam fee or question paper charges, the school education department has announced. The directive comes in the wake of the Madurai bench of the Madras high court issuing an interim injunction, restraining the collection of such fees from students of Classes VI-XII, as the practice violated the Right to Education Act. Chief education officers have been directed to enforce the rule in all schools in their jurisdiction. Usually, school heads collect â¹100 to â¹150 per student as exam-related fees. The amount is sent to a district coordinator, usually a HM, and subsequently to the printing press where the question papers are printed. Every school maintains a record of the amount collected. Chief education officers have been instructed to receive complaints in this regard and take appropriate action. âStudents, along with their parents, can approach the CEOâs office and lodge a formal complaint if the fee is collected. Further, they can make use of the helpline 108 to flag the issue,â an official with the school education department said, adding that strict action will be taken against erring school heads. Student welfare activists welcomed the move, adding that schools must also incur revelation expenses faced by higher secondary school students. âThough the amount is meagre (less than â¹500), students continue to pay for getting scanned copies of their answer sheets. For select subjects like Biology, the revaluation cost is higher as well. The govt can incur these expenses as well,â said S Arumainathan, president, TN Students Parents Welfare Association. title: PNG pipeline blast kills man, injures six in Muzaffarpur
text: Representational image Patna: A powerful explosion, suspected to have been caused by a gas leak after a PNG pipeline was damaged during drain construction, killed a coaching centre owner and injured six people in Muzaffarpurâs Gobarsahi area under Sadar police station area on Monday. The blast was heard up to 3km away and damaged several houses and vehicles, said locals. The deceased, Srinivas Singh, a resident of Srinagar Colony, was returning on his scooty after depositing his childâs school fees at a school when the explosion occurred. His father, Shyam Nandan Chaudhary, is a retired excise department sub-inspector. Srinivas suffered fatal head injuries. According to residents, an earth-moving machine engaged in drain construction near the pipeline accidentally damaged the underground gas line, triggering the blast. The explosion damaged a four-storey building and shattered windowpanes of houses within a 100-metre radius. Several other houses and vehicles were also damaged. Two motorcycle riders sustained burn injuries. An SUV bearing a Vaishali registration number and carrying a JD(U) flag was caught in the blast, injuring its two occupants. All six injured were taken to hospitals. Vijay Ram (32) of Dumri and Vikas Kumar (27) of Paramaul village in Vaishali were admitted to SKMCH. Mukesh Kumar (20) of Baradampur, Sonam Kumari (36) of Gobarsahi, and Mohammad Ayan (17) and his mother Ruksana Khatun (40) were admitted to a private hospital in Gobarsahi. Fire brigade teams rushed to the spot as panic gripped the locality. District magistrate Kumar Gaurav said the PNG pipeline was damaged during drain construction by the road construction department. âOne person has died and six others have been injured. Compensation, as admissible under disaster relief provisions, will be provided to the family of the deceased,â he said. SSP Kantesh Kumar Mishra said one injured person was critical, with around 60% burns. âA case is being registered against the contractor engaged in the work and other officials after proper investigation,â he said. title: Scientists identified an entirely new squid family from a single specimen recovered from a sperm whale's stomach; they named it after Poseidon, the Greek god of the sea
text: PC: Diversity in the squid family Ancistrocheiridae and description of a new family of the order Oegopsida (Cephalopoda) A single squid recovered from the stomach of a sperm whale has led scientists to propose an entirely new family of oceanic squids. Malcolm Clarke collected the specimen from a male sperm whale hunted in 1955â56 and first identified it as Ancistrocheirus lesueurii. According to the study published in Zoological Journal, titled â Diversity in the squid family Ancistrocheiridae and description of a new family of the order Oegopsida (Cephalopoda) â, it has white skin, no photophores and distinctive arm hooks. They named it Mobydickia poseidonii, placed it in the family Mobydickidae, and likened its hooks to Poseidonâs trident. Only one specimen of the squid is known. How did scientists identify a new squid family The researchers examined the morphology and DNA sequence of Ancistrocheirus lesueurii, the sole accepted member of the family Ancistrocheiridae. They reviewed the primary literature and, where possible, re-examined the type specimens of all Ancistrocheirus synonyms. The abstract states that this work revealed large morphological differences among the individuals examined, and that molecular analyses showed at least six cryptic Ancistrocheirus species. The specimen in question, NHM 20240079, was collected and identified as A. lesueurii by Malcolm Clarke. According to the paper, its label indicated only that it came from a male sperm whale taken between 1955 and 1956. Clarke was aboard the SS Southern Harvester that season. The authors used International Whaling Commission coordinates for the 341 male sperm whales hunted in the region to estimate where it was caught. They also examined Clarke's digitised logbook, but it held no relevant information. The type locality is given as Antarctic or sub-Antarctic waters, an area covering the Bellinghausen Sea, the Drake Passage and the Scotia Sea. What made the squid specimen different from others The specimen was sampled outside the reported distribution range of the species. Its skin is white, whereas Ancistrocheirus is purple. No photophores were present, and chromatophores were found only around the eyes. The arm hooks differ in size and shape from those of all other studied specimens. They are larger and have one large main cusp and two accessory claws over a circular base. The authors also describe differences in the beak, radula and gladius. The lower beak has a wider wing gap, a comparatively longer hood and no fold in the lateral walls. In the radula, the lateral cusps of the rachidian teeth slope shallowly towards the main cusp. The gladius has a very developed and pointed rachis. The paper notes that no DNA sequences are available because the specimen was very likely fixed in formalin. The authors also considered whether digestion or long storage had caused the pale colour, and concluded that the colour and the absence of photophores most likely represent the true condition of the species. Why did scientists establish a new squid family The paper gives three reasons for erecting a new family. The authors could not find any described family that the squid would fit. Placing it in Ancistrocheiridae would mean radically modifying the diagnosis of that family in one of its most diagnostic characters, the presence of symmetrically arranged photophores. They also state that there is no guarantee the specimen is the sister group of Ancistrocheirus. The authors add that the squid superficially resembles Ancistrocheirus because both are large squid with hooks on the arms. The diagnosis of Mobydickidae describes oegopsid squid without photophores. The chromatophore pattern is reduced to a small area around each eye. The arms are equal in length with more than 50 hooks. The gladius is very pronounced and angular with a long rachis, and the lower beak is broad with a large wing gap. According to the Discussion, Mobydickidae is, to the authors' knowledge, the first family of oceanic squids erected since Magnapinnidae (Vecchione and Young, 1998), more than a quarter of a century earlier. The authors also describe the specimen as "the largest depigmented squid species", to their knowledge. What inspired the names Mobydickia and Poseidonii The genus name Mobydickia refers to the fictional albino sperm whale Moby-Dick from Herman Melville's 1851 novel. The authors explain that the squid is depigmented, almost lacking chromatophores, and was collected from the stomach of a sperm whale hunted by whalers. The species name poseidonii honours Poseidon, the mythological figure of ancient Greek religion. According to the paper, legends say Poseidon used his trident to create chaotic springs, earthquakes, drownings and shipwrecks. The authors write that the arm hooks, with their main cusps and accessory claws, resemble a trident. Because Poseidon is a male character, the male genitive suffix was applied. The proposed vernacular names are Poseidon's squid in English and calamar de PoseidÃ³n in Spanish. The authors set out the limits of the evidence. Only one specimen exists, of unknown sex, with a dorsal mantle length of 175 mm. No gonads were found, and the paper states it cannot be confirmed whether the animal was immature or whether the gonads were missed during ingestion, since the mantle was opened and some internal organs were missing. The fins and tentacles were broken and are not included in the description. The distribution is given as probably Antarctic and sub-Antarctic waters around the Bellinghausen Sea, the Drake Passage and the Scotia Sea, with further distribution unknown.
