title: Ballot paper results expose Congâs EVM claims: BJP
text: BJP MP Sanjay Jaiswal Patna : BJP MP and partyâs former state president Sanjay Jaiswal on Thursday accused Congress of undermining constitutional institutions by questioning the Election Commission and the electoral process. He cited recent legislative council election results, held through ballot papers, to challenge the partyâs allegations. Addressing a press conference in Patna under the BJPâs âSave Democracy, End Anarchyâ campaign, Jaiswal questioned the oppositionâs objections to the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Arwal MLA Manoj Sharma and other BJP functionaries were present. Jaiswal claimed Congress won only one of 28 council seats contested in the country and lost all four seats in Karnataka , arguing its performance contradicted allegations against electronic voting machines. Defending SIR, he said the Election Commission had constitutional authority to revise electoral rolls, a process in place since 1950. He claimed the exercise in Bihar had corrected 47 lakh entries involving deceased persons, relocated voters and duplicate registrations. He said only eligible Indian citizens aged 18 or above could vote and urged parties to raise objections through prescribed procedures rather than question the commissionâs impartiality. Jaiswal also alleged forged documents were used to facilitate Bangladeshi nationalsâ enrolment in West Bengal. Sharma cited Article 324, which empowers the Election Commission to supervise elections, and urged the opposition to provide evidence of alleged irregularities. Both called for cooperation to ensure accurate electoral rolls and uphold the principle of one eligible citizen, one vote. title: Drawings decoded: From chalk to stylus
text: NID drawing dialogue Ahmedabad : Drawing existed even before humans began communicating through words, speakers said at the two-day Drawing Dialogues 2026 symposium held at the Gandhinagar campus of the National Institute of Design (NID) on Saturday. Experts from diverse disciplines discussed drawing as the most fundamental form of design, from marks made with chalk on stone to sketches created with a stylus on a digital screen. Prof Kaushik Chakraborty , senior faculty member in communication design at NID and head of the symposium, said the creative process across disciplines such as engineering, architecture, fashion and automobile design often begins with a pencil and paper. The discussions also explored the concepts of Drishti (seeing) and Anubhava (experience). âThe times are changing, and we are increasingly using tools and techniques that are transforming the way we interact with drawing. Change is inevitable and welcome, but it is important to understand its contours and nuances in the modern age. The symposium aims to document, practise, research and examine the future of drawing as an activity,â he said. Prof Vijai Singh Katiyar, chairperson (education) at NID, recalled the instituteâs Drawing-by-Design initiative launched in 2015, which featured more than 32 multidisciplinary international open-elective workshops conducted by experts from India and abroad. He said the initiative laid the foundation for a dedicated platform to discuss the role of drawing in design thinking and practice. The event featured presentations of 27 research papers. A special session for schoolchildren was also organised as part of the symposium. title: Over 1cr to elect 3,626 sarpanch in second phase today
text: Jaipur: More than 1.06 crore voters will cast their ballots Friday to elect 3,626 sarpanch and 33,804 ward panch across Rajasthan âs gram panchayats in the second phase of panchayat elections . While there are 21,839 candidates  for sarpanch posts in the fray, 45 were elected unopposed. The nomination process, including scrutiny and withdrawal of candidature, was completed Thursday with election symbols allotted and the final list of candidates released the same day. Of the 1 crore voters, 55,19,336 are men and 51,36,744 are women. Polling will be held from 7am to 6pm, followed by counting immediately after voting, with results expected by late night. Meanwhile, Rajasthan recorded a final voter turnout of 65.1% Wednesday in the second phase of elections for zila parishad and panchayat samiti members across 124 panchayat samitis and 352 zila parishad wards. A total of 1,06,56,127 voters are eligible to exercise their franchise in the second phase. Polling will be conducted at 11,799 booths across the state. Unlike elections to zila parishads and panchayat samitis, voting for sarpanch and ward panch posts will be conducted through ballot papers, not electronic voting machines (EVMs). Each voter will cast two votes â one for a ward panch candidate and the other for a sarpanch candidate. The ballot papers will be prepared by the polling parties in the respective gram panchayats after the final list of candidates is released. There will be separate ballot papers for ward panch and sarpanch elections, with candidatesâ names written by hand against their allotted election symbols. Jodhpur district will witness the highest number of elections in this phase, with voting for 442 sarpanch and 3,768 ward panch posts. Kota will have the fewest, with elections in 47 gram panchayats for 47 sarpanch and 505 ward panch posts. title: Get creative with pumpkins this Halloween
text: From carving spooky faces into pumpkins to making paper lanterns and decorating desserts, Halloween offers plenty of ways to get creative. Artists and workshop organisers are finding alternatives to the traditional Jack-oâ-lantern, using papier-mÃ¢chÃ©, clay and paint to make the activity accessible to children and beginners. For those who prefer treats to tools, spooky sweets add another dimension to the celebrations. Carve, craft and create Artist and workshop curator Rivu Bhattacharya recommends choosing a firm pumpkin with a relatively smooth surface and sketching a design before carving. After scooping out the seeds and pulp, beginners can start with simple shapes and gradually experiment with more intricate designs.âYou can also scrape the pumpkin flesh instead of cutting all the way through to create interesting lighting effects. The more you scrape, the more light it shows, so basically the values (lights and shadows) can be adjusted like in a proper sketch,â he explains. For those looking for a reusable alternative, Bhattacharya makes miniature Jack-oâ-lanterns using resin-based clay. He keeps the structure hollow with aluminium foil, carves a face into the clay and removes the foil once it dries. Acrylic paint completes the design, while fluorescent orange or yellow paint inside helps simulate the glow of a candle when a light is placed underneath. Devanshi Rungta, founder of Art Richshaw, says how they  have conducted pumpkin-carving workshops using real pumpkins and terracotta clay, and says children have also enjoyed making paper lanterns. For beginners, she recommends classic spooky faces, stars, moons and geometric patterns. Painting pumpkins with quirky expressions is another option for those who find carving difficult. âThe response has been great overall, with people across different age groups enjoying the activity and creating their own designs,â she says. âThe best part is that you can customise them to suit your own style.â Little hands, big Halloween ideas Artist and workshop organiser Shayari Ganguly prefers paper-based Jack-oâ-lanterns to carving actual pumpkins, particularly for activities involving children. Her method involves soaking newspaper in water and shaping it around a balloon or a large bowl. Once the paper dries, the mould is removed and the structure is painted to resemble a pumpkin. âWe mostly make Jack-oâ-lanterns using paper rather than carving actual pumpkins, because it is much easier to work with and preserve. This is a relatively simple technique that people can also try at home,â she says. Ganguly has noticed growing interest in Halloween-themed activities among children in Kolkata, reflected in workshop bookings. Her sessions include costume dress-ups, activities and prizes for the best outfits, alongside the familiar trick-or-treat element. She also makes small Halloween-themed resin objects, including fridge magnets, to encourage children to participate in creative activities beyond dressing up. âCarving a real pumpkin can be challenging, particularly because finding one of the right size is not always easy. Even when you manage to get one, carving it neatly requires some effort, and preserving it afterwards can be difficult,â she says. Box: Halloween treats: Ideas to try Cakes and brownies: Ghost brownies, mummy brownies, graveyard brownie pots, monster cakes, spider-web cakes, pumpkin cakes, red velvet cakes and spooky cupcakes. Cookies and biscuits: Ghost, bat, pumpkin, skeleton and black-cat cookies; witch-finger biscuits, spider cookies, mummy biscuits and haunted-house gingerbread. Bite-sized treats: Mummy cake pops, ghost marshmallows, eyeball truffles, monster cake pops, chocolate-covered strawberries, spooky doughnuts and Halloween macarons. Chocolates and confectionery: Halloween chocolate bark, chocolate skulls, candy apples, caramel apples, chocolate fudge, pretzel wands, marshmallow monsters and crispy rice treats. Desserts and drinks: Graveyard pudding cups, dirt cups with gummy worms, pumpkin cheesecake, chocolate mousse, pumpkin-spice scones, Halloween hot chocolate, pumpkin-spice lattes and themed mocktails. Dessert boxes and flavour combinations: Trick-or-treat boxes, assorted spooky cookie platters and mixed dessert hampers featuring red velvet and raspberry, Biscoff and dark chocolate, pistachio and white chocolate, or pumpkin spice and cinnamon. DIY craft tips Choose the right pumpkin: Pick one that is firm and relatively smooth. Sketch your design before carving. Scoop carefully: Use a sturdy spoon or ice-cream scoop to remove seeds and pulp. Experiment with light: Scrape selected areas of the pumpkin flesh to create different levels of light and shadow. Try papier-mÃ¢chÃ©: Shape soaked newspaper around a balloon or bowl, allow it to dry and paint it like a pumpkin. Skip the carving: Use acrylic paints, brushes and markers to create spooky faces, stars, moons or geometric patterns. Make a miniature lantern: Keep a clay structure hollow and use fluorescent orange or yellow paint inside to enhance the glow from an LED. Keep it safe: Use LED lights for paper crafts, and ensure adults handle sharp carving tools and supervise children. Quote blurbs: âHalloween is the perfect excuse to let creativity take over in the kitchen.It's ideal to explore desserts that are not just delicious but also fun, quirky, and visually exciting. This year, the idea is to give classic desserts a spooky little twist , think creepy-cute designs, eerie colours, spooky characters, and desserts that look almost too fun to eatâ - Muskaan Lodha, bake r Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. title: Hackers steal $6.3 billion from worldâs largest cryptocurrency exchange Binance in what analysts say the biggest crypto hack ever; Co-CEO speaks directly about what happened
text: Hackers steal $6.3 billion from worldâs largest cryptocurrency exchange Binance in the biggest crypto hack ever Hackers have stolen approximately $6.3 billion from Binance, the worldâs largest cryptocurrency exchange, in what industry analysts are calling the largest cyber heist in digital asset history. The incident has again highlighted concerns regarding cybersecurity and the systemic risks of holding funds on centralised trading platforms. Blockchain intelligence firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis reported that the threat actors behind the coordinated attack originated from North Korea. According to TRM Labs, the attackers targeted Binance wallets across 10 distinct blockchains, siphoning the vast majority of the funds within an estimated 20-minute window. According to news agency Reuters, TRM Labs stated with âhigh confidenceâ that key characteristics of the intrusion closely mirror previous North Korean-sponsored operations, including a major 2025 cyberattack against cryptocurrency exchange Bybit that was formally tied to Pyongyang by the US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI). Compromised laptop suspected as entry point Reuters reported that preliminary internal inquiries by Binance suggest the breach began through a single compromised endpoint. According to the exchange, unauthorised access was gained after an engineerâs laptop was hacked, allowing the attacker to infiltrate an internal network system and execute unauthorised fund withdrawals. âThe incident stems from multiple factors. Our security team is tracing the full attack path through the compromised computer which may be the entry point of the incident,â Binance stated. Aravind Srinivasan, head of the systematic OTC business at cryptocurrency market maker GSR, described the unprecedented scale simply as âthe biggest hack in history.â Binance Co-CEO Richard Teng to users: âYour money is safeâ In response to the incident, Binance co-CEO Richard Teng posted a direct message on X for users to quell market panic and address solvency fears. I want to speak to you directly about what happened. Bottom line - your money is safe, and we're covering every loss. Our initial investigation suggests this security incident may have started with a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop. That gave an attacker access to a service container, where they submitted unauthorized withdrawal transactions. To be clear: the attacker did not simply use one engineer's permissions, and this was not a single "one-click" action. It involved a more complex attack process. Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual. So far, we have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak. We'll share a detailed technical post-mortem once the investigation is complete and every fact is verified - and publish an updated Proof of Reserves once remediation is complete. What you need to know: â¢ Your funds are safe â¢ Binance will cover all losses from the SAFU fund and company funds â¢ Estimated total impact: ~$6.3B, with ~$3B frozen on-chain so far, in coordination with our blockchain partners â¢ No evidence of any wallet private key leak â¢ Deposits are unaffected and operating as normal What we've done: â¢ Temporarily suspended withdrawals while we complete a security revamp of the withdrawal service and its related addresses â¢ Revoked the affected address authorizations â¢ Engaged law enforcement and blockchain intelligence partners to trace and recover funds Our team hasn't stopped. We're working closely with law enforcement to ensure the matter is handled appropriately - and I'll share what I can, as soon as I can. title: NEET-PG counselling: Candidates struggle to join online as colleges remain unreachable
text: Candidates who have secured postgraduate medical seats through NEET-PG counselling 2026 are encountering challenges with the online joining procedure. New Delhi: Candidates allotted postgraduate medical seats under NEET-PG counselling 2026 are facing difficulties completing the online joining process, with some reporting that nodal officers listed on the official portal are unreachable or their contact details are invalid. At Vardhman Mahavir Medical College (VMMC) and Safdarjung Hospital, candidates have complained that the nodal officerâs mobile phone is switched off and landline numbers are not reachable. The Medical Counselling Committeeâs (MCC) helpline, they said, directed them to contact the allotted college, leaving them struggling to resolve admission-related queries. The problem is not limited to one institution. Candidates have also flagged similar difficulties with the University College of Medical Sciences (UCMS), where the portal displays a nodal officerâs mobile number as â00000000â, making it impossible to contact the designated official on that number. The portal lists an email address, but candidates have complained of not receiving a response. When contacted, a senior official told TOI, âwe will take up the issue with the colleges and ask them to update their contact details so that students can reach the concerned officials during counselling. Incorrect or non-functional contact numbers create unnecessary difficulties for candidates. We will also raise the matter in a meeting and seek a resolution.â The issue assumes significance for candidates who have opted for the float option in counselling. Those choosing freeze accept the allotted seat, while candidates choosing float wish to retain their current allotment while remaining eligible for an upgrade in subsequent rounds. Candidates who have to complete online reporting and submit documents are seeking timely verification and clear communication from their allotted institutes. The MCC portal itself displays a message stating that document verification is pending at the allotted institute and advises candidates to contact the nodal officer for admission-related queries. But when the listed contact details do not work, candidates are left without a clear channel to resolve their concerns. title: Water board to fine tankers Rs 5,000 for water wastage
text: File photo Hyderabad: To curb the wastage of drinking water, the HMWSSB has decided to impose a fine of Rs 5,000 on water tankers found wasting water during transportation from Nov 1. Repeat offenders will face cancellation of their registration. The orders were issued by HMWSSB managing director Ashok Reddy after the board identified instances of drinking water spilling onto roads during transportation. Some tankers were reportedly being filled beyond their capacity, while others lacked lids or had improperly secured covers, resulting in water spilling onto roads. Under the new guidelines, tankers with leaking containers, missing lids or improperly secured covers will not be allowed to fill water at HMWSSB filling stations until the defects are rectified. Officials have also been instructed to ensure that tankers are not filled beyond their capacity. Managers and in-charges of all filling stations have been directed to inspect tankers for leaks and check the condition of their lids before allowing them to fill water. Any vehicle found to have defects must be denied access to water until the necessary repairs are completed. title: Road cave-in near Phoenix Mall brings Velachery traffic to a halt
text: A road cave-in near Phoenix Marketcity brought traffic to a standstill on the Velachery Main Road on the weekend before Diwali. Chennai: A road cave-in on Velachery Main Road near Phoenix Marketcity brought traffic to a standstill on the weekend before Diwali. Metrowater officials said they received information about the cave-in around 9am and found that an old 150mm main pipeline had developed a slow leak, weakening the road surface. Around 7m of the pipeline was damaged, and 4m was replaced by Sunday evening. Officials said they would complete the remaining pipeline replacement work by 8pm. Many people traveling to a mall in Velachery were stuck in traffic. Many took to social media to warn commuters not to use Velachery Main Road. âUsually, travel from one end to another takes 10 mins, but today I was stuck for 90 mins. I had to attend a meeting, but then I attended it online sitting in my car,â said G Sunil from Chromepet, who had to travel to a mall for a meeting. The cave-in and barricades put up around the damaged stretch caused heavy traffic congestion, inconveniencing motorists travelling between Guindy and Velachery during the festive weekend. The incident comes amid concerns about road cave-ins caused by bursts in Metro Water pipelines, with similar incidents reported on OMR, Perambur Barracks Road, and GNT Road over the past two months. âThe last couple of incidents in Area 6 (Thiru-Vi-Ka-Nagar zone) occurred in arch sewers, which are very old sewer mains. We have identified vulnerable sewer mains, which will be replaced in due course. We have around 15km of arch sewers that will be replaced with ductile iron (DI) pipes,â said Metrowater MD T Anand. title: Surprise inspections & penalties: Pune civic body set to intensify checks against misuse of potable water
text: The crackdown will target activities like vehicle washing, swimming pool usage and gardening Pune: Two weeks after rolling out a once-a-week water supply cut, Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) is now preparing for the next phase of its conservation drive â surprise checks and penalties for those found using potable water for non-essential purposes. The crackdown will target activities like vehicle washing, swimming pool usage and gardening, as the city grapples with shrinking water reserves and growing pressure on PMC to deepen the existing 10% water cut to 20%. âThe implementation of Thursday cuts started on Oct 15. An advisory on usage of water was issued the same day. Two weeks were given to create awareness on avoiding use of drinking water for non-essential purposes. Now the regular checks will begin,â a civic official said. Officials stressed that the move was not meant to be punitive but preventive. âWe are not targeting anyone. We want residents to use water responsibly. With about 10 months till the next monsoon, water must be used wisely to avoid a crisis,â the official said. PMC has already begun pushing water conservation messages through social media and has directed swimming pool operators to rely on treated water instead of potable water. Vehicle washing centres, too, are expected to avoid using drinking water. âPMC supplies treated water through its distribution network. The citizens will have to play a key role in avoiding water wastage,â another official said. The scrutiny may soon extend to housing societies too. Civic teams are planning inspections of sewage treatment plants (STPs) to ensure treated water is being recycled for gardening and other non-potable uses. âThe societies are expected to use treated water for gardening and other such purposes. Societies with defunct STPs will be served notices. They are also expected to plug the leaking pipes and avoid wastage of water within their premises,â the official said. Even PMCâs own departments are tightening their belts. The garden department has directed all zonal offices to use only treated water for gardening and cleaning, with implementation expected to begin immediately. The urgency stems from a drop in water reserves. According to the irrigation department, the four dams supplying water to the city currently hold 24 TMC of water, significantly lower than the 28.5 TMC available during the same period last year. Continuous releases for both urban and rural needs have widened the deficit, raising concerns over water availability until the next monsoon. Citizens have urged PMC to take stronger steps to curb water losses. Sandip Joshi, a Satara Road resident, said, âItâs good that PMC has decided to step up monitoring of drinking water use, but what about its commitment to plug leaks in distribution lines? It should designate at least one water zone with zero leakage.â Ajay Mujumdar, a Vishrantwadi resident, said, âPMC must closely monitor tanker operations, especially those filled at PMC water points. title: AI hallucinations explained: Why chatbots get facts wrong and how to verify answers
text: AI generated image An artificial intelligence tool can produce a convincing explanation, cite a research paper, quote an expert and refer to a government report, yet get the central fact completely wrong. The answer may read like a well-researched response, leaving users with little reason to question it. This is known as an AI hallucination. It occurs when a generative AI system produces information that is false, misleading, fabricated or unsupported, often presenting it with considerable confidence. It can take the form of an incorrect date, an invented statistic, a quotation that was never made, a non-existent research paper or a genuine source that does not support the claim attributed to it. The problem is not limited to obscure questions or older AI models. It reflects how generative AI works, the information available to it and the way its performance is evaluated. Understanding why these errors occur is also the first step towards using AI responsibly. Why does AI make things up? Large language models (LLMs) generate responses by predicting which word or token is likely to come next, based on patterns learnt during training. They do not necessarily retrieve verified facts from a database every time they answer a question. These models learn associations between words, concepts and information from large volumes of data. This allows them to produce fluent explanations, summarise documents and respond to complex questions. But predicting a plausible sequence of words is not the same as establishing whether every statement is true. Google's guidance on generative AI highlights this distinction: language models predict likely sequences of words rather than independently verifying every factual claim. A model may therefore produce a seemingly complete answer even when it lacks sufficient information to establish the facts. An OpenAI research paper published in September 2025, titled Why Language Models Hallucinate, identifies another contributing factor. The researchers argue that the way models are trained and evaluated can reward guessing rather than acknowledging uncertainty. In their words, systems may be encouraged to âreward guessing over acknowledging uncertaintyâ. This means a model may attempt to provide an answer even when the available information is incomplete. The result can sound authoritative without being reliable. What are the different types of AI hallucinations ? Hallucinations do not always involve completely invented information. They can also occur when a model combines genuine facts incorrectly or misinterprets a real source. Fabricated facts: A model may invent a person's designation, company announcement, historical event, court judgment or government policy. The surrounding details may appear plausible because the names and concepts are familiar. Fake quotations and references : AI can generate quotations attributed to real people, cite research papers that do not exist or provide incorrect publication details. A genuine report may also be cited to support a conclusion it never reached. Distorted information: A model may combine two separate developments, confuse organisations with similar names or present an estimate as an established result. Outdated information : An answer may rely on details that were once correct but have since changed. This is particularly relevant to company leadership, market prices, laws, regulations and ongoing developments. Errors of context: A model may misunderstand a question, overlook a qualification in a supplied document or contradict information stated earlier in the same response. The US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) uses the term confabulation for this category of generative AI risk. Its guidance warns that systems can confidently present erroneous or false content, including fabricated explanations and citations. How can users fact-check AI-generated answers? The safest approach is to treat an AI response as a starting point for research, not as the final source of information. Check individual claims: Break a long response into separate statements. Verify names, dates, figures, designations, policy provisions and company announcements individually. One correct paragraph does not establish that the entire answer is accurate. Go to the original source : For government decisions, consult the relevant ministry notification, official order or dataset. For corporate announcements, check the company's official statement or regulatory filing. For research findings, locate the original paper, journal publication or institutional report. A news article or another AI-generated summary can help identify a lead, but should not replace the primary document. Open every citation: Check whether the cited paper, report or webpage actually exists. Then read the relevant passage. A genuine source does not automatically validate the statement attached to it. The source may be real but irrelevant, outdated or misrepresented. Verify quotations word for word : Confirm the speaker, designation, date and original context through a transcript, recording, official statement or published interview. Do not convert an AI-generated paraphrase into a direct quotation. When the original wording cannot be established, do not use quotation marks. Check numbers and comparisons: Examine the reporting period, units, denominator, methodology and geographical coverage. A statistic covering a small group of companies should not be presented as an industry-wide finding. Distinguish actual results from forecasts, estimates and company projections. Check whether the information is current: Look at both the publication date and the date of the underlying event. For regulations, market information and political developments, consult the latest official records rather than relying on a model's stored knowledge. Do search-enabled AI tools eliminate hallucinations? Some AI systems use search tools or a technique known as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to improve factual accuracy. RAG works by retrieving relevant documents and supplying them to a model before it generates an answer. This gives the system specific material to work with rather than relying only on information learnt during training. Microsoft's technical guidance describes this approach as a way to ground AI-generated responses in retrieved information. However, it does not guarantee accuracy. The system may retrieve the wrong document, miss relevant information or misinterpret a passage. Errors can persist even when sources are available. Citations and links are therefore useful starting points for verification, not proof that an answer is correct. Why does it matter? In healthcare, law, finance, education and journalism, an incorrect AI-generated answer can influence decisions or be repeated as established information. A fabricated legal precedent, an inaccurate medical explanation or a misleading financial figure can have consequences beyond the original interaction. NIST has emphasised the need for human oversight, source verification and appropriate risk management when organisations deploy generative AI. The responsibility becomes particularly important when AI is used in decisions affecting individuals or public services. AI can help organise information, explain technical subjects, identify research leads and speed up routine work. But its fluency should not be mistaken for factual authority. The most useful habit is simple: verify the source, not just the answer. A confident tone, a detailed explanation and a list of references are not evidence of accuracy. You use AI every day. title: Vastu Mistakes in the Kitchen That May Trigger Family Arguments
text: According to Vastu Shastra, poor kitchen arrangements can generate family tensions. A kitchen's layout, especially the stove and sink placement, impacts harmony among members. By rectifying these common errors and ensuring a clean environment, energy flows positively, reducing household stress. Embracing these changes can foster peace during festive cooking and celebrations. Some families argue most in the living room. A surprising number argue in the kitchen. Over whose turn it is to cook, why the tea is late, who finished the last of the milk. Small things, but they add up. Vastu Shastra treats the kitchen as the home's energy centre, where Agni, the fire element, nourishes the family. When itâs set up wrongly, Vastu says that fire spills over into tempers. With Diwali cooking about to begin, here are the kitchen mistakes most often linked with household tension. The Stove and the Sink Too Close Together This is the single most common Vastu mistake in modern kitchens. Fire and water are opposite elements. When the gas stove sits right beside the sink, or directly opposite it, Vastu holds that the two clash constantly. According to tradition, the result is friction between family members, particularly between spouses or the women who share the kitchen. The fix doesnât require breaking walls. Ideally, keep at least a small gap between stove and sink. If they must be next to each other, a small wooden board, a green plant or a tiled divider between them is believed to ease the clash. Watch Birth Date Magic: Mulank Bhagyank Decode Your Hidden Superpowers With Anuragg Shuklaa | Times Mantra Cooking While Facing South The cook's direction matters in Vastu. Cooking facing east is considered best, since the east brings health and positive energy from the rising Sun. Facing south is generally discouraged. Itâs linked with irritation, health complaints and short tempers. Facing west is acceptable but less ideal. If the kitchen layout forces a south-facing stove, keeping the area especially clean and placing a small picture of Goddess Annapurna nearby is a common traditional remedy. The Kitchen in the Wrong Zone The ideal location for a kitchen is the south-east, the corner of Agni. The north-west is an acceptable second choice. A kitchen in the north-east is considered problematic, since that corner belongs to water and spiritual energy. Fire there is believed to bring stress, health worries and disagreements. A kitchen in the south-west, the zone of stability, may lead to power struggles in the household. Most people canât move a kitchen. But they can reduce the effect. Using yellow or orange tones on the walls, keeping the space very clean and lighting a small lamp there regularly are traditional ways to soften a poorly placed kitchen. Broken Utensils and Leaking Taps Cracked cups, chipped plates and dented pans often stay in kitchens for years. Vastu treats them as signs of stagnant, broken energy. Eating or drinking from damaged vessels is believed to bring discord. A leaking tap is even more significant. Dripping water is associated with money draining away and with a steady sense of irritation in the home. Before Diwali, itâs worth fixing every tap and clearing out every broken item. Clutter, Knives and Empty Containers Crowded countertops make cooking stressful, and stress fuels quarrels. Keep only daily-use items on the counter and store the rest away. Knives and scissors are best kept in a drawer or closed holder. Sharp objects on open display are believed to encourage sharp words. Grain and flour containers should never be left empty. Vastu links an empty atta tin with scarcity and worry. Keeping a small amount in every container, even near the end of the month, signals abundance. Store medicines outside the kitchen. Keeping them near food is believed to invite illness into the family. Mirrors, Dark Colours and the Toilet Door A mirror that reflects the stove is said to double the fire element and the tension that comes with it. Remove it or move it. Black or very dark shades in a kitchen are also discouraged. Warm, light colours like cream, peach, yellow and light orange suit the fire element without overpowering it. Finally, a kitchen that shares a wall with a toilet, or whose door faces a toilet door, is considered unfortunate. Common Vastu remedies include keeping the toilet door closed at all times and placing a small bowl of sea salt in the toilet. A calm kitchen, in the end, cooks calmer meals. And families who eat together in peace tend to argue less in every other room too. Get the latest astrology news and horoscope updates. Download the TOI App.

title: Gradsâ Poll Defeat: BJP Corporators On Radar
text: Nagpur: BJP has initiated an internal review of its defeat in the Nagpur Division Graduatesâ Constituency election, with the party set to examine whether its corporators and local functionaries discharged their responsibilities effectively. Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis is expected to attend a review meeting to be conducted within a week. Guardian minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule has already accepted responsibility for the defeat of BJP candidate Sudhakar Kohale, but discontent within the party continues. Allegations of internal sabotage and organisational lapses are making the rounds across various factions. The review will primarily focus on the role of the partyâs 108 corporators, including six nominated members, who had been assigned the task of maximising graduate voter registrations and ensuring that registered voters reached polling stations on election day. The leadership wants to ascertain how many corporators actively worked towards voter enrolment, maintained contact with registered voters and mobilised them to exercise their franchise. While some are believed to have fulfilled their responsibilities, others allegedly failed to demonstrate the expected level of involvement. BJP office-bearer Munna Yadav had alleged that voter registration in CMâs constituency itself was only around 50%. Another issue under scrutiny is the controversy surrounding the marking of the numeral â2â against Kohaleâs name on ballot papers. More than 8,000 ballot papers were reportedly invalidated, triggering questions within the party about whether the mistake was accidental or deliberate. The leadership is also trying to establish who advised the candidate to write the numeral against his name. The party is also examining whether adequate efforts were made to secure second-preference votes and whether functionaries issued proper instructions to the election machinery. Fadnavis is scheduled to visit Nagpur on Nov 5 for a march. The party may convene the review meeting on the same day, adding to the anticipation among BJP corporators.
